SERMONS V (273-338) SERMONS ON THE MARTYRS
Topic: The cult of martyrs. Location: Hippo. Date: January 21, 396, feast of Saints Fructuoso, Augurio and Eulogio.

1. The Lord Jesus not only instructed the martyrs with his doctrine; He also strengthened them with his example. So that those condemned to torture would have someone to follow, he went ahead suffering for them: he showed them the path by walking it himself. Death is either of the soul or of the body. Of the soul we can affirm that it cannot die and that it can die: it cannot die, because self-consciousness never perishes; but he can die, if he loses God. As the soul is the life of its own body, so God is the life of its own soul. As the dead body is abandoned by the soul, that is, its own life, so the soul also dies if God abandons it. To prevent God from abandoning the soul, always live in faith, without fearing to die for God; That way she won't die because God has abandoned her. It only remains, then, to admit that death must be feared only in regard to the body. But also in this respect Christ the Lord reassured his martyrs. «Memories are called, says Augustine, those places that contain a famous tomb, because this serves to bring to mind the acts and glorious death of the martyr or saint. 8. So that you can see how true what I say is, listen, I urge you. According to the Acts of the Apostles, Paul having performed a great miracle in Lycaonia, the citizens of that region or province thought that the gods had descended to men, and they believed that Barnabas was Jupiter, and Paul, however, Mercury, because of his skill in the art of speaking. With that conviction, they brought them bulls with garlands and wanted to offer them a sacrifice. With the eyes of faith we have contemplated a magnificent spectacle: the total victory of the holy martyr Vincent. He won in the interrogation, he won in the torments, he won in the confession, he won in the tribulation, he won when he was burned by the flames and he won when he was submerged in the waves; Finally, he won by being tortured and won by death. When his body, in which was the trophy of the victorious Christ, was thrown from a boat into the sea, he said in silence: It is thrown to us, but sacrificium esse, quam I will possess; in quantum homo est. Nam in quantum Deus est, totum quod Patri debentur, et onlygenito Filio debentur. Ideo, carissimi, veneramini martyres, laúdate, amate, praedicate, honorate: Deum martyrum colite. That's exactly how it was. Let us praise this soul in the Lord so that the meek may hear and rejoice. The story read showed us what questions they asked him, what his answers were and what torments he overcame, and put everything that happened before our eyes. The torment he suffered in his limbs corresponded to the certainty of his words, giving the impression that one was the one who was tormented and the other was the one who spoke. And indeed it was another; The Lord had predicted it and promised it to his martyrs, saying: It is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you. Let this soul be praised in the Lord, then. Well, what is man if you don't remember him? Or what are the forces of the dust if he who made us from the dust does not help him? Let him who glories glory in the Lord. If the diabolical and seducing spirit frequently fills both false soothsayers and false martyrs, so that they apply bodily torments to themselves 1 or despise those that others apply to them, what is so extraordinary about God our Lord that, with a view to supporting the preaching of his name, he delivers the body of his preachers into the hands of the persecutors, while retaining their minds in the fortress of freedom, so that, even when he suffers iniquity, the latter proclaims the truth, and so it is not resistance, but justice, that makes one a winner? Who is a martyr is determined by the cause, not by the punishment. Many, in fact, have endured pain not out of perseverance, but rather plañe, carissimi, ita prorsus Fuit; in Domino laudemus hanc animam, ut audiant mites, et iucundentur (cf. Ps 33,3). Quas voices audierit, quas reddiderit, quae storm devicerit, decursa lectio declaravit, et nobis tanquam in conspectu quae gesta sunt posuit. So much poena erat in membris, so much securitas in verbis, tanquam alius torqueretur, alius loqueretur. Et veré alius: praedixit enim hoc Dominus, et promisit martyribus suis dices: Non vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri qui loquifur in vobis (Mt 10,20). In Domino ergo laudetur haec anima. Yum quid est homo, nisi quod mentor est eius? (Ps 8,5). Aut quae vires pulveris, nisi illo adiuvante que nos fecit ex pulvere? Ut qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur (1 Cor 1:31).

Si enim diabolicus et seductor spiritus plerumque implet vel fallaces vates, vel false martyres suos, ut storm corporis vel ipsi sibi ingerant, vel intake contemnant: quid magnum est Domino Deo nostro ad confirmandam praedicationem nominis sui, ipsorum praedicatorum carnem quidem in manus persequentium tradere mentem vero in arcem libertatis assumere; ut etiam dum illa patitur iniquitatem, haec asserat veritatem? scilicet ut victores non tolerantia faciat, sed iustitia: quoniam martyres discernit causa, non poena. In the case of our Vicente, the one who owned it won; but it was possessed by the one who had thrown the prince out of this world so that he would be defeated, even fighting externally, who had already been defeated so that he would not dominate internally. He who was thrown out prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour. But he attacks him in our place who, excluding him, reigns in us. 2. Furthermore, it was greater torment for the devil not to defeat Vicente than for Vincent to be persecuted by the devil. The more gruesome and refined the torments were, the greater was the triumph of the tortured over the torturer, and from that flesh, like earth watered with one's own blood, sprouted the palm that even caused the greatest torment to the enemy. But he who secretly shows himself cruel, secretly also suffers once defeated; It was clearly manifested in the human judge how much the devil was secretly suffering, and this invisible enemy was visible through the cracks in his own glass, which he had filled and which was bursting. In fact, the words of that man, the eyes, the look and the turbulent convulsion of his entire body indicated that the torments he suffered internally were more unbearable than those he inflicted externally on the martyr. If we consider the confusion of the torturer and the serenity of the tortured, it is easy to see who was subject to the pravo errore, non recta ratione; diabolo possidente, non persequente. In our autem vincente Vincentio, ille quidem vincebat, qui possidebat; sed ille possidebat, qui principem huius mundi miserat foras (cf. lo 12,31); ut etiam pugnans extrinsecus superaretur, qui iam fuet superatus, ne intus dominaretur. Ille quippe qui missus est foras, non cessans tanquam leo rugiens circuit requiring quem devoret (cf. 1 Petr 5,8). Sed eurn expugnat ille pro nobis, qui eo excluso regnat in nobis. 2. What will be the source of life, once the incorruptible body has been reached, if its spray is so sweet in the midst of torments! Magnificent testimony that the Lord gives to his witnesses, since he who rules the hearts of combatants does not abandon the bodies of those who die, as shown by the well-known miracle that had as its object the body of this blessed Vincent. The enemy had wanted it to be completely hidden, worrying and taking care of it; but the divine will brought it to light, showing that it should be devoutly buried and venerated so that the brilliant memory of the victory of piety and the defeat of evil would endure. Truly, the death of his saints is precious in the presence of the Lord, since not even the earth that the flesh becomes when life leaves it is despised; and, when the invisible soul leaves the visible house, the dwelling place of the servant is guarded by the Lord and honored by the faithful, his fellow servants, to the glory of the Lord. Next to the bodies of the deceased saints, what else does he do but bear witness that for him what dies does not perish? From there, we can understand what honor the souls of the martyrs enjoy at their side, if the lifeless flesh enjoys so much divine power. Speaking of the members of the Church, the Apostle took a comparison of the members of our body, to wit: We surround our vilest members with greater honor; In the same way, the providence of the Creator, granting the corpses of the martyrs such illustrious testimonies of miracles, surrounds with greater honor the lifeless remains of men, and what, when life disappears, remains deformed, is the place where the giver of life is most clearly manifested.

If impiety, although convicted by so many miracles, did not give way, if weakness, tormented with so many tortures, did not succumb, then the action of divinity is recognized. Indeed, if the Lord did not dwell in him, how could the corruptible dust resist such cruel tortures? In all of this, therefore, we must recognize, glorify and praise the one who, when calling him for the first time, gave him faith and, in his last passion, strength. Do you want to know that both things were donated to him? Listen to the apostle Paul: To you, he said, it has been given not only to believe in Christ, but also to suffer for him. Deacon Vincent had received both things; He had received them and kept them. Indeed, if he had received nothing, what would he have? He had confidence in speaking and resistance in suffering. Let no one, therefore, when he speaks, boast of his ingenuity; Let no one, when he suffers temptation, trust in his strength, since the wisdom by which we speak rightly and at the right moment comes to us from God, and from him also the patience to endure evils with fortitude. Remember Christ the Lord, who in the gospel admonished his disciples; Bring to memory the king of martyrs by equipping his cohorts with spiritual weapons, presenting to them the battles they must fight, providing them with aid and promising them rewards. After having said to his disciples: In this world you will suffer tribulation, immediately, in order to console them, since they were terrified, he added: But have confidence, for I have overcome the world. De convicta miraculis persistebat impietas, tot vexata suppliciis non cedebat infirmitas: agnoscatur ergo operata divinitas. Quando enim corruptibilis pulvis contra tam immania storm duraet, nisi in eo Dominus habitaret? In his enim omnibus ille agnoscendus, ille glorificandus, ille laudandus est, qui et in prima vocatione dedit fidem, et in suprema passione virtutem. Vultis nosse quia utrumque donatum est? Audite apostolum Paulum: Vobis, inquit, donatum est pro Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, verum etiam ut patiamini pro eo (Phil 1,29). Acceperat haec utraque levita Vincentius, acceperat et habebat. If enim non accepisset, quid haberet? habebat in sermone fiduciam, habebat in passione tolerantiam.

Although covered with wounds of all kinds, he did not abandon the fight, but rather resumed it with greater vigor, to the point that one could think that the flame, instead of burning him, hardened him, like the potter's kiln, which receives soft clay and turns it into a hard vessel. Our martyr could say to Datian 3: "Your fire no longer dries my flesh, because my vigor has dried up like a vessel." And since what is written is true: The furnace tests the clay vessel, and the righteous men the tribulation, Vincent was tested and baked with that fire; Daciano, on the other hand, burned and exploded. And if it didn't burn, where did its screams come from? What else were his words full of anger but the smoke of someone who is burning? He externally enveloped our martyr with flames, whose heart was fresh; but he himself, lit with the torch of fury, burned inside like an oven, scorching, at the same time, the devil who inhabited him. Through Daciano's angry screams, through the ferocity of his eyes, his threatening glances and the movement of his entire body, his inner tenant was manifested, and was seen through these visible signs, like cracks in the vessel that he filled and cracked. Strength and glory of Saint Vincent

4. But, brothers, all that is a thing of the past: the wrath of Datian and the torment of Vincent. Now, however, Daciano is left with torment, and Vincent is crowned. Furthermore, leaving aside the differences in future retribution, let us show the glory that martyrs possess even in this world. What region, what province within the Roman Empire or as far as the Christian name reaches, is not happy today to celebrate the birth of Vincent? 5 Who would have heard today, even if it were only the name of Daciano, if Vincent's passion had not been read? In the fact that the Lord has so carefully guarded the body of his martyr 6, what else did he manifest other than that he had directed in life someone whom he did not abandon once he was dead? Thus, Vincent, both in life and in death, defeated Datian. In life he despised the torments; Already dead, he crossed the seas. But the one who gave him an undefeated spirit between the iron hooks, he himself directed his lifeless corpse in the midst of the waves. The flame of torture did not break his heart, nor did the sea water cover his body. But in this and other similar events nothing else is manifested except that the death of his saints is precious before the Lord. CAPUT IV.—4. Vincentii gloria post passionem, etiam in hoc mundo. Be yam, fratres, illa omnia transierunt, et ira Daciani, et poena Vincentii. Ntinc autem poena Daciano, corona vero manet Vincentio. Denique his praemissis Futurae videlicet retributionis finibus, etiam in hoc mundo martyrum gloriam demonstremus. Quae today royal, quaeve province ulla, quo usque vel Romanum imperium, vel christianum nomen extenditur, natalem non gaudet celebratee Vincentii? Quis autem hodie Daciani vel nomen audisset, nisi Vincentii passionem legisset? Quod vero so much cura servavit Dominus Martyris corpus, quid aliud demonstravit, nisi se gubernasse víventem, quem non reliquit exanimem? Vicit ergo Dacianum vivos Vincentius, vicit et mortuus. Vivens storm calcavit, mortuus maria transnatavit. Sed ipse Inter undas gubernavit cadaver exstinctum, qui inter úngulas animum donavit invictum. Non flexit flamma tortoris cor eius, non mersit aqua maris corpus eius. Sed in his et huiusmodi omnibus nihil est aliud, nisi pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15). The liturgy calls birth the day of the martyrdom of its saints, since it considers it as the date of their new birth to heaven.

The Church only celebrates carnal birth in two cases: Jesus and John the Baptist. Aaustín explains why in serm.287,1. Saving what may be rhetorical hyperbole, this text is a good testimony of how widespread the cult of the Saint was, for which testimonies from the Augustinian era are lacking, but abound for later times. According to the passio, the imperial agent Dacian, to take revenge, ordered that the Saint's body be thrown into the open field, without burial, so that the flies and birds would devour him, so that the faithful would not collect his relics and venerate him as a martyr; but nothing and no one touched it. Then he ordered it to be thrown into the sea in a sack tied to a stone so that the fish would eat it, but the corpse came back intact (n.10-11).
The spiritual body
Topic: The spiritual body. Place: Basílica Restitutía de Vallis or Cartago Date: January 22, feast of Saint Vincent. In the year 413.

1. With the eyes of faith we have contemplated the fight of the martyr, and we have loved him because we found him invisibly beautiful in his fullness. What beauty of soul would he have even whose corpse was undefeated! 'In life he confessed the Lord; Even after death he defeated the enemy. Do we think, brothers, that the providence and decision of the almighty Creator granted anything to the martyr in bestowing such honor on his deceased body? What to say? If he had not been buried, would God ignore the place where he had to resurrect him? The crown is reserved for the martyr after victory and, after the resurrection, eternal life. But, thanks to his body, the Church was granted a memory 2 that serves as consolation. Frequently, and out of a certain condescension, God grants things to his servants by using other servants of his, granting something that is extra.

However, he sends it to a widow so that she can feed him, and not because there was no other way to feed the servant of God, but so that the pious widow would deserve the blessing. Thus, God grants his churches the bodies of the saints not for the glory of the martyrs, but so that they may become places of prayer. They, in fact, have their full glory alongside their creator. They do not even feel any fear regarding their body, because they can fear nothing. Furthermore, if they condescend to him, they cause him harm; If, on the contrary, guided by faith, they do not worry about it, even he wins. 2. Pay attention to this and question your faith. If Saint Vincent had denied Christ for fear of torment, he would seem to have had compassion for the body, from which, by virtue of his mortal condition, he would have to separate himself. What would he do at the moment of resurrection when he was thrown into eternal fire? Denying Christ is equivalent to being denied by Christ. Whoever denies me, he said, before men, I will deny before my Father who is in heaven. Let us suppose that he denied it, that the executioners stopped torturing him and that, although his soul was wounded, his body remained healthy; moreover, that when the soul died, the body continued in life: of what use would a brief bodily life be to one who has died for all eternity?

The spiritual body

It does not absorb the humors, and the humors do not overabundant nor are they a cause of oppression, but rather all its components are well balanced, which is called health. To put it in a few words, there is bodily health: the harmony of all the elements of which it consists. This, then, is bodily health, that is, the concord of the members and humors; but in a corruptible, needy and weak thing, in something that can still feel hunger and thirst, get tired of standing, rest while sitting; who, in turn, gets tired of sitting, who declines with hunger and recovers by eating; that barely cures some ills, it has already fallen into others, because whatever you take to recover when you are tired, means starting to get tired again, since, if you continue taking what helped you, you will later get tired of it. In this weak body, and therefore corruptible, what is health, whatever it may be? Indeed, what is called health, applied to mortal and corruptible flesh, does not admit of any comparison with the health of the angels, to whom we have been promised to be equal after the resurrection. Yet this health, whatever it may be, as I said, how delighting! How much desired by all! How rich the poor man is if he only has her and how poor the rich man is if he lacks her! What does he who abounds in riches boast about? Fever is not afraid of a silver bed or the pomp of a rich man, nor does it fear the arrows of a warrior.

Since we have not yet experienced this, from what we know we can make conjectures about it. What is health? If you ask me what seeing is, perhaps I could answer, in regards to the body, which consists of perceiving shapes and colors. If you ask me about hearing, I will answer you that perceiving sounds. If you ask me about smelling, than perceiving smells. What does touch consist of? In perceiving hard or soft, hot or cold, rough or soft, heavy or light. What is health? Not feeling anything. But these same things that occur in us seem vile in comparison with others. Your sight is sharp: that of the eagle is perhaps even sharper. Your hearing is fine: there are beasts that have it even finer. Your sense of smell is very sensitive, but it does not surpass the sagacity of a dog. You distinguish flavors very well just by tasting them: there are animals that discern herbs even without tasting them and do not take what is harmful to them, while you, even if you distinguish foods very well, can be reckless and poison yourself. The sensitivity of your touch is extraordinary: how many birds sense the arrival of summer and emigrate, or the imminence of winter, and leave for warmer regions! What you feel when it has arrived, they sense before it arrives. I praised him for his health, but he perceives nothing of that in a stone, nothing in a tree, nothing in a corpse. 6. What could someone who could be defeated by him when he was still alive do to what he felt nothing? He did what he could, and he did it full of fury. But he who clearly suffered nothing was secretly crowned. He was already in possession of the promise of his Lord, who, wanting to give us security against those who kill the body, said: Do not fear those who kill the body and can do no more. How can they not do more, if that madman committed so many atrocities on Vicente's body? But what did he do to Vicente, if he did nothing to him even when he was alive? Therefore, being healthy does not consist of not feeling anything, in the way that a stone, a tree or a corpse does not feel, but rather living in the body and not feeling its weight. But, nevertheless, no matter how healthy a man is in this life, he does not stop feeling the weight of his healthy body. Also the healthy, but corruptible body weighs down the soul. It weighs down the soul, that is, it does not obey the soul in all its desires. He obeys her in many things: he moves his hands to work, his feet to walk, his tongue to speak, his eyes to see and he applies his ears to hear voices. In all these things, the body obeys. But, if you want to change places, you feel its burden, you feel its weight. The body does not move very easily to get where it wants. Someone wants to see a friend face to face; He knows that he is far away, that there are many days between them. He has gone forward with his soul; but, when he arrives with the body, he notices how much weight he has on him. can respond immediately: God is not seen in a specific place, nor partially, nor spread throughout space or separated by intervals. Although it fills heaven and earth, it does not mean that it is half in heaven and half on earth; In fact, this air fills heaven and earth, but the part that is in the sky is not on the earth. What water fills, it fills only in terms of the space it occupies; Half the water occupies half the space and all of it occupies all of it. God is nothing like that. That must be beyond all doubt, because God is not a body. Extending through space, being limited to a place, having means, thirds, fourths and totality is typical of bodies. None of that is God, because God is everything everywhere; It does not have one half here and the other half there, but everything is everywhere. It fills heaven and earth, but it is entirely in heaven and entirely on earth. In the beginning there was the Word. This is so that you apply what you heard to the same Son, since he is also one God with the Father: equal not in magnitude, but in divinity. In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. She was in the beginning with God. Through her all things were made and without her nothing was made. And then below: And the light shines in the darkness. This only begotten who remains entirely with the Father, wholly shines in the darkness, who is wholly in heaven, wholly wholly on earth, wholly wholly in the Virgin, wholly wholly in his child's body, and not successively, as if he passed from one place to another. You are also completely in your house and completely in

the church; but, when you are in church, you are not at home, and, when you are at home, you are not in church. This is not the way in which he is all whole in heaven, all whole on earth, all whole in the Virgin, all whole in his child's body, not to mention more things, as if he were transferred from heaven to earth, from the earth to the Virgin, and from the Virgin to the child's body, but at the same time he is all whole everywhere. It is not scattered like water, nor is it removed like earth from one side and carried to another with fatigue. When everything is whole on earth, it does not leave heaven, and, in the same way, when it fills heaven, it does not move away from earth, since it reaches from one end to the other with strength and arranges all things with gentleness. 14. Therefore, if, at least once this body is transformed into a spiritual body, your eyes will be able to see a substance not limited to space; if they must be able to do so by some hidden force, never experienced and totally unknown, never perceived or valued; If you have to be able to do it, do it. We see with our eyes: we are not envious of them. We must put our efforts into one thing: not to locate God, nor to circumscribe him in a place, nor to believe him diffuse in space, as if he were a voluminous body; We don't dare to think that. Let the divine substance remain in its own dignity. Let us change for the better as much as we can, but without changing God for the worse. Above all, taking into account that in Scripture we have not found anything about it, or have not yet.

science. In this way, the singer of these words indicated how the Christian should ask to be freed from the power of enemies: not certainly by freeing himself from all suffering, but by patiently enduring what he has to suffer. Deliver me from the hand of the sinner; from the hand of him who despises the law and of the wicked. If you want to know how he wants to be delivered, pay attention to what follows: For you are my patience. Glorious will be the passion if this pious confession exists, so that whoever glories glories in the Lord. Therefore, let no one boast about himself when he has given a speech; nor of his strength when he resists temptation, since to speak well, our wisdom comes from him, and our patience to endure evils comes from him. It is ours to want, but it is required that we be called to want; It is our thing to ask, but we do not know what to ask; It is our turn to receive; but what do we receive, if we have nothing?; Ours is to have, but what do we have if we do not receive? Therefore, he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord. Thus, then, the martyr Vincent was worthy of being crowned by the Lord, because in him he chose to find his glory through wisdom and patience; worthy of this solemn celebration, worthy of eternal happiness, in the face of whose achievement the terrifying threats of the judge and everything the bloodthirsty executioner could inflict are slight. His sufferings are a thing of the past, but what he received will never happen. Whoever renounces this antidote will have no hope of regaining health. To anyone who tells me: "I will not forgive the sins that men may commit against me," I have nowhere to hold on to guarantee healing. I cannot promise what God has not promised, because I would cease to be a dispenser of his word and become a dispenser of that of the serpent. The serpent, in fact, promised good to those who sinned; God, on the other hand, threatened death. What happened to that man but what God had threatened? The promise of the serpent was far from him. Do you then, brothers, want me to say to you: "Even if you sin, even if you do not forgive men's sins, you will receive full health, because when Christ Jesus comes, he will grant forgiveness to all"? I don't say it, because I don't hear it; I don't say what I haven't been told. It is true that God promises forgiveness to the sinner; but forgive all past sins of the converted, the believers and the baptized. This is what I read, this I dare to promise, this I promise, and what I promise, is promised to me. We all hear it when it is read, because we are all fellow students: in this school there is only one teacher 4. 12. But how can he forgive you if you do not forgive those that are committed against you? 13. This sentence is for the heart of man like the jars used to bail out the water of the ship in the sea. It is impossible for water not to pass through the cracks in its structure. By gradually adding it drop by drop, such a quantity of water is collected that, if it is not drained, the ship will sink. In the same way, in this life we ​​have certain cracks, typical of our mortality and fragility, through which sin enters, coming from the waves of this world. Let's grab this sentence, as if it were a jug, to pour out the water and avoid sinking. Let us forgive the debts of our debtors, so that God may forgive us ours. By this sentence, if it happens that you say it sincerely, you cast out all the water that had entered. But be cautious; You are still on the high seas. It is not enough for you to do it once, unless, crossing this sea, you have reached the firm and solid land of your homeland, where no wave will shake you and you will not have to forgive, because no one will offend you; nor will you ask to be forgiven, because you will offend no one. 14. I think I have sufficiently insisted to your charity on this point; But, because of these waves that endanger us, I urge you to cling to this healthy remedy. Conversion of Saint Paul and Faustinus
Topic: The conversion of the apostle Paul and the pagan Faustino. Place: Carthage. Date: June 23, year 401.

1. We have just heard the words of the Apostle, or rather, those of Christ, who speaks through the mouth of the one whom he made, from a persecutor, a preacher; wounding him and healing him, giving him death and life at the same time; lamb slaughtered by wolves, makes lambs of wolves. It was already predicted in a famous prophecy. When the holy patriarch Jacob blessed his children by placing his hands on those present and looking to the future, he predicted what happened to Paul. According to his own testimony, Paul was from the tribe of Benjamin. When Jacob, in the act of blessing his children, came to Benjamin, he said of him: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. What to say? If he is a predatory wolf, will he be one forever? In no way. What then? In the morning he will take the prey and in the afternoon he will distribute the loot. This was fulfilled in Paul, because the prophecy referred to him. If it pleases you, let us consider him already taking prey in the morning and distributing the loot in the afternoon. The terms "morning" and "afternoon" here are equivalent to "before" and "after."

you?", but: Why do you persecute me? He replies: What do you want me to do? He who previously was fierce in persecution is now ready to obey. The persecutor is now taking the form of a preacher; the wolf, of sheep; the enemy, as a soldier. He heard what he had to do. He certainly went blind; In order for the inner light to shine in his heart, he was temporarily deprived of the outer light; It was taken from the persecutor to be returned to the preacher. In this way, even in their very blindness the mystery of believers was manifested, since whoever believes in Christ is the one who must look, considering other things as non-existent; so that the creature appears vile and the creator appears sweet to the heart. 2. Let's see it, then. He was led to Ananias, whose name means "sheep." See how the ravenous wolf is led to the sheep, to follow it, not to devour it. But so that the sheep would not be frightened by the sudden appearance of the wolf, that celestial shepherd who guided all these events announced to the sheep that the wolf was going to arrive, but not to shed blood. However, since the reputation of cruelty that preceded him was so great, the sheep, upon hearing his name, could not help but be filled with confusion. In fact, when the Lord Jesus announced to Ananias himself that Paul had already come to faith and that he must be approached, he said to him: Lord, I have heard about this man who has done much evil to your saints and who has now received letters from the

princes of priests so that wherever he finds followers of your name, he may take them. But the Lord replied: Don't worry, I will show you how much it is good for you to suffer for my name. Great and wonderful thing! The wolf is forbidden to be cruel and is taken captive before the sheep. So much fame had preceded him as a ravening wolf that just by hearing his name the sheep trembled even under the shepherd's hand. They encourage him to no longer consider him fierce or fear his pride. The lamb killed by the sheep reassures the sheep about the wolf. 3. Then, the one to whom last Sunday we sang: Lord, who is like you? Do not be silent or soften, O God, it is he who, however, says: Come to me and learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart. Let's see how it manifests both aspects and how both texts agree on it. He is meek and humble of heart because, like a sheep, he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb that does not bleat before the shearer, he did not open his mouth. Hanging from the tree, he suffered the unjust flames of hatred and endured tongues at the service of a terrible heart. The same tongues that wounded the saint crucified the righteous. you soften In the first place, he did not forgive error; He did not forgive cruelty, since he struck down with his voice those who were hungry for death; He deprived such a cruel man of the light and took him captive to Ananias, whom he sought when he was a persecutor. See that he is not meek, see that he is cruel; but not against man, but against error. This is not enough yet: do not remain silent yet or soften. To Ananias, who feared and trembled just by hearing the name of such a famous wolf, he said: I will show him. I will show you. Threatening veil, still hard veil: I will show him. Do not be silent or soften, O God! Show the pursuer not only your kindness, but also your severity. Show it to him; suffer what he himself did; also learn to suffer what he himself caused; experience himself what he inflicted on others. I, he said, will show him what he should suffer. Theme: The eternal happiness of Saints Perpetua and Felicidad. Location: Unknown. Date: March 7, feast of Saints Perpetua and Felicidad.

1. The anniversary we celebrate today brings to mind and in a certain way reproduces before us the day on which the holy servants of God Perpetua and Felicity, adorned with the crowns of martyrdom, flourished in perpetual happiness, being faithful to the name of Christ in combat and even finding their names united in the prize. We have heard the exhortations they received in revelations from God and the triumphs in the passion when it was read. How many people now go to the church of piety to honor them. Year after year charity contemplates with devotion what impiety sacrilegeously committed in a single day. They also contemplated it, but with very different intentions. They did with their screams what beasts did not do with their teeth. We, on the other hand, pity what the wicked did and revere what the pious suffered. They saw with the eyes of the flesh what reverted upon the cruelty of the heart; We look with the eyes of the heart at what was taken from them so that they would not see it. They rejoiced at the dead bodies of the martyrs; we feel pain because their own minds were dead. They, lacking the light of faith, thought that the martyrs had gone out; We, looking from faith, see them crowned. Finally, their very insults are our joy; this, pious and eternal; those, then evil, now non-existent. 3. We believe, brothers, and we believe with every foundation, that the rewards of the martyrs are the maximum. But, if we look closely at the combats, we will not be surprised by their greatness. In fact, although this life is tiring and temporary, it is nevertheless of such sweetness that, although men cannot avoid dying, they spare no effort to delay death. Nothing can be done to prevent death, but everything possible is done to delay it. It is true that everyone finds effort annoying, and yet even those who expect nothing good or bad after this life do

everything possible so that death does not put an end to their fatigue. Those to whom error makes them think of future and false carnal pleasures after death, or others who, guided by right faith, hope for an ineffably peaceful and happy rest, do they not also strive and worry extremely not to die soon? What does so much effort mean to obtain the necessary food, so much servitude, whether to medicine, or to other condescensions that the sick either demand or in any case are applied to them, if not to prevent the early arrival of the term that death entails? How much, then, must be paid for the exemption from death in the future life, if in this life its mere delay is so precious? I don't know what softness of this laborious life is so great and the natural horror of death in any of the living is so great, that not even those who, through death, pass to the life in which it will be impossible for them to die, want to die. 4. love to this life. Body pains are often compared to the fear of death anyway. Sometimes the first; Sometimes, the second is the one who dominates the man. The person subjected to torture lies to avoid dying; Even he who is about to die lies, so as not to be tormented. If he is not subjected to torture, he tells the truth so as not to be tormented for telling lies on his behalf. Be any of these the one that prevails in any minds. The martyrs of Christ defeated each other for the name and justice of Christ; They feared neither death nor pain. He who lived in them conquered in them, so that those who did not live for themselves, but for him, will not even die once they are dead. He showed them spiritual delights so that they would not feel bodily pain, only in the right measure to taste them without succumbing. Well, where was that woman not to realize that she was fighting with a very ferocious cow and ask when what had already been done would take place? Where was it? What was I seeing to not see this? What was he enjoying to not feel that? What love alienated her, what spectacle attracted her, what drink intoxicated her? She was still bound by the bonds of the flesh, she still carried limbs that were to die, she still felt oppressed by the corruptible body. What will happen once the souls of the martyrs, after the sweat of such dangerous combat, are freed from these chains, received in triumph by the angels and comforted there where they are not told: "Do what I have commanded you", but: "Receive what I promised you"? What spiritual joy feeds them! What security they enjoy in the Lord and how sublime

the honor and glory they receive! Who can show it with an example from this earth? 5. However, this life that the blessed martyrs now enjoy, although it no longer admits of comparison with any type of happiness or delight in this world, is nothing more than a small part of what was promised, a down payment until fullness arrives. The day of retribution will come, when, once the bodies are recovered, the entire man will receive what he deserves. Then, the members of that rich man who once adorned himself with ephemeral purple will be roasted in eternal fire, while the flesh of that poor man covered with sores, now transformed, will shine among the angels, although now he suffers in hell longing for a drop of water from the poor man's finger, while he rests deliciously in the bosom of the just. Great is the difference between the joys or sorrows of those who dream and those of those who are awake; Equally great is that which exists between the torments or joys of the dead and those of those already resurrected. I do not mean that the soul of the deceased is necessarily deceived like that of those who dream, but that one is the rest of souls deprived of bodies, and another is the radiance and happiness of the angels, with whom the multitude of the resurrected faithful will be equal, already in possession of their heavenly bodies. There the most glorious martyrs will shine with the very particular light of their honor, and the same bodies in which they suffered infamous torments will become worthy ornaments for them.

Theme: The victory of the martyrs is a gift from God. Place: Carthage. Date: Feast of Saints Mariano and Santiago: May 6, 397 or, according to others, May 8, 418.

1. Today the time has come to pay off my debt with the help of God. If the debtors are so well disposed, why are the creditors in an uproar? If everyone's minds are kept calm, the payment of the debt can reach everyone. I must talk about the passion and glory of the martyrs. Since they suffered martyrdom and were filled with glory, they are giving us a lesson in patience. They endured the cruelty of the mobs; Let us keep the people calm, since we have seen them through faith. The perseverance of the martyrs is worthy of all praise. But what eloquence is enough to do it? When will I make reality with the word what has already been accomplished in your hearts by faith? What is the origin of the great gift of patience? Where does every optimal gift come from? Where does the optimal gift come from but where does the perfect gift come from? Thus it is written: Patience produces perfect work. promises of the world; but this is little. It is not much to despise death or endure torment. In the fight to the death is full and glorious victory. Indeed, the first temptations proposed to our Lord, the king of martyrs, were something sweet: Tell all these stones to become bread. But I will give all these kingdoms. Let us see if the angels welcome you, for it is written: "Lest your foot strike against a stone." Here are the joys of the world: in bread, the lust of the flesh; in the promise of kingdoms, worldly ambition, and in the curiosity of trial, the lust of the eyes. All these things belong to the world, but they are sweet things, not cruel. Look now at the king of martyrs presenting us with examples of how we should fight and mercifully helping the combatants. Why did he allow himself to be tempted if not to teach us to resist the tempter? If the world promises you carnal pleasure, answer it: "God is more delightful." If he promises you secular honors and dignities, answer him: "The kingdom of God is higher than all." If he promises you superfluous and condemnable curiosities, answer him: "Only the truth of God is not wrong." What does the evangelist say after the Lord suffered this triple temptation, since in all the flattery of the world these three things appear: either pleasure, or curiosity, or pride? After the devil had put an end to all kinds of temptations; all kinds, but those that relied on flattery. There was still another temptation, consisting of something harsher and harder; in cruelties sed parum est; parum est enim lethum contemnere, parum est aspera tolerare; ubi usque ad sanguinem certamen, ibi glorious and full victory. While he made supplications to the Father, he listened to them with him. After his resurrection, he healed the insane people he had tolerated on the cross. He ascended to heaven, sent the Holy Spirit. But after he was resurrected, he did not reveal himself to everyone, but only to his disciples, so as not to give the impression that he wanted to mock those who had killed him. It was more important to teach humility to friends than to tell enemies the truth. He was resurrected, and in this way he did more than what was asked of him, not out of faith, but in mockery, when they told him: If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross. He who did not want to come down from the tree rose from the grave. He ascended to heaven, and sent the Holy Spirit from there; He filled the disciples with it, corrected the fearful and gave them confidence. Peter's fear suddenly turned into strength to preach. Where did this come to man? Look for Peter presuming, and you will find him denying; Seek God helping him, and you will find Peter preaching. For a moment his weakness trembled to overcome presumption, not to destroy piety. He fills him with the Holy Spirit, and turns into a courageous preacher that presumptuous man to whom he had said: You will deny me three times. Peter, in fact, had boasted of his strength; not from the gift of God, but from his free will. He had told him: I will go with you until death. He had said in his abundance: I will never move again. But he who of his own free will had given strength to her beauty, withdrew his face, and he was filled with confusion. God, he said, turned away his face: he revealed Peter himself; but then

He looked and secured Peter on the stone. Let us imitate, then, my brothers, the example of the Lord's passion as far as we can. We can do it if we ask for help; not going forward like the presumptuous Peter, but going after him and praying like the restored Peter. Pay attention to what the evangelist says when Peter denied the Lord three times: And the Lord looked at him, and Peter remembered. What does it mean: he looked at you? In fact, the Lord did not look at his face to remember him. The reality is different. Read the gospel. The Lord was being judged inside the house when Peter was tempted in the court. Therefore, the Lord looked at him not with his body, but with his majesty; not with the look of the eyes of flesh, but with his sovereign mercy. The one who had turned his face away from him looked at him and was free. Thus, then, the presumptuous would have perished had the redeemer not looked upon him. See now Peter, washed in his own tears, corrected and lifted up, dedicated to preaching. He who had denied it, now announces it; believe those who had found themselves in error. The medicine of the blood of the Lord proved to be effective in those insane. Becoming believers, they drink what they, furious, spilled. "But, someone will say, it is too much for me to imitate the Lord." Imitate your fellow servant with the grace of the Lord; He imitates Esteban, Mariano, Santiago too. They were men, they were your fellow servants; They were born like you, but they were crowned by someone who was not born that same way.

The role of martyrs in the Church
Topic: The function of martyrs in the Church. Place: Carthage. Date: May 22, feast of Saints Castus and Emilio'; from the year 397, or 405-410, or 416, according to different authors.

1. The great and pious courage, at the same time, of the holy martyrs - such is the fruitful courage, the only thing that can be called virtue, because it is at the service of God, not of pride - invites me to speak to your charity and to exhort you to celebrate the solemnity of the martyrs in such a way that, following in their footsteps, it will be a delight to imitate them. Well, not even they themselves drew from their own harvest to be brave. The water from that fountain did not reach only them. Whoever gave it to them can also give it to us, since it is a single price that has been paid for all. 2. One thing above all, you must be warned, which you must remember assiduously and which you must always think about: it is not

the penalty, but the cause, what makes the martyr of God. God delights in our justice, not our torments. And at the moment of judgment by the omnipotent and truthful God, the question will not be asked about what one has suffered, but rather why one has suffered it. We do not owe the fact that we can sign ourselves with the cross of the Lord to the suffering of the Lord, but to the cause of it. Well, if this were due to punishment, the punishment of the thieves would have been worth the same for that purpose. Three were crucified in the same place; In the middle was the Lord, who was numbered among the evildoers. Two thieves were placed on one side and the other, but their cause was not the same. They were on both sides of the crucified man, but a great distance separated them. They were crucified for their crimes; to the Lord ours. But, nevertheless, even in one of them it was sufficiently expressed how valuable not only the torment of the crucified person is, but the piety of the confessor. In the midst of pain, the thief obtained what Peter had lost out of fear. He recognized his crime, climbed the cross; He changed his cause and bought paradise. He who did not despise Christ for suffering the same penalty deserved to completely change his cause. The Jews despised him who worked miracles, he believed in him who hung from a tree. He recognized his companion on the cross as Lord, and by believing he did violence to the kingdom of heaven. The thief believed in Christ when the faith of the apostles trembled. He just deserved to hear: Today you will be with me in paradise. Not even he himself had raised hopes about it; He certainly trusted himself to great mercy, but he also thought

I think something similar has happened with these holy martyrs Castus and Emilio, whose feast day we celebrate today. Perhaps they too boasted beforehand of their strength, and that is why they fainted 4. The Lord showed them who they were and who he was. Contrary to what is said to Peter: Feed my sheep, is found in the Song of Songs: If you do not know yourself, O beautiful one among women! We certainly recognize to whom these words are spoken, and in it we too hear them. It is the Church that hears it from the mouth of Christ; the wife, from the mouth of the husband: If you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women!, go out yourself. How unpleasant is this word: Get out! They came from us, he said, but they were not ours. This sad word, come out, is opposed by another, pleasant for the good it expresses: Enter into the joy of your Lord. Therefore, if you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women, oh beautiful Catholic among heresies! If you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women, go out; I will not cast you out, but you come out. For from among our people came those who separate themselves, animal men, who do not have the Spirit. It was not said: "They were expelled", but: They left. Such was the way of proceeding of divine justice even with the first parents to sin. As they were already prone by their own weight, he let them leave paradise, he did not expel them. Therefore, if you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women!, you come out; I do not cast you out, you come out. I want heal you within my body; you want us to amputate the rot that is you. This is what was said to those who were expected to leave, so that they could recognize their state and try to remain.

Why then did they come out if not because they did not know each other? If, in fact, they had known each other, they would have seen that what they gave was not theirs, but God's. «It is I who gives it; Mine is what I give; and it is also holy, because I give it.” 6 Not knowing you, it was only fair that you left. You did not want to listen to the one who told you: If you do not know yourself, oh beautiful among women! You were beautiful once, when you were united to your husband's members. You didn't want to listen and appreciate what it means: If you don't know yourself. Indeed, he found you to be horrible; from ugly, he made you beautiful by turning you from black to white. What do you have that you haven't received? Don't you realize that it was said: If you don't know yourself, you get out? You thought you should feed your own sheep, contrary to what was said to Peter: Feed my sheep. You go out in the footsteps of the flocks and feed your goats. Not my sheep, like Peter, but your goats. In the shepherds' tents, not in that of the only shepherd. Theme: The posthumous glory of Saints Protasius and Gervasius. Location: Argentarium. Date: June 19, feast of the holy martyrs. From the year 425.

1. "Martyr" is a Greek term that custom has naturalized in the Latin language. In Latin it would be equivalent to "witness." There are, then, true martyrs and false martyrs, just as there are true witnesses and false witnesses. The Scripture says: The false witness will not go unpunished. If no false witness will go unpunished, no true witness will go uncrowned either. It was easy, in truth, to bear witness in favor of Jesus Christ the Lord and the truth of his divinity; The great thing is to give it to death. The gospel mentions some princes of the Jews who had believed in the Lord Jesus, who, however, did not dare to proclaim it publicly for fear of the Jews. And then a note was added to the statement, namely: They loved the glory of men more than that of God. 7. Sometimes, the compilation of the miracles of the martyrs that are read in your presence8 comes to mind. A few days ago a story was read according to which a certain sick woman, tortured by very acute pain, to the point of saying: "I can't stand it," the martyr who had come to heal her responded: "What would you say if you had to suffer martyrdom?" Many suffer true martyrdom in bed; many indeed. This is a more hidden and refined persecution of Satan than those of that time. A faithful person lies in bed tormented by pain; pray without being heard; rather, she is listened to, but she is tested, and exercised, and scourged to be welcomed as a son. Thus, in the midst of the torment of pain, the temptation of the tongue comes, some slut or some man, if that is what it can be called, approaches the bed, who says to the sick person: "Make such a bandage and you will recover; resort to such an incantation and you will be healed; So-and-so, and Mengano, and Zutano healed like this; ask them.” He does not give in, he does not obey them, he does not bend his heart, but he fights. His strength fails, but he defeats the devil. He achieves martyrdom on the bed, crowned by the one who hung on the tree for him. 7. Libelli de miraculis martyrum lecti in Ecclesia. Martyrium in lecto. Ego aliquando memoror de libellis miraculorum martyrum, quaa in conspectu vestro leguntur. Ante dies lectus est quidam libellus, ubi curam aegrotae quae doloribus acerrimis torquebatur, cum dixisset: Ferré non possum; ait illi ipse martyr qui sanare venerat: Quid, si martyrium duceres? Multi ergo ducunt martyrium in lecto; prossus multi. Est quaedam persecutio satanae, occultior et astutior quam tune Fuit. Iacet fidelis in lecto, torquetur doloribus, orat, non exauditur; immo exauditur, sed probatur, sed exercetur, sed ut recipiatur filius, flagellatur. Topic: The birth of John and that of Christ. Location: Hippo or surroundings. Date: June 24, feast of the nativity of Saint John the Baptist. After the year 425.

1. The story has been long, but the listener's fatigue is compensated by the sweetness of the truth. When the holy gospel was read, we heard the glorious birth of the blessed John, herald and forerunner of Christ. Your charity can deduce from this how great the man who has been born is. The Church never celebrated the carnal birth of any patriarch, prophet or apostle; It only celebrates two births: that of John and that of Christ. The same dates on which both were born contain a great mystery. Juan was a great man, but a man nonetheless. He was such a great man that only God could overcome him. Whoever comes after me is older than me. These are Juan's words: He is older than me. If he is greater than you, what does it mean that we have heard from the mouth of one who is greater than you: Among those born of women, there has been no one greater than Juan a Baptist? If no man is greater than you, what is he who is greater than you? Do you want to hear who it is?

Who is the voice, Christ the Word
Theme: John is the voice, Christ the Word. Place: Carthage. Date: June 24, feast of the birth of Saint John the Baptist. In the year 401.

1. Today's festival, in its annual return, reminds us that the forerunner of the Lord was born in an admirable way before the Admirable One himself. It is appropriate that, especially today, we reflect on this birth and praise it. For this purpose, an annual date has been dedicated to the miracle, so that oblivion does not erase from our hearts the benefits of God and the wonders of the Exalted One. John therefore, the forerunner of the Lord, was sent before him, but it was made by him. All things were made through her \ and without her nothing was made. Before the man God was sent a man who would recognize his Lord and announce his creator, distinguishing him with his mind and indicating him with his finger when he was already on earth. From John are those words that show the Lord and bear witness to him: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. No wonder, then, that a barren woman gave birth to the crier, and a virgin to the judge. Sterility

With your help, then, I make myself bolder before you, and after having explained the distinction between voice and word, I will hint at what follows from it. Juan represented the role of the voice in this mystery; but he was not the only voice. Every man who announces the Word is the voice of the Word. What the sound of our mouth is in relation to the word that we carry within us, that is the same thing that every pious soul announces in relation to that Word of which it has been said: In the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; she was in the beginning with God. Therefore, now consider the significance of those words: It is fitting that he should increase and that I should decrease. Pay attention, in case I manage to express myself; and, if that is not possible, by itself, I am able to insinuate, or at least to think, in what way, with what sense, with what intention, for what reason - in accordance with the distinction mentioned between the voice and the word - the same voice, the same John, said: It is fitting that he should increase and that I should decrease. Oh great and admirable sacrament! Consider how the person of the voice, mysterious personification of all voices, says of the person of the Word: It is fitting that he should increase and I should decrease. Because? Stay tuned. The Apostle says: We know in part and we prophesy in part; but, when perfection arrives, the partial will disappear. What is perfection? In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. See the perfection. What, then, does perfection consist of? The apostle Paul also says it: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God. To this Word of God that is next to God, equal to God the Father, by whom all were created.

Well, blessed, he said, are the pure in heart, for they will see God. He showed his flesh; He showed himself to his servants, but in the form of a servant. As if it were his own voice, among many other voices that he sent ahead, he also showed his own flesh. The Father was sought as if he could already be seen as he is; the Son, equal to the Father, spoke to his servants in the form of a servant. Lord, Philip tells him, show us the Father, and it will be enough for us. He was looking for what was the end of all his desires, that is, the end of his path, upon which he would have nothing more to search for. Show us, he said, the Father, and it is enough for us. Good, Felipe, good; You have well understood that the Father is enough for you. What does enough mean? Don't look for anything else; He will fill you, satisfy you, and bring you to perfection. But be careful, lest the one you are listening to be enough for you as well. Is he enough alone or together with the Father? But how can he be enough alone, if he never separated from the Father? So answer Philip, who wanted to see him: Have I been with you for so long and you still haven't met me? Philip, who has seen me, has also seen the Father. What does it mean: Felipe, who has seen me, has also seen

well to the Father, but: You seek the Father because you have not seen me? Philip, who has seen me, has also seen the Father. You see me and you don't see me. How else but because, existing in the form of God, he did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God? What, then, was it that Philip saw? He emptied himself by taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men and found in outward appearance like a man. This is what Philip saw: the form of a servant, later enabled to see the form of God. Thus, John personified all the voices, and Christ the Word. All voices must be diminished when we come to see Christ. The closer you come to the contemplation of wisdom, the less you need the voice. The voice appears in the prophets, in the apostles, in the psalms and in the gospel. That came: In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. When we see him as he is, will the gospel then be read? Should we listen to the prophecies? Or will we read the letters of the apostles? Because? For voices diminish as the Word grows, since it is fitting that He should increase and I should decrease. The Word itself does not increase or decrease. It is said, however, that it grows in us when we grow by progressing in it, in the same way that light grows in the eyes when, once their sight is healed, they see more, which before, when they were weak, they certainly saw less. The excellence of the Precursor

It neither decreased before nor increased afterwards. Therefore, the need for the voice decreases when the mind in its progress approaches the Word. In this way it is appropriate that Christ grows and that John, on the other hand, decreases. This is indicated by his own passions. In fact, Juan diminished when he was beheaded; Christ was exalted by growing, so to speak, on the cross. The dates of their respective births indicate the same, since from the day of John's birth the days begin to decrease, while from the day of Christ they grow again.

He who lacked faith was deprived of his voice, since it had already been written: I have believed, therefore I spoke. He did not believe, nor did he speak. John was born of a man and a woman; Christ, of only woman. Can John, perhaps, be compared to Christ? No way. However, it is not without importance that one so great preceded the Great. If the Lord our God deigns to help my effort with his gift, I will be able to explain what I feel, and my lowness will not feel alone, nor will your expectations disappointed. If, on the contrary, I am incapable of it, God our Lord will supply in your hearts what He deprived me of because of my weakness. I have anticipated this because I know and you do not know what I want to say, and I am already experiencing the difficulty of exposing it. I had to tell you about it, so that, while you pay attention, you can pray for me.

The Baptism of Jesus by John
Topic: The baptism of Jesus by John. The tree and its fruit (Mt 7,17). Location: Unknown. Date: June 24, feast of Saint John the Baptist. Before the year 405.

1. The solemnity of today requires a solemn sermon that responds to the enormity of the expectation. Therefore, with the help of the Lord, we will serve you what he grants us, remembering and keeping in mind our duty to serve, to speak not as a teacher, but as a servant; not to disciples, but to fellow disciples; because neither to servants, but to fellow servants. There is only one teacher for everyone, whose school and chair are on earth and in heaven respectively.' John was born as his precursor, whose day of birth is accepted by tradition to be today, and is celebrated today. This is how we have received it from the elders and this is how we transmit it to those who come after us with the same devotion, worthy of being imitated. Today, then, we celebrate the birth of John, not the evangelist, but the Baptist. Anticipating this, a question arises that must not be overlooked, namely: why the carnal birth of John is celebrated and not, rather, that of any other.
IN NATALI IOANNIS BAPTISTAE,

CAPUT I. — 1. Ioannis nativitas cur celebretur, non aliorum.—Diei hodiernae solemnitas solemnem desiderat tanta exspectatione sermonem. Ergo, adiuvante Domino, ministrabimus vobis quod dederit, recolentes et animo tenentes nostrae offi[1320]cium servitutis, ut loquamur, non tanquam magistri, sed tanquam ministri; non discipulis, sed condiscipulis; quia nec servís, sed conservis. Magister autem unus est nobis, cuius schola in terra est, et cathedra in cáelo; cuius praecursor Ioannes est natus, cuius natívitatis dies hodiernus traditur, hodie celebratur. Hoc maiorum traditione suscepimus, hoc ad posteros imitanda devotione transmittimus. Ioannis ergo non Evangelistae, sed Baptistae, Natalem hodie celebramus. Qua prima re posita, occurrit quaestio non praetereunda, quare Natalem, quo est ortus ex uterus Ioannes, potius celebremus,

another apostle, martyr, prophet or patriarch 2. If we are asked, what will we answer? In my opinion, as the mediocrity of my strength allows me to see, this is the cause: the disciples of the Lord were admitted to discipleship after they were born and after the passage of years had made them more capable; Their faith later associated them with the Lord, but none of them served Him from their birth. Let us also remember the prophets and bring to mind the patriarchs: they were born like all men, and, filled with the Holy Spirit, as they grew older they prophesied Christ; They were born first to prophesy later. John, on the other hand, prophesied at his very conception to the Lord, whom he greeted from the womb of his mother as soon as he was conceived. 2. Your holiness has already begun to notice how great and important this question appears: Christ had to be sent by the Father, and John sent before by Christ. John was sent first, but like the judge he is preceded by the procession. Christ the man was created later, but Christ God created John. John was, therefore, a perfect man, and the greatness of his grace was such that the Lord said of him: Among those born of women there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist. This great man recognizes the greatness of the Lord in his littleness; recognizes the man to whom he had come as the man God. Therefore, if among those born of women, that is, among men, no one has arisen

greater than John the Baptist, whoever is greater than John is not only man, but also God. Thus, this great man must not only have had disciples, but even recognized, in their company, Christ, the teacher of all. Is there a greater testimony in favor of the truth than to recognize, by humiliating oneself, someone who could envy out of emulation? He could, but he did not want to be considered Christ; He could be considered the Christ, but he did not want to. Men, deceived, said of him: "Could this not be the Christ?" He responded that he was not, to continue being what he was. In effect, this is how Adam lost, through his fall, what he was: by usurping what he was not. This great man had this very present, although insignificant compared to Christ even when he was a child; He knew this, he remembered it and retained it in his memory, because he thought about recovering what he had lost. John, this great man, as I have said, of whom the Lord gave such testimony that, emphasizing the truth, he went so far as to say: Among those born of women, no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen, could have been taken for Christ; Furthermore, those who were disoriented by the magnitude of his grace considered him to be Christ, and would even have died in that error if their own confession had not corrected them. To those who thought that he responded, saying: I am not the Christ. As if he had said: "There is no doubt that you deceive yourselves by paying me such an honor and certainly the praise you give me is great by thinking like this, but I must recognize who I am so that he can forgive your mistake." The Lord wanted to be baptized out of humility, not because he had any iniquity. Why was Christ the Lord baptized? Why was Christ the Lord, the only begotten Son of God, baptized? Investigate why he was born, and then you will find why he was baptized 4. There you will find the path of humility, which you cannot undertake with a proud foot; path that, if you do not tread with humble foot, you will not be able to reach the excellency to which it leads. He who came down for you was baptized for you. Notice how small he became despite being so great: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God. The equality of the Son with the Father was not prey, but nature. In John it would have been a robbery to want to be considered the Christ. Therefore, he did not consider it a plunder to be equal to God. Without being the result of a robbery, he was coeternal with the eternal, from whom he had been born. However, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, that is, taking the form of a man. Who, existing in the form of God, emptied himself by taking the form of a servant. He assumed what he was not without losing what he was. Remaining God, he assumed man. He took the form of a servant, and he became Godman by whom in his divine being man was made.

Consider, then, what majesty, what power, what greatness, what equality with the Father; He even put on a servile form for us; He also notes the path of humility taught by such a great teacher. It is more worth mentioning that he wanted to become a man than his willingness to be baptized by a man. 4. Thus, then, I repeat, John baptizes Christ, the servant to the Lord, the voice to the Word. Remember: I am the voice of one crying in the desert; Remember also: the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. John, I repeat again, baptizes Christ, the servant to the Lord, the voice to the Word, the creature to the Creator, the lamp to the Sun, but the Sun that created this sun; the Sun of whom it was said: The sun of righteousness has risen for me, and my salvation is in its wings. The wicked will say of him, with belated repentance, on the day of God's judgment: Of what use was pride to us? Or what did boasting about our riches bring us? All those things passed away like a shadow, and, with the shadows, those who followed the shadows. Therefore they will say: We strayed from the path of truth and the sun of righteousness did not shine on us; The sun did not rise for us. Christ is not born for those who do not recognize him. He, the sun of justice, without any cloud, does not rise for the wicked or for the impious or unfaithful. In fact, he makes this bodily sun rise every day on the good and the bad. So, as I said, the creature baptizes the Creator, the lamp the Sun, and not for that reason

Christus ut humilitatis viam doceret, baptizatus et incarnatus.—Praemissus est ergo Ioannes, ut Dominum humilem baptizaret. Baptizan enim Dominus propter humilitatem voluit, non propter iniquitatem. Dominus Christus quare est baptizatus? Dominus Christus Dei Filius unigenitus, quare est baptizatus? Inveni quare est natus, et ibi invenies quare sit baptizatus. Ibi quippe invenies humilitatis viam, quam pede superbo non carpís; quam nisi humili pede calaveris, ad celsitudinem, quo perducit, pervenire non poteris. Baptizatus est propter te, qui descendit propter te. Vide quantus factus sit tantillus: Qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. Non enim erat rapine, sed erat natura aequalitas Filii cum Patre. Ioannes si se Christum putari vellet, illi rapiña esset. Non ergo rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. Erat enim, et sine rapiña erat, coaeternus ab aeterno natus erat. Tamen semetipsum exinanivit formam serví accipiens (Phil 2,6.7); hoc est, formam hominis accipiens. Qui cum in forma Dei esset, non formam Dei accepisset; ergo cum in forma Dei esset, semetipsum exinanivit, formam serví accipiens. Sic accepit quod non erat, ut non seguiret quod erat. Manens Deus, hominem assumpsit. Formam servi accepit, et factus est Deus homo, a quo Deo factus est homo. See a broader development in Treatises on the Gospel of Saint John 4,13 and 5,3.

The Baptism of Jesus by John

He who baptized was proud, but he submitted to him who was to be baptized. To Christ, who approached him, he said: Are you coming to be baptized by me? It is I who must be baptized by you. Great confession! Safe profession of the lamp under the protection of humility! If she had been emboldened against the sun, the wind of pride would have quickly extinguished her. This is what the Lord foresaw and taught us with his baptism. He, so great, wanted to be baptized by one so small; To put it briefly, the savior for those in need of salvation. Despite his greatness, perhaps Juan remembered some of his ailments. Where else does that It is I who must be baptized by you come from? Certainly, the baptism of the Lord brings health, because health is from the Lord, since the health of men is vain. Why, then, are the words: It is I who must be baptized by you, if I had nothing that needed healing? Admirable medicine is the humility of our Lord! One baptized and the other healed. Christ, then, is the savior of all, especially of believers; It is an apostolic and true affirmation that Christ is the savior of all men. Let no one say: "I have no need to be saved." Whoever says this does not humble himself before the doctor, but perishes in his illness. If he is the savior of all men, he is also the savior of John, since John was a man. Christ is the savior of all men: John, therefore, recognizes him as his savior. In fact, it cannot be thought that Christ was not John's savior. That is not what he says, making this humble confession: It is I who must be

baptized by you. And the Lord answers: Let all justice be fulfilled for a moment. What is all justice? In humility he praised justice. It is, above all, in humility that our heavenly teacher and true Lord intimated justice to us. The fact of being baptized fell within his teaching of humility, and since what he was going to do was with a view to teaching that virtue, he said: Let all justice be fulfilled. 5. We have certainly found those who say: "I am the Christ"; not with words, but—what is worse—with actions. His audacity does not extend to uttering such words. Who would hear them? Who can be so deceived that he allows such foolish people into his heart or ears? If the person who is going to baptize a person tells him: "I am Christ," he then turns his back, abandons such obvious human arrogance and seeks the grace of God. So he does not say explicitly: "I am the Christ." But he says the same thing in another way. See how Christ is the one who heals, the one who purifies and the one who justifies; no man justifies.. What does “justify” mean? Make one righteous. Just as “mortify” means to put to death and “to quicken” means to give life to someone, “justify” means to make one righteous. Here we go through a certain baptizer who does not enter through the door, but rather climbs down through the wall; He is not the shepherd or the guardian, but a thief and robber. In a hidden way he says: "I am the one who baptizes." If you refer it to your status as a minister, I dare to assent. Don't add anything else; anything else comes from evil. Just because you don't know the evil of a tree doesn't mean it stops being bad; On the contrary, it is all the worse the more its evil is ignored. Well, another tree. «I have already mentioned another tree, you say; That's why I said: 'From God.'” Now compare these two newborns; one was baptized by a manifestly chaste man; to the other one hiddenly adulterous; The first was born of a man, the second, of God. Listen to Juan. To those who approached him he said: I baptize you with water. You too, if you know yourself, are a minister of water. I, he said, baptize you with water; but he who is to come is greater than I. To what extent? I am not worthy to untie the strap of his shoe. How much he would not have humiliated himself even if he had declared himself worthy of such a thing! But he did not even consider himself worthy to untie the strap of his shoe. He is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit. Why do you impersonate the person of Christ? He is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit. He is, therefore, the one who justifies. "What do you say?" «It is I who baptizes in the Holy Spirit; I who justify." It is true that you do not say: "I am the Christ." Is it true that you are not one of those of whom it was said: Many will come in my name, saying, "I am the Christ"? You are caught. May you be found now, once captured, you who were lost before being captured! It is a beautiful thing to be cap-

tured in the nets of truth for food to the great king. Cease, therefore, to say: "I am he who justifies, I am he who sanctifies, so that no one can prove to you that you also say: "I am the Christ." We celebrate the birth of John and that of Christ, which cannot be without meaning, and, although I may be unable to explain it as the greatness of the matter deserves, it gives rise to fruitful and profound thoughts. John is born of a barren old woman, and Christ of a young virgin. Sterility gives birth to John, and virginity to Christ. At the birth of John, the age of the parents was not appropriate, and at the birth of Christ there was no marital embrace. John is announced by an angel who proclaims him; Christ is conceived by the angel's announcement. No credit is given to Juan's birth, and his father is left mute; it is believed to be that of Christ, and is conceived by faith. First faith comes to the heart of the virgin; Then follows fertility in the mother's womb. And yet, the words of Zechariah and those of Mary are almost the same. When the angel announced it to John, he said to him: How will I know this? I am old and my wife is already getting older. She said to the angel who announced her future birth: How will this happen, since I do not know a man? Almost identical words. But let us consider what is the order of things in the very fact of building our hearts. If I think of something to say, the word is already in my heart; But, if I want to speak to you, I worry about how what is already in mine can also be in your heart. This was, without a doubt, a necessity for the faithful precursor: that Christ be announced by someone who could be his emulator. John had disciples, Christ also had them; He seemed to have a separate school, but he was united to him as a witness. Therefore, among those born of women, no one greater than Juan Bautista has emerged. There were prophets who had disciples, but before the coming of Christ. Later there were great apostles, but great because they were disciples of Christ, not because they could have disciples at the same time as Christ. John has his own disciples, he gathers them, he baptizes. What should we think? Is it inside or outside the work of Christ? In truth he is within, to be released by God as man; He is apparently out to be believed in his capacity as a witness. Pay attention to this. Suppose that, for example, Peter, Andrew, John and the other apostles gave testimony of the Lord; They could say to them: «You praise whom you follow; you announce him with whom you are associated.
