I have already told you, he replied, that I am not the Christ. The one who has the wife is the husband; He who has come from heaven is above all. Those who believed in Christ were filled with admiration, while his enemies were confused precisely then, when anyone who could be believed to be jealous of him felt compelled to announce him. The servant is forced to recognize the Lord, and the creature to bear witness to the Creator; Better yet, he does not feel obligated, but rather he does it freely, because he is a friend, not a hater; He does not look out for himself, but for his husband. 7. This is how the husband's friends behave. Even in human marriages there is a certain rite according to which, leaving aside the other friends, an intimate, knowledgeable of marital secrets, called paranymph, is chosen. But there is a difference here, and a big one. In human marriages it is one man who acts as paranymph for another; here John fulfills that function with respect to Christ; but Christ himself, the bridegroom, is also God, the mediator between God and men; but as a man, because as God is not a mediator, but equal to the Father, the same as the Father, one God with him. How could this have been a mediator?

sublimity from which we were so far away? To be in the middle, assume what you were not, but remain what you were so that we can arrive. See that God is superior to us, and we are inferior to him, the space that separates us being great; It is, above all, the abyss of sin that distances us the most. The distance being so great, where would we have to walk to reach God? God remains God, but man is united with God and a single person results, who is not a demigod, as if he were part God and part man, but God and man in their respective totalities: liberating God, mediating man, to be able to reach him through him, not through another; nor to another, but, rather, by that which we are in him by whom we were made. The Apostle certainly knew that Christ was God; for, speaking of the former merits of the Jews, he said of him: Of whom are the patriarchs and of whom was born Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all things, blessed forever; However, even though he knew that he was God and God over all things, and God over all things precisely because he had created them all, when he had to present him as a mediator he did not mention his divine being; Therefore, he is not a mediator insofar as he is God, but insofar as he became man. Such is our liberation. In fact, there is only one God. Since you are Catholics who are listening to me, educated Catholics, and you have heard carefully that there is only one God, I ask: Is God only the Father?

Or only the Son or the Holy Spirit? No, but the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God. Therefore, there is only one God and there is only one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. If he had said: "There is only one God and there is only one mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus," the impression would be given that he was dealing with a lesser God. In fact, it would seem that he was separated from that divine Trinity if one spoke of one God and one mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, as if that one God had nothing to do with him. But in the unity of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are included; preserve divinity and receive humility the mediating condition. 8. Thanks to this mediating action, the entire mass of the human race, separated from him by the sin of Adam, acquires reconciliation with God. Through Adam sin entered the world, and through sin death, and so it passed to all men, who all sinned in him. Who could be free from this? Who would distinguish themselves by moving from this mass of anger to mercy? Who, then, distinguishes you? What do you have that you haven't received? We are not distinguished by merits, but by grace. In fact, if they were deserts, it would be something due; and, if it is due, it is not free; and, if it is not free, one cannot speak of grace. The Apostle himself said this: If it comes from grace, no longer from works; for, otherwise, grace would cease to be grace. Thanks to a single person, we, the elderly, the minors, the elderly, the mature men, the children, the newborns, are saved: we are all saved thanks to just one person.

Topic: The excellence of John the Baptist. Location: Outside Hippo; probably not in Carthage. Date: June 24, feast of the birth of Saint John the Baptist. 1. The Lord wanted me to be able to offer my voice and my presence to your charity today; and he did this not by my personal disposition, but by his will. That is why I thank him along with you and give you the gift of my word, which is the ministry through which it is appropriate and convenient for me to serve you. On the other hand, it is up to you, dearly beloved, to welcome with love any dispensation of the servants of God and to give thanks, together with me, to the one who granted us this day to be together. 2. The holy John, born of a barren woman, precursor of the Lord, born of a virgin, greeted his Lord from the womb and announced him after leaving it. The excellence of John the Baptist

To come to men from the womb of a virgin, he sent many heralds before him. All the prophets were sent ahead by him, but in them he spoke, who came after them. Having, then, sent so many heralds before Him, why did this one deserve so much, why did this one, whose birth we are proud of today, have such excellence? For it is also a sign of a certain greatness that the day of his birth is known, as the day of his Lord is known. We do not know when the other prophets were born, but it was not convenient for us to ignore John's. A great merit is also manifested in the fact that others announced the Lord, whom they wanted to see and did not see; and, if they saw it in spirit, they saw what it was going to be in the future, but they were not here to see it present. The Lord himself says about them to his disciples: Many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you are seeing, and they did not see it, and to hear what you are hearing, and they did not hear it. Didn't he send them himself? But in all there was the desire to see Christ here, in the flesh, if it were possible. But since they preceded him in dying just as they had preceded him in being born, Christ did not find them here; but, nevertheless, Christ redeemed them to eternal life. And so that you may realize what desire everyone had to see Christ here, remember the old Simeon, to whom, as a no small gift, the Spirit of God announced that he would not leave this world until he had seen Christ. Christ was born; She recognized him without speaking, still in the arms of her

mother, took him and held in her hands the one whose divinity led him to himself, and, holding in her hands the Word that had not yet spoken, she blessed the Lord, saying: Now, Lord, you can let your servant go in peace, since my eyes have seen your salvation. 3. So the other prophets did not see it; Simeon saw him speechless; Juan recognized him and greeted him already conceived, announced him and saw him when he was already young. He is, therefore, more excellent than all others. Hear the testimony of the Lord about him: he put only himself before no one else. Great in the extreme was he whom no one could put before him other than Christ. Therefore the Lord says: Among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptist. And to take precedence over him: But he who is lesser in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. He claimed to be both lesser and greater: lesser by birth, greater by power; younger in age, older in majesty. Theme: John is the voice, Christ the Word. Place: Carthage. Date: Year 401.

This was said of him who was born of the virgin; This is the testimony he gave of his witness; This is the sentence that the judge pronounced about his herald; This is how the Word wanted to honor his voice, as you know and have heard even today in the morning sermon. 2. The word belongs to the heart, the voice to the ear. When the voice hurts the ear and does not lead to the mind with any words, it has an empty sound, without any useful fruit. Let us see in Christ and in John what I have said about the word and the voice. Seek Christ. In the beginning there was the Word. Where? And the Word was with God. In the beginning he was with God. How long before us! How above us! And the Word became flesh to dwell among us. And how would we know this if we had not heard the voice? In fact, Christ was already walking among men dressed in mortal flesh, and yet men approached John and asked him: Are you the Christ? But he, to show that it was the voice, suggested to them the word it preceded; He rejected that undue honor and pointed his finger at Christ. To those who asked him: Are you the Christ?, John answered: Behold the lamb of God; behold he takes away the sin of the world. Listen to it, recognize it; I precede you and announce it. Remember that I said: I am the voice of him who cries in the desert: "Prepare the way for the Lord"; not to me, but to the Lord. When I call, I announce to him, since the voice of the herald means the arrival of the judge. But when the one whom I announce arrives and rests in your heart, it is fitting that he increase and I, on the other hand, decrease. You know, in fact, dearly beloved, that the word, when it takes the voice as its auxiliary and passes through the path of the ear to the region of the heart, that same word grows in the heart at the same time as it dies in the

ear. The sound that has struck the ear does not last; It does not last forever, since it has already come to mind. Why this? Because it is appropriate for him to grow and for me to decrease. 3. May he grow and I, on the other hand, decrease. As regards his passions, John is beheaded with the sword, Christ is raised on the tree; this one is elevated, that one is brought low; One's head is cut off so that it shrinks, the other's head is extended so that it grows. It is convenient for one to grow and the other to decrease. In my opinion, the ages chosen for the mothers are also not without meaning: Juan is given birth by an elderly woman; to Christ, a virgin in the flower of age; to the former, hopeless sterility; to this one, virginity intact; lastly, to this one, a growing young girl; to that one, an old woman in decline. 4. What is this, my brothers? What is the dignity of this man, whose birth, like that of Christ the Lord, was announced to his parents by an angel? How did he deserve that? For no one has emerged greater than him among those born of women. As you know, the angel Gabriel was sent to the priest Zechariah and the virgin Mary; He promises a son to both and receives a response from both. Zechariah responded to the angel who promised him the son: How can I know? I am old, and my wife is barren and advanced in years. Mary answered him: How will that happen, since I do not know a man? No one expects anything from the laws of nature and I even believe that they were unaware that before the gift of God's grace natural laws cease. Both respond out of doubt, and yet the first is punished and the second blessed. To the first it is said: You will be mute; to Mary: Blessed are you among women. Zechariah lost his voice, Mary conceived the Word. Then the Word

He becomes flesh in the virgin, and the voice is born from the world; Juan, at birth, gives speech back to his father, and the father, speaking, gives his son his name. Everyone admires each other, everyone is stupefied, and between murmuring and murmuring they say to each other: What do you think this child will be? Let us now speak with words of the gospel. Behold, the hands of the Lord were with him. What do you think will be the one who starts like this? Still so small and already so big! And if this one that begins now will be great, what will the one that has always existed be like! The one whom Juan, still locked inside his mother's bosom, recognized when he was still hiding in the bed of a virgin's bosom and whom he greeted with his movements when he was still unable to use his voice, what will he be? Do you want to know what it will be? I will tell you briefly; Listen to the prophet: He, he said, will be called lord of all the earth. 5. As we celebrate in this festive gathering the birth of the blessed John, precursor of the Lord, a great man, let us ask for the help of his prayers. Since he is the friend of the husband, he can also grant us the ability to reach the husband to merit obtaining his grace. But, if we want to obtain his grace, let us not insult his birth. Let the relics of sacrilege disappear, let vain desires and games disappear; do not do what is usually done; not, of course, in honor of demons, but not even according to the custom of demons. Theme: Christ grows, John decreases. Location: Unknown. Date: June 24, nativity of Saint John the Baptist.

1. The Church of Christ, spread far and wide, today celebrates the birth of John the Baptist, the friend of the bridegroom and the forerunner of the Lord. On this solemnity, I owe you a sermon, you owe me attention and we all owe devotion. Among those born of women, no one greater than John the Baptist has emerged; only he who created him precedes him. Something wonderful has happened: that he preceded in birth the one without whose work he could in no way have been born. No wonder John is the voice and Christ the Word, for he said: I am the voice of him crying in the desert, while of this it was said: In the beginning was the Word. Something similar happens in our words, although very different. The word is born in the mind before becoming the voice of the speaker; The voice is uttered through the mouth, so that through it the word is manifested to the listeners. The Truth says: Among those born of women, no one greater than John the Baptist has emerged. No man, therefore, can surpass this one; but he is only a man; Christ, on the other hand, is God and man. Since the first thing that is emphasized and learned in Christian grace is that no one should glory in man, but rather that he who should glory should glory in the Lord, man said of God, the servant of his Lord: It is fitting that he should increase and I should decrease. God, certainly, neither decreases nor increases in himself; But the more and more we progress in true piety, the more divine grace grows in men and human power diminishes, until the temple of God, which is formed by all the members of Christ, is brought to that perfection in which, every principle, every power and every force being annihilated, God is all in all. John the Evangelist says: It was the true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world; John the Baptist says: We have all received of his fullness. Thus, when the light, which in itself always remains whole, increases in the one who is illuminated, he decreases in himself when what he was without God disappears. Without God, man can do nothing but sin; Consequently, human power diminishes when divine grace, destroying sin, prevails. The weakness of the creature gives way to the strength of the creator, and the pride of private love is transformed into public love, John shouting from our misery regarding the mercy of Christ: It is fitting that he should increase and I, on the other hand, should decrease.

On that occasion, Nicodemus asked him how this could happen, that is, for man to be born again, since it is impossible for him to enter his mother's womb again and be born again. Have you not paid attention to what you heard from the mouth of the Lord, from the mouth of the good teacher, to what you heard error from the mouth of truth? To show you how, he gave it, among other things, a comparison. But first he said to him: No one ascends to heaven except he who has come down from heaven, the son of man who is in heaven. While on earth, he claimed to be in heaven, and even more notable, that the Son of Man was in heaven. In this way he manifested the unity of person in both natures, that is, in his being the Son of God equal to the Father, the Word of God, who from the beginning existed as God alongside God, and in his being the son of man, assuming the soul and human flesh, dressed as a man and come to seek men. Despite both natures, therefore, we must not speak of two Christs or two sons, but of one person, one Christ, Son of God and the same Christ, not another, who is the son of man; but Son of God according to divinity and son of man according to the flesh. Who among us, so inattentive and so unwise, would not be tempted to distinguish them in this way: the Son of God in heaven and the son of man on earth? But so that we would not make such a division, introducing two persons through it, he said: No one ascends to heaven except the son of man who came down from heaven. Therefore the son of man

came down from heaven. Was not the Son of Man made on earth? Did he not become the son of man thanks to Mary? But, oh man, he says, do not separate what I want to unite. It is a small thing to say that the son of man came down, for Christ came down, being the son of man the same who is the Son of God; He is sitting in heaven who walked on earth. He was in heaven, because Christ is everywhere, and Christ himself is the Son of God and the son of man. By the uniqueness of his person, we affirm that the Son of God is on earth, and by virtue of that same unity of person we have proven that the son of man is in heaven from the words of the Lord: The son of man who is in heaven. Because of that same uniqueness of person, when he was still found and visible on earth, Peter said to him: You are Christ, the Son of the living God. 10. For all those who are reborn become his members; the only Christ born of Mary is one Christ; The head united to his body, he forms a single Christ. This is what he meant by these words: No one ascends to heaven except he who came down from heaven. No one ascended except Christ.

11. "But the desolation suffered by the human race is greater now than ever." For now, if we analyze past history regardless of what concerns us, I do not know if the disaster is greater now than ever; but let us accept that it is so, as I believe. The Lord himself gives us the solution to the problem posed. Now, the world's devastation is greater than ever, he says. Why is it greater than ever now, when the Gospel is preached everywhere? You pay attention only to the fame that accompanies his preaching and not to the impiety with which he is despised. Let us leave aside, brothers, the pagans outside and examine ourselves. The Gospel is preached that already fills the entire world. Before being preached, the will of God was unknown; With his preaching he was exposed. As the Gospel was preached, we were told what we should love, what we should despise, do, avoid, and expect. We have heard all this; Nowhere in the world is God's will unknown. Suppose the world is a servant. Listen to the voice of the Lord. This servant is the world: The servant who ignores his master's will and does not do what is right will receive few lashes. The servant is the world; servant because the world was made by him, and the world did not know him. A servant who ignores the will of his master: this was the world before. The servant who ignores his master's will and does not do what he must will receive few lashes. But the servant who knows the will of his master: such is the world now; Now you say, better, let's repeat what follows: The servant who knows his master's will and does not do what he should will receive many lashes. Hopefully

receive many spankings! They are preferable to being convicted only once. Why do you refuse to be flogged abundantly, you servant who know your master's will and do not do what you must? You are told, to indicate just one of your Lord's desires: Store up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust devours them and where thieves do not dig up or steal them. You are on earth, and he says to you from heaven: “Entrust them to me; have your treasures where I am as guardian; send them before you; Why do you leave them with you? Can the Goth take away what Christ guards? But you, more prudent and wise than your Lord, do not want to accumulate treasures except on earth. You already know the will of your Lord, who wants you to place him up there; Therefore, when you leave him on the ground, be prepared to receive lashes in abundance. Behold, you already know the will of your Lord, who wants you to keep your treasure in heaven; You, by keeping it on earth, make yourself worthy of the whippings with your action. And, when you are scourged, you blaspheme, you murmur, and you dare to say that your Lord should not have done to you what he is doing. Should you, evil servant, have done what you are doing?

Theme: Saints Peter and Paul, lovers of true life. Location: Unknown. Date: June 29, feast of saints. In the years 416-420. 1. The blood of the apostles made this day a holiday for us. Thus the servants returned what had been spent for them with the blood of the Lord. As we have heard, the Lord commands the blessed Peter to follow him, even though he had had it in his mind to precede him when he said: I will lay down my life for you. He was carried away by presumption, unaware of his own fear. He wanted to precede the one who should follow. He wanted a good thing, but he did not respect the proper order. With bitter fear he experienced how bitter death was and iam legum comminationes non patitur: coepit velle reconcilian, dum nemo terreret: vel tune crede voluntati. Whore, coactus est esse catholicus: erit paenitens. Quis illum cogit petere reconciliationis locum, nisi voluntas propria? Modo ergo admíttamus infirmitatem, ut postea probemus voluntatem.

With bitter tears he washed away the sin fruit of bitter fear. His fear was questioned by a servant; his love, for the Lord. And what was the response of fear but human trembling? What did the Lord prophesy to Peter, who gave rise to this holiday? When you were younger, he told him, you girded yourself and went where you wanted; but when you grow old, another will gird you and lead you where you do not want to go. Where is that: I will go with you until death? Where is that I will give my soul for you? Behold, you will tremble with fear, you will deny me and cry; but the one for whom you feared to die will also rise and strengthen you. What is strange, then, that Peter feared before resurrecting Christ? Behold, Christ has already risen; The truth of his soul and his flesh is already manifest, the promise already has the guarantee of example. The Lord is seen alive after the cross, death and the grave. It is little to say that it was seen: it was touched, felt and examined. He spent with his disciples forty days going in and out, eating and drinking; not by necessity, but by will; not out of necessity, but out of love; eating and drinking; not feeling hungry and thirsty, but teaching and convincing. The Lord consoles us in this regard, personifying our weakness in himself when he says: My soul is sad to the point of death. The martyrs were great because they trampled the sweetness of this world; They were great because they experienced within themselves the harshness and bitterness of death. Indeed, if suffering death were an easy thing, what did the martyrs suffer in exchange for the death of the Lord? Where does their greatness, their excellency and the crown more splendid than that of others come from? The faithful know that the name of the martyrs is read separately from that of the remaining deceased and that they are not prayed for, rather the Church entrusts itself to their prayers. In that way? Why but because the death they chose to confess Christ and not deny him is certainly bitter? It is a great truth that nature shuns death. Review all kinds of animals; You will not find anyone who does not want to live or who is not afraid to die. The human race also has that instinct. Death is hard, but that does not mean, I repeat, that life should be denied. Peter, despite being old, did not want to die. He really didn't want to die, but he preferred to follow Christ. He preferred to follow Christ rather than avoid death. If the road were so wide

We do not rebuke, we do not accuse anyone for loving this life. But this life must be loved in such a way that love for it does not lead to sin. Love life, but choose life. To the lovers of life I ask: Who is the man who wants life? Even without saying a word, you all respond: "Who is the man who does not want life?" I add what the psalm added: Who is the man who wants life and loves to see good days? The answer is: "What man is there who does not want life and does not love to see good days?" Therefore, if you want to come to life and see good days, since that is a reward, consider the work that such a reward requires. Restrain your tongue from evil. It is the continuation of the psalm. Who is the man who wants life and loves to see good days? Then he added: Restrain your tongue from evil and let your lips speak no deceit; turn away from evil and do good. Say now: "I want." Both led a concordant life, both shed their blood, both received the celestial crown and both made this day sacred to us. Focus your attention, then, on the apostle Paul, remember his words, heard recently when his letter was read: I, he said, am going to be sacrificed and the moment of my death is near. I have fought the good fight, I have finished my career, I have kept the faith. For the rest, he said, I have left the crown of righteousness that the Lord, the just judge, will give me on that day. He who even gave us what was undeserved will not deny us what we deserve. The just judge will hand over the crown; He will give it, because he has someone to give it to. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith: the crown will be given to these merits; As I said, he who gave even what was undue will not deny what is due. What did he give without being obliged to give it? Before I was a blasphemer, a persecutor and an outrager. What did he give, then, without being obliged to do so? Let us listen to the Apostle, who confesses and praises the giver of grace with the confession of his life. Before, he says, I was a blasphemer, a persecutor and an outrager. Did you deserve to be an apostle? What was owed to him who was a blasphemer, a persecutor and an outrager? What but eternal damnation? And what did he receive instead?

Topic: The victory of Saints Peter and Paul. Location: Probably Hippo or surrounding areas. Date: June 29, feast of saints. Time of the Pelagian controversy.

1. The celebration of the feast of such great martyrs, that is, of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, required a greater influx of people. In fact, if the attendance is so great for the celebration of the birth of the lambs, what must it not be for that of the rams! Of the faithful that the apostles won with their preaching it has been said: Present the sons of rams to the Lord. So that the faithful could later pass, the apostles became guides in the straits of the passion, on the road covered with brambles and in the tribulation of persecutions. The blessed Peter and Paul, first and last of the apostles, who properly worshiped God, who said: I am the first and the last, met on the same day of their passion. Peter was the one who ordained Saint Stephen. When the martyr Stephen was ordained deacon, among other apostles there was also the apostle Peter. Peter was his organizer, Paul his persecutor. I am not worthy, he says, to be called an apostle. Because? Because I persecuted the Church of God. If you persecuted the Church of God, how come you are an apostle? What I am now: an apostle, for what I was before I was: By the grace of God I am what I am, and the grace of God was not barren in me, but I worked harder than all of them. Topic: The crown reserved for Peter and Paul and all the faithful. Location: Unknown. Date: June 29, feast of Saints Peter and Paul. In the year 418. 1. Without a doubt, my words are not enough to praise such preachers as those of whom we have heard and sung: Their sound spread to the whole earth, and their words to the ends of the earth. I must dedicate myself to that task even knowing that I will not satisfy your expectations. You ask me to praise the apostles Peter and Paul today, whose solemn feast we celebrate on this date. I know what your expectation is, and before it I declare myself defeated. I see, in fact, what is expected and from whom. But since the God of the apostles deigns to be praised by all of us, let his servants not take it wrong to be exalted in any way by him who is at the service of you who listen to me. 2. As all of you who know the Holy Scriptures know, the apostle Peter was the first of the disciples to be chosen by the Lord present in the flesh. Paul, on the other hand, was not chosen among them or with them, but much later, without being

In quo disputatur contra Vélagianorum haeresim 1. Petrus Apostolorum primus, Paulus novissimus.—Praedicandis praedicatoribus, et tantis praedicatoribus, de quibus audivimus et cantavimus, quod in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum (Ps 18,5), procul dubio nulla nostra verba sufficiunt. Devotionem debenmus, vestram expectationem non implemus. Exspectatis enim a nobis hodie [1368] praedicari apostólos Petrum et Paulum, quorum solemnis hic dies est. Agnosco quid exspectetis; et ubi agnosco, suecumbo. Video enim exspectari quid, a quo. Sed quia Deus eorum Iaudari digntur ab omnibus nobis, non dedignentur servi eius uteumque praedicari ab eis qui serviunt vobis. 2. idem tractatur argumentum.—Sicut nostis, omnes qui Scripturas sanctas nostis, apostolus Petrus Inter disciples, quos Dominus praesens ¡in carne elegit, primus electus est; Paulus autem non Inter ilios, non

therefore unequal to them. Peter, therefore, was the first of the apostles, and Paul the last; God, however, of whom they were servants, heralds and preachers, is the first and the last. Peter is the first of the apostles, and Paul the last: God the first and the last, before whom there is nothing, nor after. God, then, who presents himself as the first and the last for his eternity, united in the passion the first and the last of the apostles. The passions of both are united on the date of celebration, in the same way that their lives are united by charity. His sound spread to the entire earth and his words sounded to the ends of the earth. We all know where they were chosen, where they preached and where they suffered martyrdom. But how have we been able to know them themselves except because their voice reached the whole earth? 3. When reading his letter, we hear what Paul said about his passion, which was close and imminent: I am about to be sacrificed and the time of my departure is approaching. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Finally, the crown of justice awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day. But not only to me, but to all those who love its manifestation. Let's say something about it; His words are helpful to us, reaching the ends of the earth. First of all, see his holy disposition. He did not say that he was about to die, but rather to be immolated; not because he was not going to die, but because his death was an immolation, since not everything

he who dies is immolated. Being immolated is equivalent to dying for God. The word comes from sacrificial language. To sacrifice is to put something to death for God. The Apostle understood to whom he owed his blood shed in the passion. The one in whose favor his master's blood was shed became a debtor of his blood. He, one, shed his blood, and made them all debtors. All of us who receive faith owe what we receive, and this is because he deigned to make us debtors and payers. Who among us, filled with the indigence and poverty that comes with our own weakness, can pay such a great creditor? But, as it is written, the Lord will give his word, along with great strength, to those who announce it. The word, so that they make it known; strength, so that they resist suffering. He, therefore, prepared the victims, he consecrated the sacrifices, he filled the martyrs with the Spirit, he instructed the confessors with his power. To them, in fact, he said: It is not you who speak. Although he must suffer the passion, although he must shed his blood for faith in Christ, he rightly says: What will I return to the Lord for all the goods that he gave me? What occurred to you? I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord. You thought about giving back, and you were looking for what; and, as if you were going to repay him something, it occurred to you: I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord. Is it true that you were going to give him something? Notice that you rather receive it. You received what now weighs on you like a debt, and you also receive with which to pay it; You are a debtor when you receive and when you return. That

cum illis; sed longe postea, non dispar illis. Petrus ergo primus Apostolorum, Paulus novissimus; Deus autem, cuius hi servi, cuius hi praecones, cuius hi praedicatores, primus et novissimus. Petrus in Apostolis primus, Paulus in Apostolis novissimus: Deus et primus et novissimus, ante quem nihil et post quem nihil. Deus ergo qui se primum et novissimum aeternitate commendavit, ipse Apostólos primum et novissimum passione coniunxit. Utriusque passio concordat solemnitate, utriusque vita consonat caritate. In omnem terram exiit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum sonuerunt. Ubi electi sunt, ubi praedicaverunt, ubi etiam passi sunt, omnes novimus. Illos autem ipsos unde nos novimus, nisi quia in omnem terram exiit sonus eorum? 3. Apostoli verba de passione sua imminente. Ex Dei gratia et debitores efficimur, et redditors. Martyrum virtus a Deo. Revelatione Paulus confirmatus de sua future passione et victoria.—De passione sua iam imminente et propinquante praenuntiantem audivimus Paulum, cum eius Epístola legeretur: Ego enim iam immolor, et tempus resolutionis meae instat. Bonum certamen certavi, cursum consummavi, fidem servavi; de cetero reposita est mihi corona iustitiae, quam reddet mihi Dominus in illa die tustús iudex: non solum autem, inquit, mihi, sed omnibus qui diligunt manifestationem eius (2 Tim 4,6-8). Hinc dicamus aliquid: adiuvant enim nos, quae in fines orbis terrae exierunt, verba eorum. Primo sanctam deyotionem videte. Immolari se dixit, non mori; non quia non

mori tur, qui immolatur; sed non omnis qui moritur, immolatur. Ergo immolari est Deo mori. Ductum est enim Verbum a sacrifice. Omne quod sacrificetur, Deo occiditur. Intellexit enim Apostolus cui eius sanguis in passione debenretur: factus est enim debitor sanguinis sui, pro quo fusus est sanguis Domini sui. Unus ille sanguinem fudit, et omnes oppigneravit. Quotquot illam fidem recipimus, debenmus quod accipimus: et hoc quia dignitus est faceré et debitores et redditors. Quis enim nostrum in tanta inopia et paupertate infimitatis idoneus est reddere mucho creditori? Sed quomodo scriptum est: Dominus dabit verbum evangelizantibus virtute tumba (Ps 67,12); verbum, quo diffamentur; virtutem, qua patiantur. Ipse ergo sibi victims fecit, ipse sibi sacrifice dicavit, ipse implevit Spiritu martyres, ipse virtute instruxit confessores. Eis quippe dixit, Non enim vos estis qui loquimini (Mt 10,20). Quamvis ergo passurus, quamvis pro fide Christi sangui[1369]nem fusurus; recte tamen dicit: Quid, retribuam Domino pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi? And what happened? Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invoked (Ps 115,12.13). De retributione cogitabas, quid retribueres inquirebas; And occurrit tibi quasi retributuro: Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invokebo. Certe redditurus were you? Ecce accipis. Will I return? he said. I will take the chalice of salvation. Therefore you also receive this, that is, the cup of the passion, of which the Lord says: Can you drink the cup that I must drink? Behold, the chalice is already in your hand, the passion is already imminent. What do you do to not shake? What not to doubt? What do you do to avoid not being able to drink what you already have with you? "What will I do?" he says. Also in this case I will be the one who receives, and I will become a debtor, since I will call on the name of the Lord. I, he said, am already on the verge of being immolated. He was already certain thanks to a revelation: human frailty would never have dared to promise him that. His confidence did not come from himself, but from the one who gave him everything, the one he was referring to when he previously said: What do you have that you have not received? So, then, he said, I am already on the verge of being immolated and the time of my departure is approaching. I have fought the good fight. Ask your conscience; He has no doubt, because he glories in the Lord. I have fought, he said, the good fight, I have finished the race, I have maintained the goal. No wonder you finished the race, because you kept the faith. Finally, he said, the crown of justice awaits me, which the just judge will give me on that day. 4. It will be the opposite of this concealment and taciturnity. For God will manifestly come. He who first came in secret will later come clearly. 6. Look at the Apostle himself...3 the first of whom is me. Christ Jesus, he said, that is, Christ the Savior. This is what the word “Jesus” means. And let not grammarians ask to what extent it is a Latin term, but Christians ask to what extent it is true. The Latin word is salus (health, salvation). Salvare and salvator were not Latin words before the coming of the Savior; When he came to the Latins, he also made those words Latin. 4 Therefore, Christ Jesus, Christ the Savior, came into the world. 6. Salvator Christus Iesus. Paulus primus peccator, quia ceteris persecutoribus crudelitate superior. Pro supplicio debito salus ipsi reddita. Medicus Christus artis suae vim in Pauli curatione commendavit.—Vide ipsum Apóstol et omni acceptione dign in mundum peccatores [1371] quorum primus ego sum (1 Tim 1:15). Christus, inquit, Iesus, id est Christus Salvator. Hoc est enim latin Iesus. Nec quaerant grammatici quam sit latinum, sed Christiani quam verum. Salus enim latinum nomen est. Salvare et salvator non fuerunt haec latina antequam comeret Salvator; quando ad latinos come, et haec latina fecit. Ergo Christus Iesus, Christus Salvator, come in mundum. Et quasi quaereremus, Quare? Ait: Peccatores safe faceré. Ideo Iesus venit. In effect, he persecuted the Church more harshly. Therefore, if you ask what was owed to the sinners to whom Jesus came, you will not find that anything other than torture was owed to them. If you want to find out what was owed to them, the torture was owed to them; If you want to know what was given to them, salvation was given to them: instead of torture, salvation. The torture was owed to them, and salvation was granted to them; The punishment was owed to them, and the crown was donated to them. Nothing else was due to Paul, formerly Saul, the number one sinner, who surpassed all in cruelty; Nothing was owed to him except torture, and a great torture; but they call to him from heaven: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? He is cornered so that he forgives and he can be forgiven. The wolf transforms into a sheep; It is an understatement to say that he becomes a sheep: he becomes a shepherd. Thanks to the voice from heaven he is killed and brought back to life, wounded and healed. The persecutor is knocked down and the preacher rises. What grace is this but grace itself? What good merit did he have from before? It is called grace because it is given freely. Jesus came, he said, into the world to save sinners, the first of whom is me. But I have obtained mercy precisely. Could I then have said: What will the Lord, the righteous judge, give me on that day? If on that day the Lord were to pay the first sinner as a just judge, what would he give him but what the first sinner deserves: the great punishment, eternal punishment? This was what he deserved before, and it was not given to him. I have achieved, he said, mercy precisely. I did not receive what I deserved, but

I, the first sinner, obtained mercy precisely so that Christ Jesus would manifest in me all his long-suffering, as an instruction for those who were going to believe in him for eternal life. What does it mean: as an instruction? So that no one, even if he is evil, even if he is involved in crimes, loses hope of the forgiveness that Saul received. The great physician—that is Jesus—the great physician, coming to the region of sickness to make his medicine known, chose to heal one for whom there was little hope. This man, who was like this before, now says: I am about to be sacrificed and the time for my departure is approaching. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. - Were you the one who ran without brakes; that you led Christians to death; that, when Stephen was stoned, you kept everyone's clothes, so that you would be the one who stoned him in everyone's hands? Was that you? —Yes I was, he says, but I'm not anymore. —How come you were and you're not anymore. —Because I have obtained mercy. So you received, Paul, what was not due to you. Say now with confidence what is owed to you, say it now. Finally, the crown of justice awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day. With how much confidence does he demand what is due him, the one whose debt was annulled, that is, the torture! Say to your Lord now, say calmly, with certainty and full of confidence: «I used to live in my evil; I used your undeserved mercy. Crown your merits, for it is a debt. This is enough.

Ego dico, ut vivant, finitam esse culpam; you say, yes potes, finitam esse naturam. The ancient Church had its doubts in accepting the canonicality of the book of Revelation. In early times it was unanimously accepted: Saint Justin (Dialogue with Trypho 81,3), Papias, Saint Irenaeus (Against the Heretics IV 20,11; V 30,3), Muratorian Fragment, etc. That unanimity was broken in the 20th century due to a reaction against the mountaineers and all the millenarians. From then on, Eastern tradition is frequently against admitting it in the canon (Eusebius of Caesarea, Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, Saint Gregory of Nazianzus, Saint John Chrysostom, who never cites it, etc.), although not in all its representatives (Saint Athanasius, Saint Basil, Saint Gregory Niscnus, Saint Cyril of Alexandria, etc.) admit it. The West, on the other hand, always counted it among the canonical books. This already appears in the catalog of the Council of Hippo in 393 and in those of Carthage in 397 and 419.

Let us hear, then, in the gospel what Peter deserved and in his apostolic letter what Paul deserved. The gospel has been read and we have just heard: The Lord said to Peter: "Simon Peter, do you love me?" And he: "I love you, Lord." And the Lord again: "Feed my sheep." He questions him for the third time with an intention no different from the previous two. Christ had to question him three times, but it pained Peter to have to answer a third time. Peter was saddened, the gospel says, because the Lord questioned him a third time, and said to him: “Lord, you know everything; "You know I love you." And the Lord: "Feed my sheep." He who asks what he already knows wants to teach something. What, then, did the Lord want to teach Peter by asking him for the third time what he already knew? What are we to think, brothers, except that he asked him so that love would eliminate weakness and Peter would notice that he had to confess three times out of love to whom he had denied three times out of fear? Peter deserved to feed God's sheep. Let us now say what Paul deserved. Announcing his own future passion and removing his fear by example, he said to his disciple: I testify before God and Christ Jesus, who is to come to judge the living and the dead, both his manifestation and his kingdom. Contempt of the superfluous and the necessary

Theme: Contempt for the superfluous and the necessary. Place: Carthage. Date: July 17, feast of the Scythian martyrs. The latest, in the year 413. 1. The holy martyrs, witnesses of God, preferred to be alive in death so as not to be dead in life; Loving life, they despised it, so as not to deny life for fear of death. As long as Christ was denied, the enemy promised life, but not as promised by Christ. Believing, then, in the promises of the Savior, they mocked the threats of the persecutor. When we celebrate, brothers, the solemnities of the martyrs, we must know the examples that are proposed to us, examples that we must imitate. In fact, this influx of people does not bring an increase in glory for the martyrs. His crown is known to the multitudes of angels. We have been able to hear his passion when reading 1; but what they have received, neither eye has seen nor ear has heard. Among the goods of this world, some are superfluous, others necessary. Immo, quoniam videbas quod pauperibus exinde ibam, hospites suscipiebam, quod monuerat Paulus faciebam: praecipe, inquit, divitibus huius saeculi, praecipe, non superbe sapere, ñeque sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in deo vivo, qui praestat nobis otnnia abundantr ad fruendum. Bene faciant, divites sint in operibus bonis, facile tribuant, communicent, thesaurizent sibi fundamentum bonum in futurum, ut apprehendant veram vitam (1 Tim 6:17-19). Haec mihi auferens, this operates invoices non sum: numquid apud deum ideo rmnor ero, quia voló, et non possum? An usque adeo surdus sum adversus vocem angelorum: pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis? (Luke 2:14) Tolle ergo superflua mea. Nihil intulimus in hunc mundum, sed ñeque auferre aliquid possumus. Victum et tegumentum habentes, eo contenti simus (1 Tim 6,7-8),
Contempt of the superfluous and the necessary

5. But the pursuer adds: "I take away your food and shelter." He is already facing combat; The enemy rages with greater ardor. The superfluous has been left aside and the necessary has been reached. Do not depart from me, for tribulation is coming. There is nothing so close to the soul as its flesh; hunger, thirst, heat, you feel it in your flesh; That's where I want to see you, good martyr, witness of God. —Look at me, he says; look at me Who will separate us from the love of Christ? What are your threats? —I take away your food; I take off your coat. —is there tribulation? The narrowness? Hunger? The nudity? Threaten other things. —I take away your friend, I kill your most loved ones in your presence, I will cut the throats of your children and your wife. —You give death; Do you really kill? If they don't deny, you don't kill them. What does this mean? You do not frighten me in myself, and you want to instill fear in me by turning to my loved ones? If they do not deny, you do not kill them; If they deny, you kill others.—Add even more, full of cruelty, and say: —If you do not care about your own, I will make sure that you yourself will no longer see the light. —This light; perhaps also the eternal light? What light are you depriving me of? —The one I have in common with you. —That light that you also see is not a big thing. For this light I will not deny the light. It was the true light. I know to whom I must say: Because in you is the source of life, and in your light we will see the light. Take away my life, take away my light; I will have life, I will have light. I will have the life in which I will not have to suffer that you take it from me; I will have the light that not only you, but none

night can take it away from me.—The martyr won. Or is there still something else where we should expect an even greater combat? No. He threatens death, he attacks his health, he plows his flesh with hooks, he tortures him with various torments, he burns him in the flames, he throws him to the wild beasts: this is where he wins. Why does it expire? Because in all this we comfortably win through the one who loved us. 6. Therefore, my brothers, we must not deny Christ either to save what is superfluous or to save what is necessary; No one is more necessary to us than him. I said before that health and friends were necessary. To safeguard your health you sin and deny Christ; by loving health you will lack health. You sin for your friend, and in order not to offend him you deny Christ. Woe to me! Sometimes it is denied out of shame. No persecutor shows his cruelty on you, no robber despoils you, no executioner falls on you; You deny your Lord only so as not to displease your friend. I'm seeing what your friend takes from you; show me what he's going to give you. What will it give you? The same friendships that will make you sin, that will trap you, that will make you an enemy of God. He would not be your friend if you were your own; but since you are an enemy of yourself, you think that your enemy is a friend. How is it that you are the enemy of yourself? Because you love evil. He who loves evil hates his soul. But Christ is not denied to please an impious and perverse friend; It is not denied, but the wicked reviles it, the wicked accuses it, and the faithful does not defend it out of shame, it abandons it, it remains silent,

5. Sed ait persecutor: Tollo victum, tollo tegumentum. Accessum est ad certamen, ferventius saeviebat inimicus: transita sunt superflua, perventum est ad necessaria. Ne discedas a me, quoniam tribulatio proxima est (Ps 21,11,12). Nihil tam proximum animae suae, quam caro sua; fames et sitis et aestus in carne you feel: ibi te voló videre, martyr bone, testis dei. Vide, inquit, vid. Who separates us from caritate Christi? Quid est quod minaris? Tollo victum, tollo tegumentum. Tribulatio? Still anguish? Are you still famous? Still naked? (Rom 8:35) Minetur ex altera parte. Tollo amicum, occido carissimos tuos ante oculos tuos, coniugem et filios trucidabo. Occidis, occidis? Non negent, et non occidis. Who is he? Quia non me terres de me, terres me de meis? Si non negaverint, meos [79] non occidis; If negaverint, alienate us occidis. Adhuc addat persecutor, et saeviat, et dicat: Si tuos non curas, te ipsum huic lucí auferam. Huic luci: numquid aeternae luci? Cui luci are you helping me? quam communem habeo et tecum. Non est magna, quam vides et tu. Ego pro hoc lumine non negabo lumen. Erat lumen verum (lo 1.9). Novi, cui dicam: quoniam apud te fons vitae, et in lumine tuo videbimus lumen (Ps 35,10). (873) Tolle vitam, tolle lumen: habebo vitam, habebo lumen. Habebo vitam, ubi te non patiar interfectorem; habebo lumen, quod mihi, non dicam tu, sed

nec ulla nox possit auferre. Vicit martyr. An aliquid aliud est, ubi maius certamen spectare debenamus? No. Minatur mortem, saevit in salutem, exarat ungulis, excruciat tormentis, urit flammis, admovet bestias: et hic vincitur. Quare vincitur? Quia in his omnibus supervincimus per eum, qui dilexit nos (Rom 8:37). 6. Ergo, fratres mei, non negetur Christus propter superflua, non negetur propter necessaria: nullus ipso est magis necessarius. Necessaria dicebam, salutem et amicum. Peccas propter salutem, et negas Christum: loving salutem non habebis salutem. Peccas propter amicum tuum, et, ne illum offendas, negas Christum. Heu me miserum! Aliquando erubescendo negatur. Non saevit persecutor, non expoliat depraedator, non incumbit tortor; tantum ne displiceas amico tuo, negas dominum tuum. Video quid tibi abstulerit amicus: ostende quid dabit. Quid dabit? Ipsas amicitias, per quas pecces, per quas involvaris, per quas inimicus dei efficiaris. Iste tibi amicus non esset, si tu tibi esses; thirst, quoniam ipse inimicus est tibi, amicum putas inimicum tibi. Unde autem ipse inimicus es tibi? Quia amas iniquitatem: qui autem amat iniquitatem, odit animam suam (Ps 10,6). Sed non negatur Christus, ut amico impío et perverso placeatur; non negatur, sed ab impio vituperatur, ab impio accusatur, et a fideli erubescendo non defendí tur, deseritur, tacetur, non praedicatur.
The true riches

He doesn't announce it. The tongue of the blasphemer hurts him and there is no tongue that praises him. How many evils are committed as if they were for necessary things, for food, for shelter, for health, for a friend; and all these things seem so appetizing! But if you despise present things, God will give you eternal things. Despise health: you will have immortality; despise death: you will have life; despise honors: you will have the crown; despises the human friend: you will have God for your friend. But you will not be without the friendship of your neighbor where you will have God as a friend; there you will have as friends those whose deeds and confessions were recently read. 7. We heard how some men behaved and confessed their faith bravely and manfully; and we also heard how some women, forgetting their sex, clung to Christ as if they were not women 2. There will also be friendship with them; but friendship where there will be no place for the lust of the flesh, because there will be nothing else to enjoy with friends other than wisdom. See, then, what we lose if by loving such things here we deny Christ. There we are no longer terrified by the death of our neighbor; where life is eternal there will be no crying; nor will food and shelter be necessary, having which we must be content. Our dress will be immortality; food, charity, eternal life; nor will we have to carry out there the good works that receive their name from charity, since we will not achieve it if we do not carry them out here. Where there will be no hunger,

It will not be said to you: Share your bread with the hungry; where you will not find any pilgrim, you will not be told: "Welcome in hospitality"; where there will be no enemy, you will not be told: "Release the oppressed"; where peace will be eternal, you will not be told to make peace between the litigants. See, my brothers, how much you have to tolerate here to achieve it; We will have it there where we can no longer perish. Are you looking for health? Despise it and you will have it. Fearing to offend human friendships, you deny Christ; confess Christ, and you will have as your friend the city of angels, of the patriarchs, of the prophets, of the apostles, of all the martyrs, of all the good faithful. Christ himself founded it forever.

Saevit lingua blasphemantis, et nulla est laudantis. Quanta mala committuntur quasi pro necessariis, pro victu, pro integument, pro salute, pro amico; et omnia ista, quae appetuntur, magis pereunt. Si vero praesentia contempseris, dabit tibi deus aeterna. Contemne salutem, habebis immortalitatem: contemne mortar, habebis vitam: contemne honorem, habebis coronam: contemne amicum hominem, habebis amicum deum. Sed illic, ubi [80] amicum habebis deum, sine amico proximate non eris: ibi tecum amici erunt, quorum facta et confessiones paulo ante legebantur. 7. Audivimus viros fortíter agents, viriliter confitentes, audivimus et feminas non tanquam feminas tenentes Christum, oblitas sexum. Ibi erit cum istis illa amicitia, ubi nulla erit carnis concupiscentia, et sola erit cum amicis ad fruendum sapientia. Ecce quid perdimus, si ea hic amaverimus, et Christum negaverimus. Proximus ibi nos non terret, si moriatur; nullus ibi luctus, ubi aeterna vita erit; nec illud necessarium est, victum et tegumentum habentes his contenti simus. Topic: True riches. Place: Carthage. Date: July 17, feast of the Scythian martyrs. Year 397.

1. The strength of the martyrs of Christ, male or female, is Christ himself. In fact, if only men had remained strong in passion, such strength would be attributed to their sex. Therefore, he who also the weaker sex does not (874) fecerimus. Non tibi dicetur frange esurienti panem tuum (Is 58,7), ubi fames non erit; non tibi dicetur, Suscipe hospitio, ibi nullum invenies peregrinum; non tibi dicetur, Libera oppressum, ubi nullus inimicus erit; non tibi dicetur, Concorda litigationsum, ubi pax aeterna erit. Videte, fratres mei, quomodo hic tolerateretur quaerendo: ibi eam habebimus, ubi perire non possumus. Salutem quaeris? Contemne, et habebis. Negas Christum, timendo offendere amicitias hominum: confitere Christum, et amica tibi erit civitas angelorum, civitas patriarcharum, civitas prophetarum, civitas apostolorum, civitas omnium martyrum, civitas omnium bonorum fidelium. Christus ipse fundavit eam in aeternum (Ps 47,9).
[PLS 2,625] (MA 1,550) INCIPIT TRACTATUS DE NATALE SANCTORUM SCILITANORUM IN BASÍLICA NOVARUM

1. Martyrum Christi virorum et feminarum fortitudo Christus. Si enim viri soli in passione fortes exsisterent, sexui fortiori virtus tribueretur. Ideo fortiter pati et infirmior sexus potuit, quia deus in omnibus

has been able to suffer courageously, it is explained, because it was God who gave the power to both one and the other. Therefore, whether male or female, in the face of tribulation, every person must say: The Lord is my strength; and: I will love you, oh God!, my strength. Love itself is strength, because he who knows how to love is capable of suffering anything for the one he loves. And if even lascivious love has persuaded its lovers to courageously suffer countless things for their trifles and crimes, and those who lie in wait for the modesty of others close their eyes to any kind of danger, how much stronger must those be in the love of God who love him from whom they cannot be separated either in life or in death! In fact, the impudent lover will lose what he loves if he receives death for it; On the other hand, the brave and just lover of God not only will not lose him when he dies, but through death he will find what he loved. Therefore, the lover of crime is afraid to confess, while the lover of God is afraid to deny. Let us therefore choose, brothers, the love that makes our life innocent and our death peaceful. Once such love is chosen, when our bowels are possessed by it, our living will be Christ, and our dying will be gain. When we die we avoid what we hate and reach for what we love. Therefore, whoever loves this life tries to prolong it, if it is impossible to do so when he has already loved it. Whether you love it or not, what you love flees; That which you love flees, without you being able to hold it. You add years, life decreases, what you have left is less. Indeed, adding years is not equivalent to lengthening your life; On the contrary, if you look at what you have left, those years are gone. If they had joined you, they would have made your life longer. Now, potuit. Proinde licet sit vir, licet sit femina, in tribulatione sua debent dicere: dominas fortitudo mea (Ps 117,14), et diligam te, domine, virtus mea (Ps 17,2). Ipsa dilectio virtus est: qui enim novit amare, pro eo quod amat omnia perpeti potest. Et si hoc amor lascivus persuasit amatoribus, ut pro suis nugis et delictis plana fortiter patiantur, nec periculum ullum ante oculos [626] ponunt, qui alieno puderi insidiantur; quanto debent esse fortiores in caritate dei, qui illum diligunt, a quo et vivos et morientes separai non possunt? Amator quippe inpudicus perdet quod amat, si pro amata fuerit occisus; amator autem dei (551) fortis et iustus non solum, quia moritur, quod amavit non perdet, sed moriendo invenit quod amavit.

Denique amator delicti confiten timet, amator dei negare timet. Eligamus ergo amorem, fratres, in quo innocenter vivamus, et securi moriamur: hoc enim amore elect, cum ab eo fuerint possessa nostra praecordia, vivere nobis Christus erit, et mori lucrum (Phil 1,21). Dying quod odimus Evitamus; dying ad quod amamus pervenimus. Proinde qui amat hanc vitam, faciat, si post loving daytime non potest. Ames, non ames, fugit quod amas: fugit, nec tenes quod amas. Anni accessunt, aetas deficit, quod testat breviatur: non ergo anni producta vita
The true riches

For example, you had thirty years left; If you continue living, they decrease. Without reason, then, you added many years to your birth, years that with your long life you have been reducing. Do the counting using your fingers; Let them tell you not the years that have passed, but the ones you have left, and you will see that they are heading towards non-existence. Indeed, if it is now twelve noon, you cannot make nine in the morning return; Nor can you make a tomorrow with the yesterday that is gone; Furthermore, before long, even tomorrow will be yesterday. What good is it not to despise these things that you cannot hold here with your love? Your beloved day is passing, the desired God is approaching you. Love what you can reach with your love. He is faithful, he is by your side, come to him. Even for this you were lazy: he came to you, was born for you and died for you. 2. Do not fear, then, the bitter pill of death; Death is certainly bitter, but through that bitterness we reach great sweetness. That bitterness heals the viscera of your soul; but not the fact of dying, but dying for the truth. That bitterness is medicinal, not deadly; drink it calmly, it will heal your interior. Why does the patient hesitate to drink what the doctor did not hesitate to drink? He had nothing in himself that needed curing by the bitterness of such a drink; He drank it for you, so that you would not think that you were being offered poison. He drank it for you, so that you would learn to say: The death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord. Those who confessed Christ have suffered a variety of torments. Some were heritua accesserunt, sed, si tendes quod remanent, recesserunt. Nam si accessissent, longiorem vitam tibi fecissent: never vero restabant tibi, verbi gratia, triginta anni; ad hoc vivis, ut minuantur. Sine causa natali tuo multos annos addedidisti, ques pauciores diu vidando fecisti. Attende digits conputantis, non ut qui transierunt tibi renuntientur, sed qui remanserunt; et vides eos ad hoc vinore, ut non sint. Non enim, si agis horam tertiam, revocas primam: aut de die hesterno fugitivo crastinum facis; post paululum et crastinus erit hesternus. Quid prode est ista non contemnere, quae loving non potes detinere? Fugit te dies amatus, accit deus desideratus. Hoc ama, quo amarando pervenias. Fidelis est, stat ad te: veni ad eum. Et hoc piger eras: venit ad te, natus est propter te, mortuus est propter te. 2.

Noli ergo timere amarum poculum mortis: mors enim amara est, sed per hanc amaritudinem ad magnam transitur dulcedinem. Amaritudo is viscera animae tuae curat; non si moriaris, sed si pro veritate moriaris. Amaritudo is medicinalis est, non lethalis: sanat interiora tua, bibe securus. Quod non dubitavit bibere medicus, quare dubitat bibere aegrotus? lile, quod in se amaritudine poculi illius curaet, non habebat; propter te bibit, ne tibi venenum dari putares. Propter te bibit, ut disceres dicere: pretiosa in conspectu domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15). Confitentes Christum diverse perpessi sunt: alii gladio percussi,
The true riches

two were put to the sword, others were given over to the fire, others were thrown to wild beasts, and others were not even allowed to be buried. All things that are hard, cruel and horrifying, but in the eyes of men. That is why Scripture, when it praises the death of martyrs, says: The death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord, in the eyes of him who knows how to judge without being able to make mistakes. The fools and infidels seeing that the wise and faithful despised the happiness of this life, considered those who died for the name of Christ as unfortunate. Lacking the eyes of faith, they were unable to look at what they had promised. The maker and keeper of the promise came; With his words he confirmed them, and, granting the Spirit, left them completely healthy. He said in effect: Do not fear those who kill the body, without being able to do more. Look at those fools who are so cruel: if only they heard that they can't do more! There are many mischiefs that they do with the corpses: they tear them apart, burn them, scatter their ashes, do not allow them to be buried, and, as if glorifying, they say: "Where is what Christ said that, when a man kills another man, he can do nothing more? See how much I have done with the dead man's corpse. This person is, in his heart, similar to the other, who no longer feels in the flesh. Man without guts and fool! What have you done? You could have caused something to him if he had sensitivity; But, if it no longer has it, your cruelty has been in vain. I show you, he said, who you have to fear: the one who, in addition to killing you, has the power to throw you into hell. Power that the man who hurts does not have

and it kills, since its action only reaches the flesh; He cannot pursue the soul that leaves the body, because he does not even see it. Who is there to fear? Look who kills you and look how you die. Whoever had it before death has power over you after death, since no man would have done anything to you if he had not allowed it. Are you surprised that he allows it? Listen to the prince of martyrs, who, when judged by a man, he hidden God, manifest man, where he was an object of contempt; When, I repeat, he was judged by a man, this man swelled. “Aren't you answering me?” he said. Don't you know that I have the power to kill you and to set you free? But he, humble, Lord of all, servant of all, at the service of the sick out of love, not because of the demands of his nature, healed even that inflated and swollen man. It seemed that Christ was judged by him, and he was healed by Christ. The patient was terrified, but the doctor cut him off. He got an answer about what allowed him to swell at will. He did not say to him: “You have no power over me; Rather, it is I who has it over you. If he had said it, he would have told the truth, but he would not have given us an example. Even when he suffered he was teaching us, as he taught us when he was tempted. Just as he taught you what to respond to the tempter in the moment of temptation, in the same way he taught you what to respond to the persecutor when you are judged. Those words were our words; the head spoke instead of the body. What did he say to him, then? You would have no power over me if it had not been given to you from above. He didn't say he didn't have it, but

alii ignibus concremati, alii feris obiecti, alii nec sepeliri permissi. Dura omnia, saeva omnia, horrenda [627] omnia: sed in conspectu (552) hominum. Ideo scriptura cum mortes martyrum commendaret, pretiosa, inquit, in conspectu domini mors sanctorum eius: in conspectu eius, qui novit iudicare, et nescit errare. Attendentes enim stulti et infideles praesentem felicitatem contemni a sapientibus et fidelibus, miseros putaverunt, qui pro Christi nomine moriebantur; oculos enim fidei non habebant, ideo ad ea quae promissa erant prospicere non valebant. Venit promissor et dator: monendo confirmavit, giving spiritum perfecte sanavit. Ait enim: nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, et amplius quod faciant non habent (Luke 12,4). Vide stultos saevientes, si hoc audiant, non habent amplius quod faciant. Faciunt enim fines de cadaveribus: laniant, incendunt, spargunt, sepeliri non sinunt; et quasi gloriantes dicunt: Ubi est quod Christus dixit, quia cum occiderit homo hominem, amplius quid faciat non habet? Ecce so many feci de ca<da>vere mortui. Similis est corde ei, qui non sentit in carne. Dure et stolide, quid fecisti? If you felt, you fecisti; si non sentit, inaniter insanisti. Ostendo, inquit, vobis quem timeatis: qui, cum occiderit, habet potestatem mittere in gehennam (Luke 12,5). Quod non habet homo percussor et interfector, qui usque ad carnem

ferit, exeunte spiritu non sequitur, quia nec videt. Quis est timendus? Vide a quo occidaris, vide quomodo moriaris. Habet te in potestate post mortem, qui habebat ante mortem; nam nec homo in te aliquid faceret, nisi Ule permitteret. Miraris quia ille permittit? Audi martyrum principem, qui cum iudicaretur ab homine, deus oceultus, homo manifestus, in quo contemnebatur; ille ergo cum iudicaretur ab homine, inflavit se homo. Non mihi, inquit, do you answer? nescis quia potestatem drooling occidendi te et dimittendi te? (lo 19,10) Et ille mitis, dominus omnium, servus omnium, serviens aegrotis non condicione sed dilectione, et ipsum inflatum et tumentem curavit. Christus ab illo quasi iudicabatur, ille a Christo curabatur: tumidus terruit, sed medicus secuit. Ad ubi se inflavit ut voluit, responsum accepit; non ut diceretur ei, Non habes in me potestatem, sed ego habeo in te potius potestatem. Quod si dominus diceret, verum diceret, sed nobis exemplum non praeberet. Ille et cum pateretur docuit, quia et cum temtaretur docuit. Quomodo te docuit quid responderas temtatori, quando temtatus est, sic te docuit (553) quid responderas persecutori, quando iudicatus est. Vox illa nostra erat, caput [628] pro corpore loquebatur. Quid ergo ait? Non haberes in me potestatem, nisi datum tibi esset desuper (lo 19,11), Non dixit, Non habes; sed, Non S.Ag. 2}

that he would not have had if it had not been given to him from above. He taught the martyr that he must be submitted not to a man, but to God; He taught the martyr not to fear man when he has to suffer something, but rather the one who allows man to do that, the one who gives power to man. Instructed by such teaching, that most courageous woman said: We honor Caesar as Caesar, but we fear only God. He gave each one his own, with fair distribution; she responded neither proud nor timid. He set his sights on the Apostle, who said: Submit yourselves to all human authority for God's sake. We honor, he said, Caesar as Caesar. Even if you are cruel, be honest; maintain the order of submission, even if he does not have the supremacy of power. In fact, the greatest power is held by the one in whose hands we and our words are. Fear therefore, says the Lord, him who has power; power that, when it causes death, does not stop here, unable to go any further, but when it causes death, it is able to cast into the fires of hell. 3. Oh infidel, you who focus on present things and only the present terrify you!, sometimes think about the future. After one tomorrow and another, the last tomorrow will eventually arrive; One day pushes another day, but it does not drag down the one who made the day. In it, in fact, the day occurs without yesterday or tomorrow; in it the day occurs without birth or sunset; In it is the everlasting light, where the source of life is and in whose light we will see the light. Let the heart at least be there as long as it is necessary for the

meat is here; the heart is there. If the heart is there, everything will be there. The rich man dressed in purple and fine linen had no more pleasures; The poor man, full of sores, had no more miseries. The former feared the last day, the latter desired it. He arrived for both of them, but he did not find them both the same; and, since he did not find them both equal, he did not come equally for both. Dying was similar in both; Ending this life was a common condition for both. You heard what brought them together; Pay attention now to what separates them: It came to pass, then, that the poor man died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom; The rich man also died, and was buried. That one, perhaps, was not even buried. You already know the rest. The rich man was tormented in hell, the poor man rested in the bosom of Abraham. The pleasures and miseries passed. Everything is over and transformed. One went from pleasures to torments; the other, from miseries to pleasures. Indeed, both the pleasures and the miseries had been temporary; The torments and pleasures that befell them have no end. Riches are neither condemned in the person of the rich nor poverty praised in the person of the poor; but in the first impiety was condemned and in the second piety was praised. It sometimes happens that men hear these things in the gospel, and those who have nothing are filled with joy and even the beggar exults at those words. "In Abraham's bosom, he says, I will be, not that rich man." Let us respond to the poor man: «Your wounds are missing; apply yourself to achieve merits; He even desires the tongues of dogs. habuisses, nisi accepisses. Topic: The profession of faith of the Scythian martyrs. Location: Unknown. Date: July 17, feast of the Scythian martyrs. 1. The solemnity of this day exhorts us to speak to you about the martyrs of Christ, that is, about the witnesses of Christ who were not ashamed to confess his name before men. Whoever said to them: Do not think about what you are going to say, for the Holy Spirit will teach you what is convenient for you to speak, allow me to tell you what is convenient for you. "Martyr" is a Greek term that is equivalent, in our bes? Dominus dedit. Did you lose? Dominus abstulit. Gaude, quoniam, qui abstulit, non se abstulit. An tibi non sufficit, qui te facit? sicut domino placuit, ita factum est (Iob 1,21). Dec, what times? Cum tu sis malus, et ille bonus, tibi placet bonum, et illi malum? Non potest fieri. Crede bonum esse, quod placuit bono. Sicut domino placuit, ita factum est: sit nomen domini benedictum. Scimus quia diligentibus deum omnia cooperantur in bonum (Rom 8:28). language, to "witness." The holy martyrs, truthful witnesses, not false ones, testified with their blood that the other life must be put before the present; they/in fact, bravely despised this one, which is temporary. You heard, when they were read, the answers of the martyrs whose solemn feast we celebrate today. Since we cannot say everything, let us remember, at least, something about the constancy that burned within them, about the desire for the kingdom of heaven that was manifested in the fire of the words that enveloped them during the interrogation and about the person to whom they were united, from whom perhaps they received their own answers. You remember, dearly beloved, how, when the judge presiding over the hearing spoke of his confession in terms of "persuasion of vanity," one of them replied: Persuasion of vanity is committing murder and uttering false testimony.' In which of those things does the persuasion of vanity have to be seen? In the bad, with all certainty. Was not what vanity persuaded bad? Not in vain, then, was mentioned both by the one who was told not to think about what he was going to say, because the Holy Spirit would suggest it to him at the opportune moment. The Holy Spirit was, therefore, the one who moved him. The same case was on scene. Persuasion of vanity, he said, is committing murder and giving false testimony. Which is equivalent to saying: «You want to commit murder and you force me to give false testimony. "To deny Christ is to witness falsely." Say that Christ is not God and that those we worship are. Both statements are false: Christ

He is God and the others are not. Deny what you believe. «What you do not want me to have in my mouth, tear it from my heart; "Why do you forbid me to speak what you cannot take from my heart?" The truthful witness expresses what he has inside. Indeed, I have listened to the Apostle; better, to Christ through the mouth of the Apostle: With the heart one believes for righteousness and with the mouth one confesses for health. But the scoffer of truth and lover of vanity will say: “How is it that one confesses with the mouth for health? They speak, and death comes upon them. How then do they speak for health, if when they speak they only achieve death? If they said nothing, they would not die. As? It is confessed for the health that those who gave testimony saw, but not those who were frightened with death. The enemy threatened to take away their health, but they looked at something else that they were going to receive and that they would never lose. Looking at her made them strong, and, inflamed by her beauty, they despised the transitory health they have in common with animals. One is the health that is possessed in common with the angels and another is that which is possessed in common with the animals. The man is halfway between both. It has something similar to angels. That? The mind, reason, intelligence, wisdom. And what does it have in common with beasts? The flesh, weakness, destitution, mortality. Look at those other things and ignore them. IN SOLEMNITATE MARTYRUM MACHABAEORUM, I

CAPUT I. — 1. Christiani ante Christum nonnulli exstitere.—Istum diem nobis solemnem [1377] gloria Machabaeorum fecit: quorum mirabiles passiones, cum legerentur, non solum audivimus, sed etiam vidimus

dores to them. They happened a long time ago, before the incarnation and passion of Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior. They were members of that first people of which the prophets were also members, who predicted what we are seeing now. Let no one think that there was not a people consecrated to God before the Christian people existed. Furthermore, to speak in truth and not according to the usual use of names, even that people were then Christians. Not even Christ began to have a people after his passion, since his was that people born of Abraham to whom the Lord himself testified when he said: Abraham desired to see my day; He saw it and was filled with joy. That is why that people who were slaves in Egypt were born from Abraham, who with a powerful hand were freed from the house of slavery by the work of the servant of God Moses, led through the middle of the Red Sea, the waves opening a way for it; tested in the wilderness, subjected to the law and established in a kingdom. In the same town where, as I said, the prophets appeared, these martyrs flourished. It is true that Christ had not yet died, but the future death of Christ made them martyrs. 2. One thing, above all, I must recommend to your charity: when you feel full of admiration for these martyrs, do not think that they were not Christians. They were indeed Christians and with their heroic acts preceded the Christian name spread later. It might be thought that they did not confess Christ, since the impious and persecuting king did not force them to deny him,

something that the martyrs were later compelled to do; and, by resisting it, they achieved identical glory. Later persecutors of the Christian people forced the persecuted to deny the name of Christ; These, remaining firm in it, suffered the same as the Maccabees suffered, as we heard when their passion was read. These more recent martyrs, whose blood has stained the earth purple, were told and ordered by the persecutors to deny Christ. By not doing so, they suffered the same as the others. These, however, were required to deny the law of Moses. By not paying attention to them, they suffered for the law of Moses. Some for the name of Christ; the others, by the law of Moses. 3. To that person we respond: "In truth, being one of those who did not believe in Christ, branches broken off from the olive tree, later replaced by the wild olive tree, which dried up isolated, what are you going to say, one of those perfidious ones?" They did not explicitly confess Christ, because his mystery was still hidden. The Old Testament is the New veiled, and the New is the Old revealed. Look, then, at what the apostle Paul says about the unfaithful Jews, your fathers, but brothers.
