Do not think that the prayers of the saints for all of us can come out empty of the presence of the Lord; associated with theirs, neither will yours and mine be useless before God. I am going to give you an example taken from Holy Scripture. Tabitha, a widowed woman, dressed other widows. It came to pass that he died, the apostle Peter was called, and he came. They showed him the robes he had woven for the poor. The Lord was moved with mercy; He listened to Pedro, and brought the good worker back to the light. As she was rescued from death by the prayers of the widows, so also the Lord is able to deliver us from all evil through the prayers of blessed Cyprian and all the saints. 8. Itaque, fratres mei, obtestor caritatem vestram, ut firmum et paratum cor habeatis in deo. Topic: Commentary on Psalm 51:10. Place: Carthage, in the basilica of Cyprian. Date: September 14, feast of San Cipriano. In the year 397.

1. I will start by responding to my brother and colleague'. In the morning I said that charity had to be active, not lazy. But since he wanted it that way, let us obey him, and God through him and you; May God grant you to obey. We have sung: I have waited on God's mercy. Let's say something about our hope. The words of my sermon will adapt to the demands of the time; On the other hand, the hope that the sermon is about must endure and not end when my sermon ends. I have to speak and remain silent; She always cries out to God. But even hope itself - what I am going to say may be harsh, but it won't bother me if I show why I say it; I believe so—even hope itself will not be eternal. When reality arrives, there will be no hope; In fact, we talk about hope until we have the reality.

give, according to the words of the Apostle: But the hope that is seen is not hope; In fact, what one sees, how do you expect it? If, then, we hope for what we do not see, through patience we hope for it. Therefore, if the hope that is seen is not hope, since what one sees, how does one expect it? And it is called hope precisely because we hope for what we do not see, when the moment of vision arrives there will no longer be hope, because reality will be present. Then it will not be a curse to live without hope; On the other hand, now living without it is a curse and a disgrace. And woe to him who now lacks hope! It is harmful for him to live without it, since he does not yet possess reality; Hope will cease to exist when you are in possession of reality. 2. What is that reality that will be possessed? What will come after hope? We see, in fact, men now expecting many earthly things; Limiting ourselves to mundane aspects, no man lives without hope, and until the moment of death there is no one who does not have it; Children have the hope of growing up, of learning, of knowing something; young people, to get married and have children; parents, to feed their children, to instruct them, to see those they caressed as children grow up, to refer in a particular way to the core of human hope, which is the most natural, the most excusable and the most frequent. There are, in fact, many vulgar and completely reprehensible hopes; but let us hold on to this which is common and natural. Everyone is born for this: to grow, to get married,

to procreate children, to educate them and also to be called the father of children. What else do you want? But hope is not over yet: she wants to get her children married and she is still waiting. When you have achieved this, you want to have grandchildren; and, when he has attained this desire, he enters the third generation, and the old man is lazy to leave his place to the children. He is still after something to be desired and hoped for, and he seems benevolent. I hope, he says, that child can call me grandfather! When I hear it from your own mouth, I may die! The child grows up, calls him grandfather, and he still does not recognize himself as such. Indeed, if he is already a grandfather, if he is already old, why does he not realize that he must leave this world so that those who were born from him can succeed him? But, when he hears that honorable name in the child's mouth, he wants to educate him himself. Aren't you also expecting a great-grandson? Thus he dies, still with hopes; He expects one thing and another once he has received what he previously expected. When he receives what he expected, he is not satisfied, and longs for other things. Why did what you expected come? In all certainty, so that you put a limit on your path. That limit does not extend. How many are deceived by this hope, a trite hope! First of all, it does not satisfy when it arrives; but how many it does not reach! How many were waiting for a woman, and couldn't get married! How many were waiting for someone with whom they got along well, and married someone else who was a cause of torment! How many hoped to have children, and didn't get it! How many groaned because of the evils they received! And so everything. One expected riches; If he did not achieve them, he was tormented by ambition; If you got them,

What, then, is that long-awaited thing that, once it arrives, hope ceases, because its reality will happen to it? What is it? The land? No. Something that originates from the earth, like gold, silver, trees, harvest, water? None of these things. Something that flies in the air? The soul refuses it. Perhaps the sky, so beautiful and so adorned with its luminaries? What is more delightful and more beautiful among visible things? Neither is he. What is it then? All these things cause delight, they are beautiful, they are good; Look for who made them: he is your hope. He is now your hope and he will later be your possession. The holy and appropriate readings that are read publicly at the solemnities of the martyrs show us that their victories were predicted in advance and that they came true with the help of him who had promised them. If the world hates you, said the Lord, know that it hated me first; If you were of the world, the world would love what is its own. How great was the similarity between his passion and that of his Lord and Savior! False witnesses against one and against another and on the same matter. You know and remember what the false witnesses said against the Lord: We have heard him say: "I will destroy this temple and raise a new one in three days." That was not what the Lord had said; but the falsehood wanted to stay close to the truth. Why are they false witnesses? Because they heard him say: Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up in three days, the evangelist being careful to clarify: This he said about the temple of his body. The false witnesses changed Destroy to I will Destroy. A minimal change in syllables, but false witnesses; all the worse because they wanted to get closer to the truth through slander. And what was Esteban reproached for? We heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this temple and change the customs of the law. They bore false testimony while prophesying the truth. In the same way, that Caiphas, his teacher, prince of the priests, advising the Jews to kill Christ, said: It is better that one die before an entire people perishes. But the evangelist comments: He did not say this from his own perspective, but, as he was pontiff that year, he prophesied that consint electi, et ab Apostolis ordinati septem diaconi, in quibus sanctus Stephanus erat. Non autem hoc Dominus dixerat: sed vicina voluit esse falsitas veritati. How do I provide false tests? Audierunt dixisse: Solvite templum hoc, et post triduum resuscitabo illud. Evangelist autem dicit: Hoc autem dicebat de temple corporis sui (lo 2,19-21).

Falsi testes, pro eo quod dictum est Solvite, dixerunt Solvo. Modicum in syllabis mutaverunt; sed both falsi testes peiores fuerunt, quanto propinquare veritati per calumniam voluerunt. They brought him before the Sanhedrin so that the trial would have greater solemnity. But the friend of Christ, in stating his own cause, preached the truth of his Lord. He was going to die: what was the point of his pious tongue being silent before the wicked? Why not die for the truth? Only in this he bears no resemblance to his Lord as regards his passion, and this contains a mystery. He is, in fact, God by the excellence of his majesty. When the Lord was led to his passion, he preferred to remain silent during the interrogation; Esteban did not remain silent. Why did the Lord prefer to remain silent? For it had been prophesied of him: He was led like a sheep to the sacrifice, and like a lamb that does not bleat before the shearer, so he did not open his mouth. Why did Esteban, on the other hand, not want to remain silent? For the Lord himself had said: What I say to you in the darkness, say it in the light, and what you hear in the ear, announce it on the roofs. How did Saint Stephen announce it on the rooftops? Trampling the mud house. He who does not fear death tramples the flesh. He began by exposing the law of God to them from its beginnings: from Abraham to Moses; then, until the delivery of pontifex anni illius, prophetavit quia oportebat Christum morí pro gente (lo 11,50.51). Quid hoc est, brothers? Magna vis est veritatis. Oderunt veritatem nomines, et veritatem prophetant nescientes. Non agunt, sed agitur de illis. Processerunt ergo isti falsi testes similes falsis testibus, sed pro quibus occisus est Christus. CAPUT II.—3. Stephanus in concilium adductus cur non exemplo Christi tacet. Hearing this, as if what he had just said were a blasphemy, they covered their ears and ran to pick up stones. The psalm had said: Like a deaf asp that stops its ear. They clearly showed what was prophesied about them to be fulfilled. They began to stone him. Look now at that cruel man, remember the harshness of his words: Men who are stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears. He appears almost like an enemy; as if he wanted to kill everyone, if it were possible. This can be said by those who do not see the heart. His heart remained hidden; but, once his last words were heard, at the moment of being stoned, his interior was revealed. Lord Jesus, he said, receive my spirit. I have told it to you, to you for whom I die. Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. Because you helped him, your protégé won. Receive my spirit from the hands of those who hate it. Saint Stephen said this while standing. Then he bowed his knee and said: Lord, do not impute this sin to them.

Quis non crederet iratum, quis non crederet odiorum facibus inflammatum, quando dicebat: Dura cervice, et non circumeisi corde et auribus? Interea de cáelo Dominus aspexit, et vidit. Illi hoc audito, quasi blasphemia esset, quod ille dixisset, aures obturaverunt, ad lapides cucurrerunt. In Psalmo erat dictum: Sicut aspidis surdae, et obturantis aures (Ps 57,5). Prorsus exhibituerunt quod de iílis praedictum erat. Coepit they stone. Modo attendite illum saevientem, reedit verba dura: Dura cervice, et non circumeisi corde et auribus (Act 7,51). Quasi inimicus erat: tanquam, si fieri posset, omnes occidere cupiebat. Hoc dicat, qui cor non videt. Latebat cor eius; sed audita sunt novissima verba eius, et patuerunt oceulta eius, cum lapidaretur. Domine Iesu, inquit, accipe spiritum meum (ib., 58). Tibi dixi; tibi morior. Domine Iesu, accipe spiritum meum. Quia adiuvisti, vicit quem suscipis. Accipe spiritum meum, de manu eorum qui oderunt tuum. Hoc dixit sanctus Stephanus stans.

Where is that thing about Stiff-necked Men? How much shouting for this? Is this what all your cruelty boils down to? Outwardly you screamed, but inside you prayed. 6. Lord Jesus, receive my spirit; He said this standing up. By saying: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, he demanded what was owed to him. He demanded that what was promised to the martyrs be paid; a debt of which the Apostle says: I am already about to be sacrificed and the time of my departure is imminent. I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Finally, the crown of justice awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day. He will give me, he will pay me what he owes me. Who before only had to expect torture, later began to have God as a giver of rewards. Why is it that the apostle Paul could only expect torture? For having been an enemy and persecutor of the Church. Listen to him: I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God. I am not worthy: talk about deserts. Why don't you deserve it? I deserved to suffer punishments, to go to hell, to be tormented for my merits; but being an apostle did not deserve it. Where did that come from, then, that you did not deserve? Thus it continues: But by the grace of God I am what I am. Unfortunately for me, I was what I was; By the gift of God I am what I am. Therefore, in order to later demand what was owed to me, I first had to receive what I did not deserve. What was owed to me next? The crown of justice awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day. He will give it to me because

he owes it, even if it was previously undeserved. Because? I am not worthy to be called an apostle; but by the grace of God I am what I am. Thus, Saint Stephen also said: Lord Jesus, standing tall, in the confidence of having been a good soldier, of having fought well, of having not given in to the enemy, of having trampled on fear and of having defeated the world and the devil. This is the reason why he stood when he said: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. 7. At the time when Stephen claimed what was owed to him, the apostle Paul increased his personal debt. That one asked for the good that was owed to him; This added figures to his bad debt. What do you think, brothers? You heard when Stephen was stoned; But perhaps you did not notice that the false witnesses who were going to stone Stephen laid their clothes at the feet of a certain young man named Saul. This Saul was later Paul: Saul when a persecutor, Paul when a preacher. The name Saul comes from Saul. What Saul was to David, Paul was to Stephen. Then, however, he was called from heaven; He was called, torn down, transformed, and began to announce the word of God. He changed his own name, and was called Pablo. Why did you choose this name? Because Pablo (Paulus) means little, little one. We ourselves usually speak like this: Post paulum, that is, I will see you shortly. Why then is his name Paul? I am the least of the apostles. Saulus in Stephani falls saevior persecutor. Saulus a Saüle dictus Paulus, modicus, parvus. Quid enim putatis, fratres? Quando lapidabatur Stephanus, audistis, sed forte non advertistis, posuerunt falsi testes lapidaturi Stephanum, posuerunt ropa sua ad pedes cuiusdam adolescentis, nomine Sauli. CAPUT V.—Iste Saulus, et postea Paulus: persecutor Saulus, praedicator Paulus. Saulus enim nomen est a Saüle. Saül persecutor erat regis David. Talis fuet Saül in David, qualis Saulus in Stephanum. Post vero cum vocatus esset de cáelo; vocatus, prostratus, mutatus, ubi coepit apostolus praedicare verbum Dei; mutavit sibi nomen, et dixit se Paulum. Et hoc quare elegit? Quia Paulus modicus est, Paulus parvus est. Nos solemus sic loqui: Videbo te post paulum, id est post modicum. Unde ergo Paulus? Ego sum minimus Apostolorum (1 Cor 15:9). Magna, divine

show! Who was a persecutor at the time of Stephen's death, later became a preacher of the kingdom of heaven. Do you want to hear what his cruelty was in that death? He kept the stoners' clothes so he could stone him with everyone's hands. So, after the holy Stephen, standing, demanded what was owed to him with these words: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, turning his gaze on his enemies, who, by stoning him, contracted an evil debt to pay and added it to that treasure of which the apostle Paul says: Vero, according to your hardness and impenitence of heart, you store up wrath for the day of wrath and the revelation of the just judgment of God, he looked at them, he had compassion on them. and for them he bowed his knee. For them he bowed his knee, although he remained standing on his own. He distinguished between the righteous and the sinners. He prayed standing for the righteous, because he demanded the reward; For sinners he bowed his knees, because he knew how difficult his prayer could be heard by such criminal people. Though righteous, though with the crown on his head, he did not boast of himself, but bowed down on his knees; He did not look at what he deserved to receive in his prayer, but rather at what those from whom he wanted to keep such horrendous tortures away deserved. Lord, he said, do not impute this sin to them. 8. What the humble Stephen did, the exalted Christ did; What that one did while bending on the ground, this one did hanging from the tree. Remember that he also said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. He was sitting on the chair of the cross, and teaching Stephen the rule of piety.

Oh good teacher, you have spoken well, you have taught well! Behold, your disciple prays for his enemies, for his stoners. He showed how the humble should imitate you, exalted one; the creature to the creator, the victim to the mediator, the man to God and man; to God, but who, as a man, is on the cross; to Christ God, but man when he was on the cross and said with a clear voice: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. Someone will say: «He prayed for his enemies, but as Christ, as God, as the only Son; "Who am I to do the same?" If you consider it very important for you to imitate your Lord, do you not know that Stephen is a servant like you? God taught you through Stephen about to die. My brothers, if you see that there are already cases like this in the gospel, let no one say in their heart: "Who can do that?" See that Esteban did it. By himself? By your own strength? If, on the other hand, he did it by the gift of God, did he close the door on you as soon as he entered? Did he cut the bridge after passing it? Is it too much for you? Pray too. The fountain continues to flow; It hasn't dried yet. 9. My brothers, with all sincerity I exhort your charity: exercise yourselves as much as you can to show yourselves meek even towards your enemies. Put brakes on the anger that drives you to revenge, because anger is like a scorpion. If he excites you with his inner flames, you think that taking revenge on your enemy is something great. If I vindicate you, see yourself

in your own anger; She is, in truth, your enemy, since she kills your soul. Oh good man! I do not want to address you as a bad man; It is better for me to treat you as I want you to be rather than as you are. Good man! What can your enemy do to you? What can he do to you even if he can do a lot, even if God grants him everything he wants? He wants to spill your blood; It is certainly difficult and even enemies who bring their cruelty to the point of death are rare. Even enemies themselves, when they see that those they persecute are afflicted, usually turn their anger into mercy. It is difficult for you to find an enemy who will rage to the point of causing death. But suppose it is so. Think of an enemy who torments you until you die. What can it do to you? The same as the Jews with Stephen: seeking punishment for themselves and the crown for himself. Is your enemy going to kill you? Aren't you going to die? Or are you going to live forever? The enemy will do nothing more than fever will ever have to do; If it causes you death, it will be like a fever. So, by killing you, is it going to harm you? No; On the contrary, if you die well and love him, you are adding something to your heavenly reward. Do you not know how much his own stoners gave to Saint Stephen? Did they perhaps know that he would be awarded a crown for his goodness, while they would receive the punishment for their own evil? How many good things did the devil not give us? He has given us all the martyrs. But does he have to leave here? 'But these benefits he does not

I had them in view; That is why what he personally sought will be imputed to him, not what God did through him. Consequently, no enemy of yours will harm you even if it causes your death. 10. Look at the damage anger causes. Recognize her as your enemy; warns that it is she with whom you fight in the amphitheater within you. That amphitheater is narrow, but God is there as a spectator; tame your enemy there. Do you want to see how she is, in truth, your enemy? I'll show you. You start praying to God; The time must come when you have to say: "Forgive us our debts. How do you continue? Just as we also forgive our debtors. There your enemy stands, offering you resistance; she cuts off your prayer; she builds a wall that prevents you from moving forward. You have said everything before: Our Father. The prayer ran fluidly until: Forgive us our debts. What comes next? As we also forgive our debtors. Behold, your enemy is He confronts you not in the arena, but within you; in the very secret chamber of your heart he raises his voice against you and contradicts you. And what an enemy, brothers, that which contradicts you! Just as we also forgive you, it is better for you to rage against your enemy than for him to conquer a city. What I have just said is written.

If you face some enemies and find yourself facing a large, well-garrisoned, walled city that offers resistance, don't you claim the honors of triumph if you conquer it, defeat it, or destroy it? However, as the Scripture says, better is he who controls anger than he who conquers a city. This is in your hand. If you can't make it disappear, you can at least master it. If you are strong, overcome anger and forgive the city. I see that you are attentive and I know how well you have received it. May God assist you in your battles so that it may be of benefit to you to have attended as spectators the combat of such a great martyr, so that as you saw him win and acclaimed him in his victory, so you too may win in your hearts.
Topic: The circumstances of the martyrdom of Saint Stephen. Location: Hippo. Date: December 26, feast of Saint Stephen. Not before the year 425.

1. The blessed and glorious martyr in Christ Saint Stephen has already satisfied us with his word; but after this satiety I present to you as a second table in the word venit ad aliquos hostes, et invenit civitatem munitam, armatis instructam, optimam, adversantem sibi, si illam ceperit, si illam vicerit, si illam everterit, triumphos quaerit? IN SOLEMNITATE STEPHANI MARTYRIS,

CAPUT I.—1. Stephanus Inter deacons primus. Prodigy a Stepbano boasts, sed per nomen Christi.—Beatissimus et in Christo gloriosissimus martyr Stephanus iam sermone suo saginavit nos: sed post illam saginam appono vobis de sermone ministerii mei quasi secundam mensam. et

required by my ministry. And what can I find more sweet to serve than Christ and the martyr himself? One is Lord, another is servant; but Esteban, from a servant, became a friend. We are, without a doubt, servants; May he grant us to also be friends. But what kind of servants? Servants who can sing, lift up the forehead of conscience: Your friends have been extremely honored to me, O God! You heard what Saint Stephen was like when he was chosen by the apostles, before he received death in public and was crowned in secret. He appears as the first of the deacons, just like Peter the first of the apostles. Despite having been ordained by the apostles, in a short time he preceded those who had ordained him in the passion; they ordained him, but he was crowned before them. What did you hear when his passion was read? Stephen, full of grace and the Holy Spirit, performed great wonders and signs among the people in the name of Jesus Christ the Lord. Notice who did them and in whose name. Those of you who love Stephen, love him in Christ. This is what he wants and what pleases him; This causes him joy and gives him satisfaction. In fact, he did not want to boast about his name before the stoners. Observe who he confessed when he was stoned, who he confessed on earth and who he saw in heaven; for whom he gave his flesh and to whom he entrusted his soul. Have we read, or can we read somewhere as long as it is a sound doctrine, that Jesus did or does signs in the name of Stephen? Stephen made them, but in the quid dulcius invenio quod in ea ponam, quam Christum et Martyrem ipsum? lile enim Dominus, iste servus: sed Stephanus de servo amicus. Nos autem sine dubio servi: [1432] ille praestet ut simus et amici. What did I serve? You want to die, you rush to be stoned, you burn with desire to be crowned. You always resist the Holy Spirit. When he said this, they roared and gnashed their teeth. Add something else, Esteban; Add something else that they cannot bear or tolerate: add what gives them reason to stone you, so that we can find something to celebrate. The heavens opened: the martyr saw the head of the martyrs; he saw Jesus at the right hand of the Father; He saw it so as not to silence him. They did not see it, but hated it; What's more, they didn't see him because they hated him. He did not keep quiet about what he saw to get to what he saw. CAPUT I.—1. Reliquiae Stephani in Africam translatae, ac ubique ob Dei benefit diffamatae. Praeceptum diligendi inimicos habet grande praemium. Exemplum de Patre caelesti datum.—Martyr Stephanus, beatus et primus post Apostólos ab Apostolis diaconus ordinatus, ante Apostólos coronatus; illas terras passus illustravit, istas mortuus visitavit. Sed mortuus non visitaet, nisi et mortuus viveret. Exiguus pulvis tantum populum congregavit: cinis latet, benefit patent. Cogitate, carissimi, quae nobis Deus servet in regione vivorum, qui tanta praestat de pulvere mortuorum. Caro sancti Stephani per loca singular diffamatur: sed fidei eius meritum commendatur. Sic exspectemus consequi temporalia benefit, ut

of his faith. Let us hope to obtain the temporal benefits so that by imitating him we deserve to receive the eternal ones. Meditate, believe and practice what the blessed martyr proposed to us as an object of imitation in his passion; That is what the authentic celebration of the solemnity of the martyr consists of. Among the magnificent and salutary, at the same time divine and most high, precepts that our Lord gave to his disciples, the one that seems the most burdensome to men is the command to love one's enemies. The precept is onerous, but the reward associated with it is great. Furthermore, see what he said when intimating that precept: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you and pray for those who persecute you. You just heard the assignment; wait for the reward and see what he adds: That you may be, he said, children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes the sun rise on the good and the evil and sends rain on the just and the unjust. We are seeing this and we cannot deny it. Has it been said, perhaps, to the clouds: "Rain on the fields of my worshipers and stay away from those of those who blaspheme against me"? Has it been said, perhaps, to the sun: "See my worshipers and let those who curse me not see you"? Benefits of heaven, benefits of earth: the fountains flow, the fields are fertile and the trees are adorned with fruits. These things are common to good and bad; to the grateful and the ungrateful. Are we to think that he reserves nothing for the good who grants so much to the good and the bad? He gives to the good and the bad what he also gave to Stephen's stoners, but he reserves for the good what he gave to Stephen.

2. Following the example of this martyr, brothers, let us learn, above all, to love our enemies. We have been given the example of God the Father, who makes the sun rise on the good and the bad. The Son of God also said it, after becoming man, through the mouth of his flesh, which he took for love of his enemies. He who came into the world as a lover of his enemies found that absolutely all of them were enemies, not a single one was a friend. He shed his blood for his enemies, but with his blood he converted them. With his blood he erased the sins of his enemies, and, nullifying their sins, he turned them from enemies into friends. One of these friends was also Esteban; Better, it is and it will be. However, it was the Lord who was the first to show on the cross what he had taught. Referring to the Jews, who were roaring everywhere, furious, mocking, who insulted him and crucified him, he said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. Blindness is, in truth, what has crucified me. Blindness was crucifying him, and, once crucified, he made his blood a salve for them. 3. But there are men who are as lazy in the precept as they are eager for the reward, who do not love their enemies, but rather presume to take revenge on them, without fixing their eyes on God, who, if he wanted to take revenge on his enemies, not one would be left to praise him. eum imitating accipere mereamur aeterna. Quod nobis beatus Martyr imitandum in his passione proposuit, hoc attendere, hoc credere, hoc implere, veré est solemnia Martyris celebrare. Dominus noster Inter praecepta magna et salubria, divina et altissima quae dedit discipulis suis, hoc videtur hominibus grave, quod iussit ut diligant inimicos suos. Grave praeceptum, sed grande praemium. Denique cum hoc moneret, videte quid dixerit: Diligite inimicos vestros, benefacite bis qui vos oderunt, et orate pro persequentibus vos. Audisti opus, exspecta mercedem; et vide quid addat: Ut sitis, inquit, filii Patris vestri qui in caelis est, qui solem suum facit oriri super bonds et malas, et pluit super iustos et iniustos (Mt 5,44.45). Hoc videmus, hoc negare non possumus. Numquid dictum est nubibus: Pluite super agros culturarum meorum, et recedite ab agris blasphematorum meorum? Numquid dictum est soli: Videant te qui me colunt, non te videant qui mihi maledicunt? Benefits from heat, benefits from earth; scatent fontes, agri pinguescunt, arbores fructibus onerantur. Habent is boni, habent et mali; habent grati, habent ingrati. Qui praestat tanta bonis et malis, putamus nihil servat bonis? Hoc dat bonis et malis, quod dedit et lapidatoribus Stephani: hoc vero servat bonis quod dedit Stephano.

CAPUT II.—2. Exemplum aliud in Christo.—Máxime ergo, fratres, exemplo huius Martyris, inimicos nostros amare discamus. Exemplum propositum est de Deo Patre, qui solem suum oriri facit super bonds et malo. Dixit hoc etiam Filius Dei, post acceptionem carnis suae, per os carnis suae, quam suscepit loving inimicos suos. Qui enim amator inimicorum suorum [1436] in mundum venit, omnes prorsus inimicos suos invenit, neminem amicum invenit. Pro inimicis sanguinem fudit: sed sanguine suo inimicos convertit. Inimicorum suorum peccata suo sanguine delevit: delendo peccata, ex inimicis amicos fecit. De his amicis erat etiam Stephanus: immo est et erit. Ostendit tamen primus ipse Dominus in intersection, quod monuit. Undique enim Iudaeis frementibus, irascentibus, irridentibus, insultantibus, crucifigentibus, ait: Pater, ignosce Mis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt (Luke 23,34). Caecitas enim crucified me. Caecitas crucifigebat: et crucifixus eis de sanguine suo collyrium faciebat. 3. Exemplum et in Stephano. et parvus et magnus; raptor agnorum, et pastor agnorum; in ipso the candelabra lights up, when it says: Mihi utem absit glorian, nisi in cruz Domini nostri Iesu Christi, per quem mihi mundus crucifixus est, et ego mundo (Gal 6,14). Sed non accepit a se. Numquid accepit, et clausit tibi? Fons communis est: bibe unde bibit. Benefit Dei accepit: abundat qui dedit; et tu pete, et accipe. CAPUT IV.—5. Obiurgatio amantis nonnunquam acerba. Stephani amor erga suos interfectores.—Dominus amare et acerbe arguit Iudaeos, sed loving: Vae vobis, Scribae et Pharisaei hypocritae (Mt 23,13). Quando dicebat ista, quis non diceret quia oderat illos? Come ad cruzem, et ait: Pater, ignosce Mis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt (Luke 23,34). Sic et Stephanus in sermone suo prius arguit: Dura cervice, et non circumeisi corde et auribus. Verba sunt sancti Stephani, quando Iudaeos alloquebatur: Dura cervice, et non circumeisi corde et auribus; vos semper Spiritui sancto restitistis, sicut et paires vestri. Quem prophetarum non occiderunt paires vestri? (Act 7,51) This is saying, quasi odit, quasi saevit. Lingua clamat, cor amat. Audivimus linguam clamantem, probemus animum diligentem, Nam cum ad lapides cucurrissent, duri ad duros, iactabant in
love of enemies

against him what they were themselves. He who died for the Stone was stoned with stones, as the Apostle says: The stone was Christ. And, since his perseverance in teaching was so great, see what his patience was in death. His enemies destroyed his body with stones, while he prayed for them; The outer man was beaten, while the inner man begged. But the Lord, who had girded him, who had tested him, who had marked his seal not on his hand, but on his forehead, looked down on his soldier, ready to help him in combat and crown him in victory. Finally, it appeared to him. Behold, he said, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. Only he saw it, only he appeared to him. And what does he say in his own favor? Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. By himself he prayed standing; for them, on their knees. By itself, right; by them, inclined; by itself, erect; for them, in a humble attitude. He knelt down and said: Lord, do not impute this sin to them. And with that, he fell asleep. Oh. dream of peace! Who slept among the stones of the enemies, how will he wake among their ashes! He slept peacefully, peacefully, because he entrusted his spirit to the Lord.

standing, for them he knelt. It certainly fulfilled what is written. He was found a true imitator of the passion of the Lord and a perfect disciple of Christ who made reality in his own passion what he had heard from the teacher. Indeed, the Lord said while hanging on the cross: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do; The blessed Stephen, for his part, when he was almost covered with stones, said: Lord Jesus, do not impute this sin to them. Oh apostolic man, now converted from disciple into teacher! It was certainly appropriate for the first martyr of Christ to follow the teacher's teachings. Pray for the wicked, pray for the blasphemers, for those who were stoning him. Since it was difficult to be heard in his prayers for them, he added weakness to strengthen love. He knelt, he extorted. Do you think that he was not heard when he said: Lord, do not impute this sin to them? It was heard. Indeed, many of them believed. But I don't want to take you too far. That Saul who stoned him with everyone's hands, since he kept everyone else's clothes...; Stephen was heard in his plea for him. Even afterwards he breathed cruelty; Having received letters, he set out, tormenting the Christians; He was thirsty for blood and longed for deaths. But the Lord, who had listened to Stephen on his behalf, said to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? He whom you killed has prayed for you. "I also choose you to confess me and die for me."

We celebrate, then, the birth of Saint Stephen, and we have pro illis genu fixit. Utique quod scriptum est impleuit. Verus imitator dominicae passionis et perfectus est Christi discipulus adprobatus, qui quod a magistro audierat in sua passione complebat. Dominus enim, cum penderet in intersection, ait: Pater ignosce illis quia nesciunt quid faciunt (Luke 23,34); et beatus Stephanus, cum iam penis lapidibus obrueretur, sic ait: Domine Iesu ne statuas illis hoc peccatum (Act 7,59). O apostolicum uirum, iam ex disciple magistrum. Oportebat enim primum martirem Christi doctrinam sequi magistri. Rogat pro impiis, rogat pro blasphemis, pro lapidatoribus suis. Quia ergo difficile erat pro talibus exaudiri, accessit infirmitas, ut firmaretur caritas. Genua fixit, extortion. Putatis illum non exauditum, quando ait: Domine ne statuas illis hoc [205] peccatum? Exauditus est. Multi enim ex ipsis crediderunt. Sed non uos mitto longe. Saulus ille, qui omnium manibus lapidabat, qui lapidantium uestimenta seruabat (cf. ib., 60a.57), exauditus est pro illo Stephanus. Post saeuiebat; acceptis scriptis in christianos pergebat saeuiens; sanguinem sitiebat, caedes eagerbat (cf. Acts 9, lss; 22,5). Et dominus, qui pro illo exaudierat Stephanum: Saule Saule, inquit, quid persequeris me? (ib., 9,4; 22,7; 26,14). Quem occidisti roguit pro te. Et ego eligo te, ut confitearis me et moriaris pro me (cf. ib., 9,15; 26,16). Sancti ergo Stephani natalem celebremus et cum debita ueneratione

to celebrate it with due veneration. We have celebrated the birth of the Lord; Let us also celebrate that of his servant. Many of us attended the birth of the Savior, let us attend in equal numbers the birth of the martyr. The incorrupt Virgin Mary gave birth to the Lord, and the glorious martyr was brought to the palm of martyrdom by the holy Mother Church.

when it pleased the creator. Thus, some years ago in Milan, when I was still young, the bodies of the holy martyrs Gervase and Protasius 2 were found. You know that Gervase and Protasius suffered the passion long after the blessed Stephen. Why, then, did the former's appear first and then the latter's? Nobody gets into arguments; God's will asks for faith, not questions. What was true was revealed to whoever showed the discovery. The prodigies that preceded it already indicated the place; as it had been revealed, so it was found. Many took the relics from there, because such was the will of God, and brought them here. Both the place and the day are recommended to your charity: both must be celebrated in honor of God, whom Stephen confessed. We have not built an altar to Stephen in this place, but, with Stephen's relics, an altar to God. These altars are pleasing to God. Do you ask why? Because the death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord. Those who shed their own for the redeemer were redeemed with his blood. He poured it out to rescue his salvation; They poured it out so that the Gospel could spread. They paid him in the same coin; but not of his own, since he himself granted them what he could have done; The fact that what they were able to do was done was their gift. By showing them his benevolence, he gave them the opportunity to do the same. That's how it was: they suffered passion, because they had trampled the world.
Topic: The hard combat of martyrdom. Place: Hippo, in memory of Esteban. Date: Arrival of the relics of Saint Stephen. In the year 425.

1. Your holiness hopes to know what has been placed in this place today.' They are the relics of the first and most blessed martyr Stephen. When his passion was read in the canonical book of the Acts of the Apostles, you heard how he was stoned to death by the Jews, how he entrusted his soul to God and how, finally, he prayed on his knees for those who were stoning him. His body was hidden from then until current times; However, recently it was discovered, as is often the case with the bodies of holy martyrs, by revelation of God, colamus. Celebrauimus natalem domini; celebremus et serui. Frequentauimus natiuitatem saluatoris; frequentemus et natalem martyris. Dominum nostrum peperit incorrupta uirgo María, et Stephanum gloriosum ad martyrii palmam sancta mater prouexit ecclesia.
BY MARTYRE STEPHANO, V

1. Reliquiae Stephani martyris in loco sacro collocatae. Detectio corporum Gervasii et Protasii. Altare Deo erectum super relics Stephani.—Exspectat Sanctitas vestra scire quid hodie in isto loco positum sit. Reliquiae sunt primi et beatissimi martyris Stephani. Audistis, cum passionis eius lectio legeretur de libro [1438] canonical Actuum Apostolorum, quemadmodum lapidatus sit a Iudaeis, quemadmodum Domino commendaverit spiritum suum, quemadmodum etiam in extreme genibus fixis oraverit pro lapidatoribus suis (cf. Act 7). Huius corpus ex illo usque ad ista tempora latuit; nuper autem apparuit, sicut solent apparere sanctorum corpora martyrum, revelatione Dei, quando placuit Creatori. Sic ante Perhaps the sermon was preached on the day of the deposition of the martyr's remains in the basilica built for that purpose.

aliquot annos, nobis iuvenibus apud Mediolanum constituías, apparuerunt corpora sanctorum martyrum Gervasii et Protasii. Scitis quod Gervasius et Protasius longe posterius passi sunt, quam beatissimus Stephanus. Quare ergo illorum prius, et huius postea? Nemo disputet: voluntas Dei fidem quaerit, non quaestionem. Verum autem revelatum Fuit ei, qui res ipsas inventas monstravit. Praecedentibus enim signis locus demosstratus est; et quomodo fuet revelatum, sic et inventum est. Multi inde relics acceperunt, quia Deus voluit, et huc venerunt. Commendatur ergo Caritati vestrae et locus et dies: utrumque celebrandum in honorem Dei, quem confessus est Stephanus. We enim in isto loco non aram fecimus Stephano, sed de reliquiis Stephani aram Deo. Grata sunt Deo huiusmodi altaría. Quaeris quare? Quia pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15). Redempti sunt sanguine, qui sanguinem pro Redemptore fuderunt. Ule fudit, ut eorum salus redimeretur: illi fuderunt, ut Evangelium eius diffamaretur. Reddiderunt vicem, sed non de suo: ut enim hoc possent, Ule donavit; et ut ieront quod ab ipsis fieri potuit, ille donavit. Exhibiting dignityem, dedit occasionem. Factum est, passi sunt, calcaverant mundum.
See Confessions IX 7,15.
The hard fight of martyrdom

2. It was little for them to despise worldly delights: they overcame punishments, threats and torments. It is a great thing to despise what delights by confessing God; but it costs less to despise what delights than to overcome what annoys. Imagine someone being told, "Deny Christ and I will give you what you do not have." He despised what delights him and did not deny it. But the same persecutor added: «Don't you want to receive what you lack? I take away what you have." Gain does not taste as good as loss tastes like pain, since it is easier not to eat than to vomit. He did not acquire it: he did not eat; he lost what he had acquired: he vomited what he had eaten. By not eating you defraud gluttony; When you vomit, your stomach turns. He shows greater strength in confessing Christ who does not fear losses than he who despises new gains. What losses are these? Loss of money, assets, everything he had. But the enemy hasn't gotten too close yet. Things that are external to us have been lost. If you don't love them when you have them, they don't cause sadness when you lose them. And, to put it simply, they leave behind as much sadness as they could have been loved when they were owned. It seemed little to the persecutor of those times when the saints died to say: “I will take from you what you have. I torment you, he said; "I chain you, I kill you." He who does not fear this has conquered the world. Those who fought to these limits took the fight for truth to the summit. This is what the letter says to the

Hebrews: You have not yet fought sin to the point of blood. Those are the perfect ones: those who have fought against sin until blood was shed. What does against sin mean? Against the great sin, against the denial of Christ. You know how Susanna fought against sin to the point of blood. But so that the consolation of this example does not reach only women and that men seek among their sex something similar to that of Susanna, you know how Joseph fought against sin to the point of blood. The reason was identical. She had as false witnesses those whose desires she did not want to condescend to so as not to sin; he to the same woman to whom he did not give his consent. False testimonies were borne against both by those who saw how they were denied consent to sin. Those who heard them gave them faith, but they did not defeat God. She was freed and he was freed too. If they had died, what would have happened? Would they not have obtained a greater liberation because they would certainly have been crowned? Why did I say that they would certainly have been crowned? Because there would be no proof left for them. Indeed, although Susanna was freed, she is still subject to temptation; and Joseph was also delivered, but is still subject to temptation. Where will the temptation come from? Human life on earth is a temptation. Until the moment of death there is nothing but temptation; after it only happiness, but for the saints, whose death is precious in the eyes of God. She and he fought to the blood against sin: against

2. Martyres non tantunt saeculi delights, thirst, quod difficilius est, storm vicerunt. Contest usque ad sanguinem.—Parum eis Fuit contemnere delicias saeculi; poenas, mines, storm vicerunt. Pro confessione enim Dei contemnere quod delectat, valde magnum: sed minus est contemnere quod delectat, quam vincere quod molestat. Constitue alicui dictum esse, Nega Christum, et do tibi quod non habes: contempsit quod delectat, et non negavit. At the persecutor adiecit: Non vis accipere quod non habes? tollo quod habes. Non sic sapit lucrum, quomodo dolet damnum: quia facilius est non manducare, quam vomere. Non acquisivit, non manducavit: quod acquisierat perdidit, quod manducaverat vomuit. In non manducando gluttony fraudatur, in vomendo stomachus evertitur. Fortior est ergo in confessione Christi, qui damna non timuit, quam qui lucra contempsit. Sed damna qualia? Amissionem pecuniae, amissionem patrimonii, amissionem rerum omnium, quas habebat. Sed inimicus nondum proxime accessit. Res perierunt, quae forinsecus adiacebant. Si non sunt amatae cum haberentur, non contristaverunt cum amitterentur. Et ut breviter dicam, quando amittuntur, tantum maeroris dimittunt, quantum cum ha[1439]berentur, amari potuerunt. Sed persecutor illorum temporum, quando occidebantur sancti, parum Fuit dicere: Aufero quod habes. Torqueo, inquit, ligo, occido. Hoc qui non timuit, mundum vicit. Certamen pro veritate ad summum perduxerunt, qui usque ad ista certa-

verunt. Hoc est quod dicit in Epistle ad Hebraeos: Nondum enim usque ad sanguinem ádversus peccatum certastis (Hebr 12,4). Ipsi sunt perfecti, qui ádversus peccatum usque ad sanguinem certaverunt. What is this adversus peccatum? Ádversus magnum peccatum: adversus negationem Christi. Nostis quomodo certaverit adversus peccatum Susanna usque ad sanguinem (cf. Dan 13). Sed ne solae feminae hinc habeant consolationem, et viri de numero suo aliquid quaerant tale, quale in Susanna exstitit: nostis quemadmodum Ioseph contra peccatum usque ad sanguinem certavit (cf. Gen 39). Similis est causa. Et illa habuit false tests eos ipsos, quibus consentiré noluit, ne peccaret; et ille eam ipsam, cui noluit consentiré. Utrique quibus non est ad peccatum consensum, falsum dixerunt testimonium; et qui audierunt crediderunt: sed Deum non vicerunt. Liberatur illa, liberatur et ille. Quid, si et morerentur, nonne amplius liberaentur, quando securi coronarentur? Quare dixi, securi coronarentur? Quia mile tentatio remaneret. Nam etsi liberata est Susanna, adhuc tentanda; et ipse Ioseph adhuc tentandus liberatus est. Unde tentandus? quia tentatio est vita humano super terram (Iob 7,1). Usque ad mortem tota tentatio: post mortem sola beatitudo; sed Sanctorum, quorum mors pretiosa est in conspectu Dei. Et illa ergo contra peccatum, id est contra adulterium, et ille contra tale peccatum, üsque ad sanguinem certaverunt. Maius peccatum
Saint Stephen, martyr of Christ

adultery. It is a greater sin to deny Christ than to commit adultery. Adultery of the flesh consists of lying illicitly with another woman or man; that of the heart, in denying the truth. In faith, in the soul: that is where chastity must exist. The first to be corrupted there was mother Eva. Do you want to know the magnitude of the evil of that sin? Consider in us, born of it, the magnitude of our evils. I will cite Scripture as a witness to what I have just said: Sin, he said, began with the woman, and because of her we all died. What she received as punishment is what the martyrs for victory despise. So that they would not sin, God threatened them with death; To make them sin, the enemy threatened the martyrs with death. The first parents sinned to die; The martyrs died so as not to sin. From where punishment came to those, from there came glory to these. 3. So they fought and conquered. They were the first to win, but they did not cut the bridge they crossed, preventing us from accessing it. It is open to whoever wants; But it is not necessary to desire persecution like the one they suffered, because every day we encounter the temptation that is human life. It happens that a faithful person falls ill: there the tempter is present. He is promised, in exchange for recovering his health, an illicit sacrifice, a harmful and sacrilegious amulet, a nefarious spell, a magical rite, and he is told: "So-and-so found themselves in greater danger than you, and in this way they managed to escape from it; If you want to live, do that; If you don't do it, you will die. Consider whether that is not the same as this: "If

"You do not deny Christ, you will die." What the persecutor said openly to the martyr, the hidden tempter tells you in secret. "Apply this remedy and you will live": is this not the same as: "Sacrifice and you will live"? "If you don't, you will die": isn't that equivalent to saying, "If you don't sacrifice, you will die"? You have to face an equal struggle; expect an equal palm. You are in bed, and it is as if you were in the stadium; you lie sick, and you are fighting. Remain in faith, and your fatigue will be your victory. You have, therefore, dearly beloved, no small relief: this place of prayer. Let the martyr Stephen be honored here; but in his honor be worshiped who crowned Stephen.

est Christum deniale, quam adulterium perpetrare. Adulterium carnis est, illicite concumbere: adulterium cordis est, veritatem negare. In fide, in mente, ibi debent esse castitas. Prima ibi es parens Eva corrupt. Vis nosse in illa corruptione magnitudeinem iniquitatis? Attend in nobis, qui inde nati sumus, magnitudeinem calamitatis. Verbi huius mei sanctam Scripturam testem citabo: A mullere, inquit, initiutn factum est peccati, et propter Mam morimur otnnes (Eccli 25,33). Quod illa accepit in poena, hoc contemnunt martyres pro victoria. Mortem illis comminatus est Deus, ne peccarent: mortem martyribus inimicus comminatus est, ut peccarent. lili ut morerentur, peccaverunt: martyres mortui sunt, ne peccarent. Unde illis poena inflicta, inde istis gloria suscitata. 3. Martyrii quaedam luda in tentationibus quotidianis.—Certaverunt ergo, et vicerunt. Priores vicerunt: sed non pontem quo transiere praeciderunt, et nostrum accessum prohibuerunt. Patet cui placet: nec qualem illi passi sunt, optanda est persecutio; sed quotidiana est humanoe vitae tentatio. Aliquando aegrotat fidelis, et ibi est temptor. Promittitur illi pro salute illicitum sacrificium, noxia et sacrilega ligatura, nefanda incantatip, magic consecratio promittitur, eique dicitur: Ule et Ule peius te periclitati sunt, et [1440] sic evaserunt; fac, si vis vivere; you will die, yes
Theme: Saint Stephen, martyr of Christ. Place: Hippo, memory of Esteban. Date: Not before the year 425.

1. May the Lord grant me to say a few salutary words to you, who granted Saint Stephen the courage to say so many. As if he feared them, this is how he began, addressing his pursuers: Men, brothers and fathers, listen. Is there greater softness and condescension? The audience was conciliated to praise the Savior. He began with softness, so that he esnon feceris. Vide si non est, Morieris, si Christum non negaveris. Quod dicebat aperte martyri persecutor, hoc tibi ex obliquo dicit occultus tentator. Fac tibi hoc remedium, et Vives: nonne hoc est, Sacrifica, et Vives? If you do not feceris, you die: nonne hoc est, If you do not sacrifice you see, you die? Invenisti parem pugnam, quaere parem palmam. In lecto it is, et in stadio it is; iaces, et luctaris. Remain in fide; et dum fatiguetus es, vincis. Habetis ergo, carissimi, non parvum solatium, orationum locum. Martyr Stephanus hic honoretur: sed in eius honore coronator Stephani adoretur.
BY STEPHANO MARTYRE, VI

CAPUT I.—1. Stephani ad Iudaeos oratio quam prudens. Stephanus tanquam servus miracula facit in Christi nomine.—Donet mihi Dominus pauca dicere salubriter, qui donavit sancto Stephano tanta dicere fortiter. Sit coepit ad suos persecutors loqui, quasi timeret eos: Viri fratres et paires, audite (Act 7,1). Quid lenius? quid clementius? Conciliabat auditorem, ut commendaret Salvatorem. Blande coepit, ut diu audiretur. et
Saint Stephen, martyr of Christ

spoon for longer. And since he had been accused of having spoken against God and the law, he exposed the same law to them, becoming a preacher of the law who was accused of destroying it. You have heard this just as I have; Many words from me are not necessary, because you have already heard enough. I exhort only one thing to your charity to edify you: know that holy Stephen sought the honor of Christ; know that the holy martyr was a witness of Christ; know that he then performed such great miracles in the name of Christ. For your salvation, you know that holy Stephen worked miracles in the name of Christ, while Christ did not work any miracles in the name of Stephen. Distinguish, then, the servant of the Lord, the one who worships God, the worshiper from the one worthy of worship. When you make this distinction is when he loves you, because he did not shed his blood for himself, but for Christ. 2. See to whom he entrusted his soul. Behold, he said, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. He saw Christ when he confessed Christ, about to die for Christ and leave for Christ. And at the end, when the stones rained more intensely on him; when those hard hearts caused him harsh wounds; When he found himself close not to perdition, but to departure, he saw that his soul was about to emigrate and he entrusted it. Whom? To him whom he saw, whom he adored, whom he served, in whose name he preached, for whose Gospel he gave his life; He entrusted his soul to him.

Lord Jesus, he said, receive my spirit. You were the author of my victory, receive me in triumph. Receive my spirit. They persecute me, you welcome me; They cast me out, you welcome me in. Say to my spirit: Enter into the joy of your Lord. Nothing else means: Receive my spirit. 3. Where did Jesus receive Stephen's spirit? In what abode, in what heaven of heaven? Who can understand or explain it? Do you want to hear it in a few words? Listen to Christ himself: Father, I want them to be with me where I am. Being where Christ is, what thought can understand it? What words will be enough to explain it? Proclaim faith and do not expect a response from the tongue. When the gospel was read, you heard this: Where I am, there my servant will also be. If you use a Greek codex, you will find the word "deacon", which, translated into Latin, means "servant." In Greek it is said "deacon"; "deacon" in Greek and "servant" in Latin, as martyr and witness, apostle and envoy respectively. But we have become accustomed to using Greek terms instead of Latin ones. In fact, there are many codices in which we read like this: Where I am, there my deacon will also be. Consider that, as it is in truth, the text sounded like this: Where I am, there my deacon will also be. No wonder, therefore, his deacon said: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. You promised it; I have read and announced your Gospel: Where I am, there my deacon will also be. I was your day

quia hinc fuet accusatus, quod verba dixerat contra Deum et legem, ipsam legem illís exposuít, ut eius legis esset praedicator, cuius accusabatur esse vastator. Hoc et audimus et audistis: non sunt nostra fines necessaria, quia fines audistis. When we still lived in Caesarea of ​​Cappadocia, our homeland, our eldest brother covered our common mother with such serious and intolerable insults that he did not even hesitate to lay his hand on her. All of us children gathered there patiently suffered this, to the point of not saying a word to our brother in favor of our mother or asking him why he did that. But she, excited by the pangs of her womanly pain, determined to punish her son's outrage with a curse. After the rooster crowed, he hurried to the baptismal font to invoke the wrath of God on the aforementioned son. Then I don't know who, under the figure of our uncle, apparently the devil, came out to meet him and, anticipating it, asked him where he was going. She responded that she was going to curse her son for that intolerable affront. Then that enemy, as it was easy for him to find a seat in the woman's enraged heart, persuaded her to curse us all. Inflamed by such viperous advice, she lay down next to the sacred fountain, and on top of it, her hair loose and her breasts uncovered, she asked God, above all, that, banished from the homeland and wandering through strange lands, we would serve as a terrifying example for the entire human race. Immediately, maternal pleas become effective revenge, and instantly the same older brother in age and guilt began to tremble in his limbs as great as the one your holiness saw in me three days ago. In the space of a year, the same punishment befell us all, in the order in which we were born. The mother, seeing the frightful effectiveness of her curses, could no longer bear the consciousness of her evil.

Cum adhuc in patria nostra Caesarea Cappadociae moraremur, frater noster natu maior gravibus atque intolerandis communem matrem affecit iniuriis, in tantum ut ei etiam manus non dubitaret inferre. Quod nos omnes filii pariter congregan patienter tulimus, ut ne verbum quidem fratri nostro pro matre nostra, cur hoc faceret, dixerimus. Illa autem feminei doloris stimulis incitata, iniuriosum filium maledicendo puniré constituit. Cumque ad sacri Baptismatis fontem post gallorum cantus memorato filio suo iram Dei imprecatura properaret, tune ei nescio quis in patrui nostri similarityine, ut intellegitur, daemon oceurrit, et ab ea prior quo pergeret requisivit. Cui illa, ad maledicendum filio suo ob intolerabilem contumeliam se iré irrespondit. Tune autem ille inimicus, quoniam in mulieris corde insaniente locum facile invenire potuit, ut ómnibus malediceret persuasit. Illa autem vipereis inflammata consiliis, sacrum fontem provoluta corripuit, et sparsis crinibus nudatisque uberibus hoc a Deo potissimum postulavit, ut extorres patria et circumeuntes alienas terras, omne hominum genus nostro terreremus exemplo. Not bearing our disgrace, we all left there and, abandoning our common homeland, we dispersed to different places. Of the ten brothers that we are, the one who follows the first deserved to recover health in the memory of the glorious martyr Lorenzo, who has recently risen near Ravenna, as we have heard. I, the sixth of the brothers, accompanied by my sister, who is next in age to me, filled with the desire to regain my health, undertook the journey and appeared in any town and region where there were sacred places, in which God performed miracles. Not to mention other places celebrated by saints, on this pilgrimage I reached Ancona, a city in Italy, where God performs many miracles through the mediation of the most glorious martyr Stephen. But I could not achieve healing there precisely because divine Providence had reserved me for here. Nor did I pass by the African city of Uzala, where it is proclaimed that the blessed martyr Stephen frequently works wonders. However, three months ago, that is, on the same day as the Kalends of January, both I and my sister, who accompanies me and who is still a prey to the same evil, were warned by a vision that left no doubt. Topic: Why martyrs are celebrated. Place: Hippo, in memory of the twenty martyrs. Date: November 15, feast of the twenty martyrs of Hippo. Between the year 405 and 411.

1. On this solemn date of the martyrs I owe you my sermon. Help me the prayers of the martyrs to speak of their glory and to briefly present the justice of their cause. In these solemnities, the first thing your holiness must remember is that we must not think that something is granted to the martyrs for celebrating these festivities. They have no need of our festivities, because they enjoy heaven in the company of angels; But they enjoy us not if we honor them, but if we imitate them. The very act of honoring them is of benefit to us, not to them. But honoring them and not imitating them is nothing other than falsely flattering them. For this purpose, the Probatum est cor fidele mulieris has arranged these festivities. Ubi ergo tale miraculum fecit Deus peí Martyrem suum, non potuit ibi istos curare? And this is also what we are directing. Conversi ad Dominum, etc.

If then we are offered, for us to imitate, the example of Jesus Christ our Lord, who, being God, put on flesh precisely to indoctrinate men of mortal flesh and present to them an example, of which it is written: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example so that we may follow in his footsteps, here too he replicates human fragility: "How are Christ and I alike? Although he is flesh, he is, nevertheless, Word and flesh, for the Word became flesh to dwell among us; he took on the flesh, but did not leave the Word; he received what he was not without losing what he was. Indeed, God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself. "How are Christ and I alike?" To remove every excuse for fragility lacking faith, the martyrs have opened a paved path for us. It had to be paved with carved stone so that we could walk calmly on it. This was the work of the martyrs, who did it with their blood and their confessions. Topic: The behavior of the martyrs. Location: Hippo. Date: November 15, feast of the twenty holy martyrs. 1. The solemnity of the blessed martyrs has made this day more joyful for us. We rejoice because the martyrs went from the land of cultivation to the place of rest; but they did not deserve it by dancing, but by praying; not drinking, but fasting; not fighting, but tolerating. I think that their parents were full of sadness when they left for the torture, but they were happy and said: I have been happy with what they told me: "We will go to the house of the Lord." Do not cry, fathers, for what are our joys. If you do not want those whom you nourished to go to the fire, rather than prevent them, you must imitate them. They knew where they were going; but his parents, unfaithful, cried for no reason. Then, loving the children of their flesh, they wept; Then, already believing in God, they said: You turned my tears into joy, you tore my coat and girded me with joy. Topic: The cause of the martyr. Location: Unknown. Date: A feast of martyrs. In the years 405-411.

1. With the voice of the martyrs we have sung to God: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from that of evil people. It is the voice of the martyrs. Who will dare to say: JúzEt ille: «Quam ergo auctoritatem potestis habere, cum vos videatis supplicio subiacere?» Et Martyres said: "Auctoritatem Regis aeterni portamus, ideo auctoritatem mortalis hominis non curamus." Tune in carceribus missi, catenis onerati sunt. Quantum dictum est ab impiis: Ubi est Deus eorum (Ps 113,2)? Veniat Deus eorum, in quem crediderunt, et liberet eos de carceribus, eripiat eos a gladio, eripiat eos a bestiis. Omnia ista dicebant, sed in petra pósitos non deiciebant. lili saeviebant, sed ílli non timebant. Sciebant ubi eos dimittebant, et quo festínabant. Coronantur Martyres confessores, et remanserunt iudices deserters. Sic Deus vult unumquemque christianum provere, ut probatum velit cum Martyribus coronare.

1. Martyres a sceleratis discernit, non poena, sed causa.—Cantavimus Deo martyrum voce: ludica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (Ps 42,1). Martyrum vox est. Quis audeat dícere: ludica me.

game, oh God! But who has a good cause? The soul is tempted with promises and threats, it is softened by pleasure and tormented by pain: all this was overcome by Christ the undefeated martyrs. They defeated the world with their promises and threats. Neither pleasure dominated them nor torment terrified them. Gold purified in the crucible does not fear the fire of hell. Therefore, as if purified by the fire of tribulation, the blessed martyr calmly says: Judge me, O God! Judge how much good you find in me; you have given me what pleases you; Find it in me and judge me. The sweetness of the world has not dominated me, nor will the tribulation of the world separate me from you. Judge me and distinguish my cause from that of evil people. There are many who suffer tribulations; but, the penalty being identical, the cause is not. «Adulterers, malefactors, robbers and murderers, all criminals, suffer many evils; many evils, he says, I, your martyr, also suffer; but distinguish my cause from that of evil people, from that of robbers, murderers and criminals of all kinds. They may suffer the same as me, but not have the same cause. In the furnace, I am purified, they reduced to ashes. Heretics also suffer it, many times at their own hand, wanting to be considered martyrs.' But against them we have sung: Distinguish my cause from that of evil people. A martyr is not made by the punishment, but by the cause. Deus, nisi qui habet optimam causam? Promissis et minis tentatur anima, mulcetur illecebris, torquetur doloribus: omnia pro Christo victa sunt ab invictis martyribus. Victus est promittens mundus, victus est saeviens mundus. Non tenuit voluptas, non terruit cruciatus. Aurum in fornace purgatum ignem gehennae non timet. Ideo tanquam purgatus igne tribulationis beatissimus martyr securus dicit, ludica me, Deus. Quidquid in me inveneris bonum, judica. Donasti mihi quod tibi placeat; inveni in me, et judica me. Non me tenuit dulcedo saeculi, non me a te detorquet tribulaúo saeculi. ludica me, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (ib.). Multi patiuntur tribulationes; parem habent poenam, sed parem non ha[1451]bent causam. Multa mala patiuntur adulteri, Mula mala patiuntur malefici, Mula mala patiuntur latrones et homicídae, Mula mala patiuntur scelerati omnes, Mula mala, inquit, et ego martyr tuus patior: sed discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (ib.), latronum, homicidarum, scelestorum omnium.

Pati talia, qualia ego, possunt: habere talem causam non possunt. Ego in fornace purgor; illi cinerescunt. Et haeretici patiuntur, et plura a se ipsis; et volunt martyres dici. Sed contra illos cantavimus, Discerne causam meam de gente non sancta. Non facit martyrem poena, sed causa. See supplementary note 4: Grief and the bed p.776.

2. In the passion of the Lord there were three crosses; The punishment was identical, but not the cause. On the right was a thief, on the left another; In the middle was the judge, hanging from the cross between them, as if pronouncing a sentence in a court. He heard one say to him: Deliver yourself, if you are just; He heard the other correct him, saying: Don't you fear God? We suffer this for the evils we have committed, but this is just. Personally, he had a bad cause, but he distinguished the cause of the martyrs. What else does it mean: We suffer this for the evils we have committed, but this is just? Who can distinguish the cause of the martyrs from the cause of the wicked who suffer punishment? «This one, he said, is seen to be just; "We suffer because of ourselves, because of our evils." Mister; notices what he says to his fellow sufferer. Christ was hung like him, but not debased like him. Whoever hung recognized him as Lord. The same torment of the cross associated them; but the prize was not the same. What am I saying? «Do you give a reward to Christ, giver of all rewards? Lord, he said, remember me when you come to your kingdom. "I saw him hanging and crucified, and yet I hoped that he would reign." «Remember me, he said; but not now, but when you arrive at your kingdom. I have committed many evils, he confessed; I don't expect an immediate break. The torments suffered until your arrival are enough for me. Be tormented now; But when you come, forgive me. He postponed it, but Christ offered

paradise to those who did not ask for it. Remember me; but when? When you arrive at your kingdom. And the Lord: «Truly I tell you that today you will be with me in paradise. My disciples abandoned me, losing hope in me, while you recognized me on the cross; You did not despise me, finding me about to die, and you waited for me to reign: Today you will be with me in paradise. I'm not leaving you." The cause is different; is it worth it? Good, then, is this cry: judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from that of evil people. All of us who live in this world should strive to have a good cause, so that if something happens to us in it, we can get out of it with a good cause.

Ad dexteram unus latro, ad sinistram alter latro: in medio iudex, Inter both pendens in intersection, quasi pronuntías de tribunali, audívit unum dícentem, Libera te, si iustus es; audivit alterum parem suum corripientem et dicentem, Tu non times Deum? Nos pro malis nostris ista patimur; nam iste iustus est. Malam habebat causam, et discernebat martyrum causam. Quid est enim aliud, Nos pro malis nostris ista patimur; nam iste iustus est? (Luke 23:39). Quis causam discerneret martyrum a causa impiorum poenam patientium? Iste, inquit, iustus agnoscitur; nos pro nobis patimur, pro malis nostris patimur. Domine: vide quid dicat partner poenae suae. Christus pariter pendebat; sed non pariter vilescebat. Agnoscebatur Dominus a pendente. Unum erat crucis consortium; non erat unum praemium. What do I say? Das Christo praemium, qui dator est praemiorum? Domine, inquit, memento mei, cum veneris in regnum tuum (ib., 42). Pendentem videbat, crucifixum videbat; et regnaturum sperabat. Memento, inquit, mei, non moda, sed cum veneris in regnum tuum. Fine, inquit, mala feci, requiem celerem non mihi spero: sufficiant storm mea usque ad adventum tuum. Stubborn mode; cum veneris, tune mihi parce. Ule se differebat, sed Christus paradisum non petenti offerebat.

He went ahead, and many followed him. The road was very rough, but he made it smooth as he passed before the others. As he went ahead, the others were not afraid to follow him. He died, and this filled his disciples with terror. He resurrected, and took away their fear by granting them love. When Christ died, the disciples were frightened and thought that he had perished. See the grace of God in him when they followed him. The thief believed in him precisely when the disciples trembled with fear. A thief was nailed to the cross with him, and he believed in him so much that he said: Lord, think of me when you come to your kingdom. Who instructed him but who was hanging at his side? It was nailed to his side, but it lived in his heart. 2. In the same psalm in which we read: The death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord, it is also written what you heard: I said in my rapture: "Every man is a liar." What did we just say, brothers? Every man is a liar. According to that, were the martyrs also liars? If, on the contrary, the martyrs were truthful, how is it true that every man is a liar? The Scripture says it: Every man is a liar. If we say that the martyrs were truthful, we make the Scripture mendacious. And if Scripture is true in stating that every man is a liar, then the martyrs were liars. How then are we to show that both the Scripture and the martyrs are truthful? Weren't the martyrs men? And if they were men, how

Is it true that every man is a liar? To do? Shall I endeavor to show you that the Scripture is true, and that every man is a liar, and that the martyrs were truthful, because they died for the truth? Indeed, if they are martyrs, it is because they died for the truth. "Martyr" is a Greek term that in our language is equivalent to "witness." Therefore, if they were true witnesses, they told the truth, and by telling the truth they received the crown. If, on the other hand, they were false witnesses—far be it from us!—they did not go to the crown, but to torments, since it is written: A false witness will not go unpunished. Let us show, then, that they were truthful. They already show themselves this way by wanting to die for the truth. How then is the Scripture true, which says: Every man is a liar? Let us beseech our Lord Jesus Christ; He will solve this problem for us. What will be used to solve it for us? Of the gospel, of the text that we just talked about when it was read to you. 3. Martyr graece, Testis latine.—In isto autem psalmo, ubi diximus: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius, ibi scriptum est et quod audistis: Ego dixi in ecstasi mea, Omnis homo mendax (Ps 115,15.11). CAPUT II.—Quid dicimus, fratres? Omnis homo mendax. Ergo et martyres mendaces fuerunt? If autem truthful martyres fuerunt; Quomodo verum est, Omnis homo mendax? Scriptura dicit: Omnis homo mendax. Si dixerimus: Truthful werent martyres; Scripturam facimus mendacem. Si autem verum dixit Scriptura, quia omnis homo mendax; ergo mendacious martyres fuerunt. Quomodo ergo habemus ostendere et Scripturam veracem et martyres veraces? An forte martyres non fuerunt nomines?

Si autem fuent homines, quomodo verum est, Omnis homo mendax? Quid ergo faciemus? Laborabimus, ut ostendamus vobis quia et Scriptura vera est, et omnis homo mendax; et martyres veraces fuerunt, quia pro veritate mortui sunt? Ideo enim sunt martyres, quia pro veritate passi sunt. Martyr enim est verbum graecum, et latine Testis dicitur. Si ergo veri testes fuerunt, vera dixerunt; et vera saying crowns acceperunt. Si autem testes falsi fuerunt, quod absit, non ad coronas, sed ad poenas ierunt, quia scriptum est: Testis falsus non erit impunitus (Prov 19,5). Ergo ostendamus illos veraces. Iam ipsi se ostenderunt, quando pro veritate etiam mori voluerunt. Quomodo ergo verax est Scriptura, quae dicit: Omnis homo mendax? Rogemus Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum; et ipse nobis solvet istam quaestionem. Unde habet illam nobis solvere? Of the Gospel, quo modo loquebamur, quando vobis legebatur. CAPUT III.—3. Veraces martyres, quia in eis Spiritus Dei loquebatur.—Audistis enim, quando legebatur Evangelium, quia martyribus dicebat Dominus Iesus: Cum tradent vos, nolite cogitare quid loquamini, aut quid dicatis, dahitur enim vobis in illa hora quid loquamini. Non enim vos estis qui loquimini, sed Spiritus Patris vestri, qui loquitur in vobis (Mt 10,19.[1453]20). Quia si vos loquimini, mendacium dicitis, quia omnis homo mendax. Vidit ergo ipse Dominus, quia omnis homo mendax, et dedit martyribus Spiritum suum; ut non ipsi loquerentur,

who spoke, but his Spirit; so that they would not be liars, but truthful. See here how they were truthful: for it was not they who spoke, but his Spirit. And even in what I am telling you now, if I speak about mine, I speak a lie. If, on the contrary, what I tell you is from the Spirit of God, for that very reason it is true. You yourselves take advantage: you do not want to talk about your own, if you want to speak truth, so as not to remain in your condition as lying men, instead of being truthful children of God. 4. All heretics suffer even for falsehood, not for truth, since they lie against Christ himself. Whatever the pagans suffer, all the wicked, they suffer because of falsehood. Therefore, let no one be proud and glory in having suffered; show the truth first to your tongue. You show the pain, I look for the cause. You say: "I have suffered"; I ask why you have suffered; Well, if we look only at the sufferings, even thieves must be crowned. Does he dare to say: "I have suffered this and this"? Why not? Because the answer is: «You have suffered it to carry out your bad actions; That is why your suffering was bad: because beforehand your cause was bad. If having suffered is a reason for glory, even the devil can glory. See how much he suffers: his temples are destroyed everywhere, his idols are demolished everywhere, his priests fall and are possessed everywhere. Can he say: "I too am a martyr, since I suffer so much"? Consequently, the man of God must be chosen first.

Thus, then, the righteous will live in eternal memory and will not be afraid to hear anything evil. The judge of the living and the dead will arrive, as we read in the gospel. That will be a reality, since what we are seeing now did not exist when it was announced to us as the future. You are now seeing how the name of Christ is announced to all peoples, how men are converted to the only God, how idols and demons are abandoned, while their temples collapse and their images are shattered; All these things did not exist then, but they were announced and now we see them. In the same Scriptures in which what we now see is announced - such things were written when they were not seen, but their future existence was indicated - in those same Scriptures, I repeat, we read what has not yet come. In quibus ergo Litteris scripta sunt ista, quae iam videmus (tune autem scripta sunt, quando non videbantur, sed future promittebantur), in ipsis Litteris legimus quod nondum venit. Whoever does all this perishes in the company of the devil, since all of this is nothing more than devices of demons, not saving signs of angels. Therefore, he who despises all these practices, and if he is ever told: "If you do not do this, you will die," he answers: "It is better for me to die than to do that," lies on his bed and is headed for martyrdom. Lying in bed and fatigued by fever, although he cannot move, he is fighting. He does not move his limbs, but with the arms of faith he smothers the lion, of which the apostle Peter says: You do not know that your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. He described the devil as a roaring lion that prowls around and seeks to snatch or hurt some sheep from the sheepfold. He never gives up. He never, until the end, stops laying ambushes. If, then, our adversary does not sleep, our fight is daily. Without even seeing our adversary, we defeat him. Why don't we see him? Because we feel within us what he wants to defeat us with, and in that very sense we dominate him. You do not see the devil, your enemy, but you feel your greed in yourself. You do not see the devil, tu et propitio deo uincit et facit magnam uictoriam, nemine uídente, in corpore evena; pugnat corde, coronatur in corde sed ab illo qui uidet in corde — ecce ergo ut aliquid dicam: aegrotat forte aliquis uestrum. But the price of these deaths is the death of just one. How many deaths he bought by dying who, if he had not died, the grain of wheat would not have multiplied! You heard the words he said at the approach of his passion, that is, at the approach of our redemption: If the grain of wheat, fallen to the ground, does not die, it remains alone; If, however, it dies, it bears much fruit. In the tuam. Non uides diabolum inimicum tuum sed tristes iracundiam tuam. Vince quae intus sentiments et uincuntur qui insidiantur foris.
