Pretiosa mors Martyrum empta pretio mortis Christi.—Per tam gloriosa sanctorum martyrum gesta, quibus ubique floret Ecclesia, ipsis oculis nostris probamus quam verum sit quod cantavimus, quia pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15): quando et in conspectu nostro pretiosa est, et in conspectu eius, pro cuius nomine facta est. Sed pretium mortium istarum mors est unius. Quantas mortes emit unus moriens, qui si non moreretur, granum frumenti non multiplicaretur? Audistis verba eius cum appropinquaret passioni, id est, cum nostrae appropinquaret redemptioni: Nisi granum tritici cadens in terram mortuum fuerit, ipsum solum manet: si autem mortuum fuerit, multum

fructum affert (lo 12,24,25). Egit enim in cruz grande commercium; ibi solutus est saeculus pretii nostri: quando latus eius apertum est lancea percussoris, emanavit inde pretium totius orbis. Empti sunt fideles et martyres: sed martyrum fides [1455] probata est; testis est sanguis. Quod fllis impensum est, reddiderunt, et impleverunt quod ait sanctus Ioannes: Sicut Christus pro nobis animam suam posuit, sic et nos debenmus pro fratribus animas will put (1 lo 3,16). Et alibi dicitur: Ad mensam magnam sedisti, diligent consider quae apponuntur tibi, quoniam talia te oportet praeparare (Prov 23,1.2). Mensa magna est, ubi epulae sunt ipse dominus mensae. Nemo pascit convivas de se ipso: hoc facit Dominus Christus; ipse invitationtor, ipse cibus et potus. Agnoverunt ergo martyres quid comederent et biberent, ut talia redderent. 2. Martyres non ex se, sed ex Dei gratia Victors.—Sed unde talia redderent, nisi ille daret unde redderent, qui prior impendit? Unde et Psalmus, ubi scriptum cantavimus: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15), quid nobis commendat? Consideravit illie homo quanta accepit a Deo; circumspexit quanta muñera gratiae Omnipotentis qui eum creavit, qui perditum quaesivit, qui invento veniam dedit, qui pugnantem infirmis viribus iuvit, qui se periclitanti non subtraxit, qui vincentem coronavit, qui praemium se ipsum dedit: consideravit haec omnia, et exclamavit, et dixit: Quid retribuam Domino pro

to the Lord for all the goods he has returned to me? I didn't want to be ungrateful, I wanted to reciprocate, and I didn't have the means. He did not say: "What will I return to the Lord for all that he gave me," but rather, What will I return to the Lord for all the goods that he has returned to me. He did not give it, but gave it back. If he returned, it means that we had given him something. Indeed, we had given him our evil deeds, and he returned his goods to us; He returned goods to us instead of evils, although we returned evils for goods. So look for something to give back to him; He is in trouble because he cannot find a way to pay the debt. What will I return to the Lord for all the goods he returned to me? And as if he had found something to return to him, he said: I will receive the cup of salvation and I will call on the name of the Lord. What is this? With all certainty, he planned to give back, but he still thinks about receiving: I will receive the cup of salvation. What chalice is this? The chalice of passion, bitter and healthy; chalice that, if the doctor had not drunk it first, the patient would have feared even touching it. That is the chalice he speaks of. We recognize this chalice in the mouth of Christ by saying: May, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me. The sons of Zebedee claimed for themselves, through the mouth of their mother, the most privileged places, namely: that one should sit on the right and another on the left. He answered them: Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink? Are you looking for the top? You reach the mountain through the valley. Are you looking for the most resplendent place? Drink first the chalice of humility. Referring to that chalice, the martyrs said: I will receive the chalice of salvation and invoke

the name of the Lord. — Aren't you afraid of fainting along the way? "No," he said. - Because? —For I will call upon the name of the Lord.—How could the martyrs have conquered had he not conquered in them who said: Rejoice, for I have conquered the world? The emperor of heaven ruled his mind and his tongue, and through them he defeated the devil on earth, while crowning the martyrs in heaven. Oh blessed ones, who thus drank this chalice! For them the pain ended and they received the honors. Pay attention, then, beloved ones; With your eyes it is not possible, but with your mind and soul think and see that the death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord.

Give us the power who gave us the will. This made the martyrs burn; Burned with love for invisible things, they despised the visible. What did he love in himself who even despised himself so as not to lose himself? They were temples of God, and they felt that God lived in them, so they did not worship strange gods. They had heard, thirstily they had drunk, they had made it reach the intimate fibers of their hearts, and in a certain way they had made them flesh of their flesh, these words of the Lord: If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself. Deny, he said, yourself, take up your cross and follow me. I want to say something about this; Your attention scares me; send me your prayer. 2. What does it mean, I beg you: If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross and follow me? We understand what he means by the words: Take up your cross, that is, endure your tribulations; here, you are about to endure, suffer. Accept with patience, he said, everything you have to suffer for me. And follow me. Where to? Where we know he went after he was resurrected: he ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father. He has placed us there too. Meanwhile hope goes ahead, so that reality follows. How should hope go forward? Those who listen know it: “Let us lift up our hearts.” It only remains for us to find out—to the extent that the Lord helps us, to discuss; enter, if he opens for us; find out, if he grants it to us, and explain to you what he has been able to find, what it means: Niétem, qui tribuit voluntatem. In hoc enim martyres flagraverunt: invisibilium enim amore succensi visibilia contempsemnt. Quid amavit in se, qui contempsit et se, ne seguiret se? Templa enim Dei erant, et Deum verum in se habitare sentiebant; false ideo déos non colebant. Audierant, sitienter hauserant, medullisque intimis cordis tradiderant, sibique quodam moda invisceraverant quod Dominus dixit: If you want to come post me, neget semetipsum. Neget, inquit, semetipsum, et tollat ​​cruzem suam, et sequatur me (Mt 16:24). Hinc aliquid voló dicere, et terret me vestra intentio, iubet oratio. 2. Negare se quomodo debeat Christi discipulus.—Quid est, rogo vos, Si quis vult post me vinore, neget semetipsum, et tollat ​​cruzem suam, et sequatur me? Intellegimus quid est, Tollat ​​cruzem suam; sustineat tribulationem suam: tollat ​​enim est ferat, sufferat. Patienter, inquit, accipiat omnia quae patitur propter me. Et sequatur me. What?

geese How does someone who loves himself deny himself? This is reasoning, but human reasoning; A man asks me: "How does he who loves me deny himself?" But the Lord answers that man: "If you love yourself, deny yourself." In fact, by loving yourself, you lose yourself, and by denying yourself, you find yourself. He who loves, he says, his life, will lose it. He was sent by someone who knows what to send, because he knows how to advise; who knows how to instruct and knows how to repair who deigned to create. He who loves loses. It's a sad thing to lose what you love; But sometimes the farmer also loses what he sows. He throws the grain, scatters it, throws it and covers it with earth. What do you miss? He who thus despises it and loses it is a miser at harvest time. Winter and summer show what he did: the joy of the reaper shows you the purpose of the sower. Therefore, he who loves his life will lose it. Whoever seeks fruit from it, let him sow it. This means refusal; lest, by loving her perversely, he be lost. 3. There is no one who does not love himself; but we must seek right love and avoid perverse one. He who loves himself, abandoning God, and he who abandons God by loving himself, does not even remain in himself, but even goes out of himself. He is banished from his heart, despising the interior and loving the exterior. What have I said? Do not all those who do evil despise their conscience? Quid factum sit, hiems et aestas probavit; ostendit tibi gaudium metentis consilium seminantis. [1457] Ergo qui amat animam suam, perdet eam. Qui fructum in ea quaerit, seminet eam. Hoc est ergo neget se, ne perverse eam loving perdat se. 3. Amor sui perversus, verius est sui contemptus.

Vecuniae amor usque ad animae contemptum.—Nemo enim est qui non se amet; sed rectus amor est quaerendus, perversus cavendus. Quisquis enim dimisso Deo amaverit se, Deumque dimiserit amando se, non remanet nec in se, sed exit et a se. Exit exsul pectoris sui, containing inside, loving outside. What did you say? Omnes qui mala faciunt, nonne conscientiam suam contemnunt? Ponit autem modum iniquitati suae, quisquis erubuerit conscientiae suae. Ergo quia contempsit Deum ut amaret se, loving

what is not himself, he also despised himself. Go and listen to the Apostle, who provides testimony in favor of this interpretation. In recent times, he says, dangerous times will come. What are these dangerous times? There will be men who love themselves. Here is the beginning of evil. Let us see, then, if, by loving themselves, they remain, at least, within themselves; Let's see it, let's listen to what follows: There will be, he says, men who love themselves, lovers of money. Where are you who loved yourself? You are effectively out. Tell me, I beg you: "Are you perhaps the money?" Therefore, you who, abandoning God, loved yourself by loving money, you also abandoned yourself. First you abandoned yourself, then you lost yourself. The love of money was what caused you to get lost. For money you come to lie: The mouth that lies kills the soul. Behold, then, when you go after money, you have lost your soul. Bring the balance, but that of truth, not that of ambition; Bring it, I beg you, and put the money in one saucer and the soul in the other. It is you who weigh them, and, carried away by ambition, you fraudulently insert your fingers: you want the saucer containing the money to lower. Cease, do not weigh; you want to commit fraud against yourself; I see what you're doing. You want to put money before your soul; you want to lie for him and lose her. Get away, let God be the one who weighs; Despite him, he cannot deceive nor be deceived. See how heavy he is; See him weighing and listen to his ruling: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world? They are divine words, words

of those who weigh without deceiving; words of the one who announces and warns. You put the money in one part, and the soul in the other; Look where you put the money. He does not love him, he does not love him at harvest time. The other way means this: Don't love her so as not to lose her. Those who fear dying give the impression of loving their life. If the martyrs had loved their souls in this way, they would have lost them without a doubt. What good would it be to have a soul in this life and lose it for the future? What use would it be to have a soul on earth and lose it to heaven? And what does having it consist of? Have it for how long? What you have is gone; If you lose it, you find it in you. Behold, the martyrs possessed their souls; but how would they be martyrs if they had always preserved it? And if they had preserved it, would they have lived to this day? If by denying Christ they had preserved their souls in this life, would they not have already abandoned this life and most certainly lost their souls? But since they did not deny Christ, they passed from this world to the Father. They sought Christ by confessing Him and they achieved it by dying. Because of you we are led to death all day long. That is why the martyr is not made by the punishment, but by the cause. In the passion of the Lord, the cause distinguished the three crosses. He was crucified between two thieves; The criminals were nailed to one side and the other, and he was in the middle. And as if that stake were a court, he condemned the one who insulted him and crowned the one who confessed it. What will he do when he comes to judge if he could do so much when he was judged? Now, then, I could see the crosses. In fact, if one looked at punishment, Christ was like thieves. But if someone asks the cross why Christ was crucified, it will answer: "For you." Let the martyrs also tell him: "We too have died for you." He died for us, we for him. But he died for us to grant us a benefit; We die for him, but not to grant him any favors. That is why in both cases we are in the spotlight: what comes from him reaches us, and what we do for him returns to us. He is, in truth, of whom the soul says: I said to the Lord: "You are my God, because you do not need my goods." What does it mean you don't need my goods but "your gifts"? And how can the giver of all good need any good? 3. Nature gave us so that we existed; He gave us the soul so that we could live; He gave us the intelligence to understand; He gave us food to sustain mortal life; He gave us the light of heaven and the sources of earth.

But all these gifts are common to the good and the bad. If this gave to the bad, does it not reserve anything peculiar for the good? Yes, reserve it. And what is it? What the eye did not see, nor the ear hear, nor enter into the heart of man. If anything rose to the heart of man, it was because it was beneath him; That is why he ascended to the heart, because the heart to which he ascended is above. The heart ascended to what it reserves for the good. What God has in store for you is not something that has ascended to your heart, but rather what your heart has ascended to. Do not listen as if you were deaf to the words: "Let us lift up our hearts." No eye has seen it, no ear has heard it, nor has it entered into the heart of man; The eye did not see it, because it has no color; The ear did not hear it, because it is not a sound; nor did it ascend to the heart of man, because it is not an earthly thought. Understand it this way: Eye has not seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man what God has prepared for those who love him. 4. You may still ask me what that is. Those who attend the same theatrical show love each other, those who get drunk in taverns love each other, and those who are associated by a bad conscience love each other. Therefore, when Christ said: This is my commandment, that you love one another, he must have distinguished between love and love. So he did; listen. The evangelist John says the same thing in his letter: As Christ gave his life for us, so we must also give it up for our brothers. You are going to approach the table of the powerful lord; You faithful know well which table you are going to approach; Remember what the Scripture says: When you approach the table of the powerful, know that it is appropriate for you to prepare another like it. What is the table of the powerful to which you approach? The one in which he offers himself, not a table with food prepared according to culinary art; Christ shows you his table, that is, himself. Come to that table and get your fill. Be poor, and you will be satisfied. The poor will eat and be satisfied. Know that it is convenient for you to prepare another one just like it. So that you understand the phrase, listen to Juan, who explains it. Maybe you didn't know what it means: When you approach the table of the powerful, know that it is best for you to prepare another one just like it. Listen to the commentator: "As

Christ gave his life for us, so we too must prepare such things. What does this mean? Give your life for your brothers. 3. Being poor, you came to be satisfied yourself. What will you prepare a similar table with? Ask the same person who invited you, to have something to feed him. If he doesn't give it to you, you will have nothing to offer him. Do you even have a little love anymore? You must not attribute it to yourself: What do you have that you have not received? Do you already have a little love? Ask Him to increase it for you, to perfect it until you reach that greater table than which there is no other in this life: No one has greater love than he who gives his life for his friends. You approached being poor and you return rich; better, don't come back, because you will only be rich by staying in it. The martyrs received from him the fact that they had suffered for him; believe it, they received it from him. The father of the family gave them what they could feed him. We have him, let's ask him. And, if we are not worthy to receive anything, let us ask for it through his friends, who fed him with what he had given them. Let them pray for us, so that he may grant it to us too. Having more, we receive from heaven. Listen to John, his precursor: Man can receive nothing that is not given to him from heaven. Consequently, even what we have, we have received from heaven, and having more, we receive from heaven. 4. Such is the city that comes down from heaven; let us be such that we deserve to enter it. You just heard who's coming in

Quantum diligere invicem praecipimur.—Accessit [1462] adhuc Dominus, et docuit adhuc: tanquam diceremus ei, Et quomodo nos dilexisti, ut sciamus et nos quemadmodum nos diligere debenamus? Audite: Maiorem hac caritatem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat pro amicis suis (lo 15,13). Sic diligite invicem, ut unusquisque animam suam ponat pro ceteris. Hoc enim martyres fecerunt, quod et ipse Ioannes evangelista in Epístola sua dicit: Sicut Christus animam suam pro nobis posuit, sic et nos debenmus animas nostras pro fratribus donde (1 lo 3,16). Acceditis ad mensam potentis: nostis fideles ad quam mensam accessitis; recolite Scripturam dicentem: Cum accessis ad mensam potentis, scito quoniam oportet te talia praeparare (Prov 23:1). Ad quam mensam potentis accessis? Qui tibi exhibitat se ipsum, non mensam coquorum arte conditam: exhibitat tibi Christus suam mensam, scilicet semetipsum. Access ad hanc mensam, et saturare. This pauper, et saturaberis. Edent pauperes, et saturabuntur (Ps 21,27). Scito quoniam talia te oportet praeparare. Ut íntellegas, Ioannem expositorem attende. Forte enim nesciebas quid sit: Cum accessis ad mensam potentis, scito quoniam talia te oportet praeparare (Prov 23,1). Audi exhibitor: Sicut Christus animam suam

pro nobis posit, sic et nos debenmus talia praeparare. What is it, talia praeparare? Animas pro fratribus I will put (1 lo 3,16). 3. Caritas Dei donum.—Ut saturareris, pauper accessisti; where talia praeparabis? Ab ipso qui te invitation pete, ut habeas unde illum pascas. Nisi ipse tibi dederit, nihil habebis. Sed habes iam aliquid caritatis? Nec hoc tibi imputes: Quid enim habes quod non accepisti (1 Cor 4,7)? Have you aliquid caritatis? Pete ut augeat, pete ut perficiat, quousque pervenias ad illam mensam, qua maior in hac vita non est. Maiorem hac caritatem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat pro amicis suis (lo 15,13). Accessisti pauper, recedis dives: immo non recedis, sed manendo dives eris. Ab illo martyres acceperunt quod pro illo passi sunf. credit; ab illo acceperunt. Paterfamilias dedit illis unde illum pascerent. Ipsum habemus, ab ipso petamus. Et si accipere minus digni sumus, per amicos ipsius, qui eum de ipsius dono paverunt, petamus. Orent ipsi pro nobis, ut donet et nobis. Et ut plus habeamus, de cáelo accipimus. Ioannem audi praecursorem ipsius, Non potest homo accipere quidquam, nisi fuerit ei datum de cáelo (lo 3,27). Ergo et quod habemus, de cáelo accepimus; et ut plus habeamus, de cáelo accipimus. 4. Fornicatores non esse intraturos in caelestem civitatem.—Ipsa est civitas, quae de cáelo descendit: such simus, ut intremus in eam. Audistis enim quales intrent, quales non intrent. and who doesn't. Do not be like those who will not enter; above all, do not be fornicators. In fact, when the Scripture mentioned who will not enter, it also named the murderers, and you were not afraid; but when he named the fornicators, I heard the beating of the chest. I have heard it myself; I have heard and seen it; What I did not see in your rooms, I have seen in the noise you have caused, I have seen it in your chests when you hit them. Throw away the sin, because hitting the chest and continuing to do the same is nothing other than callousing the sin. My brothers, my children, be chaste, love chastity, embrace it, love purity, because God, author of the purity of his temple, who is you, seeks it; He expels the impure far from the temple. Be sufficient for your wives, since you want them to be content with you. You don't want her to do anything outside of you; Don't do it outside of it. You are the master, she is the servant; but God made you both. The Scripture says: Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him her lord. That's how it is; the bishop signed those acts ': your women are your servants; You are masters of your women. But, when it comes to the act in which the different sexes unite with each other, the woman does not have power over her body, but the man does. You were happy, you stood proud and you boasted. «The Apostle spoke well, with complete reason he said that vessel of choice: a woman does not have power over her body, but a man. I am the owner." You just applauded him; listen to what follows; listen

what you don't want to hear, and I beg you to do it. What is this about? Listen: Likewise, the man, that owner; Likewise, the man does not have power over his body, but the woman does. Listen to this with pleasure. Your vice is taken away, not your authority; You are forbidden to commit adultery, a woman is not lifted above you. You are a man, prove it; “male” (vir) comes from “virtue,” or “virtue” from “male.” Do you then have virtue? Voluptuousness conquers. The man, he said, is the head of the woman. If you are the head, guide her and let her follow you; But pay attention to where you take it. You are the head: guide it where it follows you. Don't go where you don't want her to follow you. Don't fall off the cliff, try to go straight. This is how you must prepare to enter that newly married woman, beautified and adorned for her husband not with jewels, but with virtues. If you enter being chaste, holy and good, you will also be members of that new bride, the blessed and glorious heavenly Jerusalem.

The martyrs are sure of possessing God
SERMON Topic: to God.
The martyrs are sure to possess
Location: Unknown. Date: A feast of martyrs. Perhaps August 6, feast of Saint Sixtus I I.

1. This is the cry of all good faithful Christians and, above all, of the glorious martyrs: If God is with us, who can be against us? The world raged against them, the people plotted vain plots and the princes made alliances; They invented new tortures and cruelty managed to find incredible punishments. They were covered with insults, they were accused of false crimes, locked up in unbearable prisons, their bodies were torn with hooks, they perished by the sword, they were thrown to wild beasts, they were handed over to the fire, and they were still called the martyrs of Christ. If God is with us, who can be against us? The whole world is against you, and you say: Who is against us? They answer you: "And what is the whole world if we die for the one who made the world?" Say, say it; Let us listen to them, let us say it with them: If God is with us, who can be against us? They can mistreat us, they can curse us, slander us, fill us with apparent affronts; can, finally, not only make

1. Martyrum securitas sub praesidio Dei.—Omnium quidem bonorum fidelium Christianorum, máxime tamen gloriosorum martyrum est vox ista: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? (Rom 8:31). Fremebat mundus adversus eos, populi meditabantur inania, principes conveniebant in unum (cf. Ps 2,1.2): excogitabantur novi cruciatus, et poenas incredibiles inveniebat ingenious crudelitas. Obruebantur opprobriis, falsis arguebantur criminibus, custodiis intolerabilibus includebantur, ungulis exarabantur, ferro perimebantur, bestiis subrigebantur, ignibus cremabantur, et dice[1468]bant martyres Christi: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Totus mundus contra vos, et dicitis: Quis contra nos? Respondent tibi: Et quis est totus mundus, quando pro eo nos morimur, per quem factus est mundus? Dicant, dicant, audiamus, simul dicamus: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Saevire possunt, maledicere possunt, calumnian possunt, falsis opprobriis agitare possunt, postremo possunt corpus non solum

let the body perish, but also tear it to pieces; but what else can they do? Behold, God is my helper, and the Lord who receives my soul. —Tell me, blessed martyr: they are tearing your body to pieces, and you claim that none of this concerns you? —I said it. -As? Tell us why. —Because the Lord is the one who receives my soul. My body will be restored through my soul. Not a hair will perish, and will my head perish? Not a hair of mine will perish. —But your body is torn to pieces by dogs. —What about me? Although my body is destroyed by dogs, it will be resurrected by the Lord. The world kills my body, but the Lord is the one who receives my soul. And if the Lord is the one who receives my soul, what harm does it harm me if the world kills my body? What have I lost? What have they taken from me? If the Lord receives my soul, he will also restore my body. If my enemy should tear all my members in pieces, what can I lack, if the Lord counts all my hairs? Christ, exhorting his martyrs not to fear the persecuting enemies, said: All your hairs are numbered. Am I going to fear, then, that my limbs will suffer damage if I have insured up to the number of my hairs?—Let us say, then, let us say with faith, let us say with hope and with burning charity: If God is for us, who can be against us? 2. You have the king against you, and you say: Who can against us? You have the entire people against you, and do you say: Whoever conperimere, sed etiam laniare; et quid facient? Ecce enim Deus auxiliator mihi est, et Dominus susceptor est animae rneae (Ps 53,6). Dec mihi, beate martyr; corpus tuum laniatur, et tu dicis: Nihíl ad me pertinet? Etiam dixi. Quare? dic nobis quare. Quia Dominus susceptor est animae meae. Corpus meum per animam meam restauratur. Capillus meus non perit, et caput perit? Pilus meus non perit. Sed a canibus corpus tuum laceratur. Et quid ad me? Etsi a canibus corpus meum laceratur, sed a Domino suscitatur. Mundus interfector est corporis mei, sed Dominus susceptor est animae meae. Et quid mihi obest, cum sit Dominus susceptor animae meae, quod mundus interfector est corporis mei? What did I lose? What's up, friend? Quando Dominus susceptor est animae meae, erit et restitutor corporis mei. Quid mihi deerit, si membra mea dilaceret inimicus, quando capillos meos dinumerat Deus? Exhortans martyres suos Christus, ne ab inimicis persecutoribus aliquid formidarent, Capilli, inquit, vestri omnes numerati sunt (Luke 12:7).

Timebo ergo de damno membrorum, quando securitatem accepi de numero capillorum? Ergo dicamus, dicamus ex fide, dicamus in spe, dicamus flagrantissima caritate: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? 2. after us? How do you prove it, oh glorious martyr? How do you prove to me what you say: If God is with us, who can be against us? It is evident that, if God is with you, one can ask: "Who can be against you?" But you have to prove to me that God is with you. I'm not going to try it? See, I teach you: Who did not spare his own son, but gave him up for us all. You heard the continuation of the text when it was read to the Apostle. After having said: If God is with us, who can be against us?, as if it were said to him: "Prove that God is with you," he immediately adduced a great proof, he brought to the stand the Martyr of martyrs, the Witness of witnesses, that is, the Son whom the Father did not forgive, but handed him over for all of us. From there, the Apostle proved that he had spoken the truth: If God is with us, who can be against us? God, who did not spare even his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how can he not give us all things with him? If with him he gave us all things, he also gave us himself. Will the roars of the world terrify me, who has been given the architect of the world? Let us rejoice that Christ has been given to us and let us not fear any enemy of Christ in this world. See who it is that has been given to us: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Such is Christ, the only begotten Son of God, coeternal with him who begat him. By her all things were made. How could he not give us all the things made by him,

If he gave himself to us, by whom was it all made? And so that you may know that it is he himself: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Desire and ask that the life of Christ be granted to you, and until you reach it, have the death of Christ as a guarantee. By promising us that he would live with us, he could not offer us a better guarantee than dying for us. «I have suffered, he said, your evils; "Am I not going to give you my goods in exchange?" He made the promise, left a deposit and gave a guarantee, and you still hesitate to believe? He made the promise when he walked here in the company of men; He left the guarantee in the written gospel. Before its guarantee you say every day: "Amen" 1. You have received the guarantee, every day it is dispensed to you; Do not lose hope, you who receive life from that guarantee. 3. Or is it an insult to the only begotten Son when it is said that he has been given to us to be our future possession? It certainly must be. If someone gave you today a leafy and fertile farm where you would always like to live because of its luxuriance and where you could easily sustain yourself because of its fertility, would you not accept the gift and thank the person who gave it to you? We are to remain in Christ. How can he not be our possession, in whom we will remain and from whom we will live? Let Scripture also say so so as not to leave the impression that, relying on our conjectures, we have said something against the word of God. probas, or glorified martyr; unde mihi probas quod dicis, Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Manifestum est enim quia si Deus pro vobis, quis contra vos? Be proba quia Deus pro vobis. Non ergo probo? Ecce twelve: Qui Filio proprio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum (Rom 8:32). Hoc quod sequitur, cum Apostolus legeretur, audistis. Qui etiam filio proprio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit illum. Quomodo non et cum illo omnia nobis donavit (ib., 8,31-32)? Quando cum illo omnia donavit nobis, et ipsum donavit nobis. Numquid terret me fremitus mundi, cui donatus est artifex mundi? Christum nobis donatum esse gaudeamus, et millos Christi inimicos in hoc saeculo timeamus. per ipsum facta sunt, quando nobis donatus est ipse, per quem omnia facta sunt? Et ut sciatis quia ipse est: Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,1.3.14). Christus ipse futurus possessio nostra.—An forte iniuria fit unigénito Filio, cum dicitur quod donatus est nobis, tanquam ipse futurus sit nostra possessio? Plan ipse futurus est. after us? The Lord, he said, is the portion of my inheritance. He did not say: "O Lord, what will you give me as an inheritance?" Anything you give me is vile. This is to love God freely, to wait for God at the hands of God, to hasten to be filled with God and to be satisfied with him. He, indeed, is enough for you; outside of it, nothing else is. He will be for us everything that we here desire outside of him and for which we frequently offend him. When God is all in all, he will be all to us. You sin against God to eat, to dress, to live, to receive honors. When will I finish mentioning everything? Do not sin against God for these things. Do you sin against God because of food? God will be your eternal food. Because of the dress? God has to clothe you with immortality. Because of honors? God will be your honor. For the love of temporary life? God will be eternal life for you. Don't sin against him for anything. You must love him freely, since he can satisfy you instead of all things. quia si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Hoc est Deum gratis amare, de Deo Deum sperare, de Deo properare impleri, de ipso satiari. Ipse enim sufficit tibí; praeter illum nihil sufficit tibí. Propter cibum peccas in Deum? cibus tibí aeternus erit Deus. Propter vestem peccas in Deum? immortalitate te vestiturus est Deus.

Topic: The meaning of martyrdom. Location: Unknown. Date: A feast of martyrs. In the years 410-412. 1. When it comes to the feast of the holy martyrs, what can we talk about better than their glory? Help us the Lord of martyrs, since he is their crown. Recently we heard the blessed apostle Paul proclaiming the cry of the martyrs: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Such is the cry of the martyrs. The tribulation? The anguish? The chase? Hunger? The nudity? The dangers? The sword? For it is written: "For your sake we are mortified all day long and considered like sheep to be slaughtered." But in all these things we conquer through him who loved us. This is the cry of the martyrs: to endure everything, not to boast about themselves and to love those who are glorified in their own, so that whoever glorifies may glorify himself in the Lord. They also knew what we recently sang: Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you righteous. If the righteous rejoice in the Lord, the unrighteous only know how to rejoice in the world. But this is the first

CAPUT I.—1. Sanctorum martyrum voices. Delectationes et dolors vicerunt martyres.—Quoniam dies sanctorum martyrum est, unde potius aliquid delectet nos dicere, nisi de gloria ipsorum? Adiuvet nos Dominus martyrum, quia ipse est corona eorum. Voce martyrum audimus paulo ante beatum apostolum Paulum praedicantem: Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? Ista vox est martyrum: Tribulatio? still anguish? did he persecute? are you famous? still naked? an periculum? an gladius? Sicut scriptum est: Propter te morte afficimur tota die, deputati sumus ut oves occisionis. Be in his omnibus superamus per eum qui dilexit nos (Rom 8:35-37). Haec est vox martyrum, omnia tolerare, et de se nihil praesumere, illum diligere qui glorificatur in suis: ut qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur (1 Cor 1:31). Noveránt et illud quod nos cantavimus paulo ante: Laetamini in Domino, et exsultate, iusti (Ps 31,11). Si iusti in Domino laetantur, iniustí non noverunt laetari nisi in saeculo. Sed ipsa est prima acies
The meaning of martyrdom

mer army that must be defeated: first you must defeat pleasure and then pain. How can he overcome the cruelty of the world who is unable to overcome its flattery? The love of goods
Theme: The love of incorruptible goods. Location: Outside Hippo. Date: Feast of a martyr. Between the year 405 and 411.

1. * As the day of the birth of the blessed martyr that the Lord wanted me to celebrate with you has shone for us, I am going to speak something—whatever he grants me—about the glory and patience of the martyrs. Glory was despised and patience tested. Glory remained hidden in the heavens, patience was exercised on earth. He who does not feel horror at his patience will reach glory. It is considered a misery to suffer hardness and roughness in the flesh, because in reality it is a bothersome thing. If it were not a bothersome thing for men, it would not bring glory to the martyrs. 2. Imagine before your eyes two as persons: one represents concupiscence and the other charity. I call concupiscence the love of sin, since sometimes it is also called concupiscence even though it has good as its object. In the same way, I call charity the love of a righteous life, since sometimes charity is also spoken of in reference to something evil. SERMO

That's why I wanted to define the terms. The faithful desire the kingdom of heaven. Thieves also call each other dear, but there is no charity in those who are united by a bad conscience, but in those whom wisdom delights in common. 3. Reflect, then, and distinguish how many evils many anxious men suffer and how hard are the things they endure for what they desire, to the point of seeming unbearable to those who do not have such desires. Love makes them strong. But the love of evil is called concupiscence, and the love of good is called charity. There are many things that ambitious people love, and sometimes so diverse that they even seem to oppose each other. Greed collects money, lust scatters it; the former appears as a beggar and the latter as a spendthrift; And what things are more contrary to each other like gathering and scattering? But by the command of greed, how many things are done, how many hardness and harshness they endure, enduring the pain... the pleasure that you love! And sometimes because of the same madness of love one loves her clumsily and because of her many things are endured with strength. 4. It is not strange, then, dearly beloved, that charity also has the strength of its love. The martyrs possessed it, and thanks to it they endured all the hardships they endured. They loved what they did not see, but they had the certainty of faith and they saw it with their hearts, as much as a man carrying his flesh can see it. Does not this flesh truly have its beauty? [752] Et quid prodest cum propter pecuniam perieris? Et tu peris et illam non inuenis. Immo, si quam habeas, pereundo hic dimittis. Transís; tum uenit alius amator eius. Quanti illam lovers reliquerunt, et amando et transeundo perierunt. Quamquam enim in imagine ambulet homo, tamen uane conturbatur (Ps 38,7). Miserandum

compassion, since, although he walks in the image, certainly of God, he toils uselessly: He treasures, and does not know for whom. Why do you toil except to hoard? Treasure, yes, but where wisdom commanded you, not where greed remains. 8. Regarding money, the Lord gave you advice on how not to lose what you have acquired. Make friends, he said, with the money of iniquity, so that they may receive you into eternal mansions. The martyrs, who had a good cause and endured much for the love of God, were received by some when they were hungry; clothed, when they were naked, and welcomed, when they were pilgrims. There is, indeed, a service for those who are in tribulation. They made friends with the money of iniquity. So, also about money, the Lord gave good advice, in case anyone wants to listen to it. Undoubtedly, if you love your money, you must be careful not to lose it. If it certainly perished for them, it perishes for you. It goes away to you, it comes to someone else. Act, then, so that you do not lose it. And, since he leaves first, store him up in heaven, where the thief does not enter nor the moth corrupt him. It is a fortified place; Why do you hesitate to take him there? Send ahead what you have to reach the place where you sent it. Buy yourself something that cannot perish. You know, dearly beloved, what determination those greedy for money make when they see that they already have a certain amount of currency. What do they say? «The coin is round, it rolls, it is lost; "You have to tie it with the purchase of some possession." And they want to hold their money buying

a farm Lo and behold, they have already bought the farm and will own that farm. Will the farm possess them forever? But even they will have nowhere to emigrate without delay after a short time. You can't hold your soul where you held your money. The time will come when your soul is asked for. Whose item did you buy? Therefore, neither will you possess the property nor will the property possess you, except as regards the body, if you die and are buried therein. Then something strange will happen: she will have you, not you her. 9. The Lord, therefore, gives good and golden advice by saying: —Take it where you will not lose it. •—What advice is this! “This way I won't see my money,” you say. —You'll see it later. —You will not see what you sent, because you have lent it with interest. You give one amount and you will receive another. Omnipotent is the one to whom you lent it. He receives small things and returns large things; He receives little and will give back a lot. This is the land he created for you: you throw in a few grains and then fill the granaries. If such is the earth that He created for you, what will He who made heaven and earth have in store for you, who sow good works? 10. But I am speaking for deaf ambitious people, whether for lascivious lovers of beautiful bodies, or for misers who gather and hoard money on earth. I speak to the deaf; They don't hear me. Heal them, Lord, so that they may hear. Nothing is impossible for you. For you there is no incurable disease, because you are a great doctor, especially because you showed us your love in advance.

Aliquid inde tibi eme quod perire non possit. Nostis, carissimi, quo consilio agant cupidi pecuniae quando uident se aliquid nummorum habere. What did you say? "Rotunda estres, uoluitur, perit, aliqua possessionis emptione ligada est." Et uolunt

Vbi ligasti pecuniam tuam, ligare ibi non potes animam tuam. Veniet enim tempus quando reposcetur a te anima (402) tua. Quod emisti, cuius erit? Ergo nec uillam habebis, nec uilla te habebit, nisi forte secundum corpus ibi fueris mortuus sepultas. Fit enim tune mirum aliquid: ipsa te habebit, tu illam non habebis. 9. Bonum ergo domini consilium et aureum da tur cui dicitur: «Migra ubi non perdas» — «Quale consilium datur! "Sed non uidebo," he inquired. Post uidebis. Sed hoc quod misisti non uidebis. In usuram enim dedisti. Aliud dedisti, aliud tibi reddetur. Omnipotens est quem fenerare uoluisti. Accipit parua, sed [753] dat magna. Accipit pauca, reddet plurima. Sed cupidis surdis loquimur, siue lasciuis amantibus pulchra corpora et auaris congregantibus et thesaurizantibus in terra pecuniam. Surdis loquimur, non nos audiunt. Domine, sanentur ut audiant. Impossible tibi nihil est. Nullus tibi est insanabilis morbus, quia magnus es mediais, máxime quia ostendisti in nos praecedentem caritatem tuam, quia proprio

towards us by not forgiving your own Son and handing him over to all of us. How could you not have given us everything with him! «Open your jaws, miser; "Despise the little now, because you will have much." He had conquered, crushed and trampled greed who said: As someone who has nothing and possesses everything. 11. To many lascivious and greedy people, the martyrs of Christ seemed crazy when they suffered so many torments for the name of Christ and always confessed it truthfully. They were urged to deny it: they confessed it, they died, they were burned and thrown to wild beasts; In the light of day they suffered horrible things, but in secret they were crowned. If they had sought earthly things, what can be added to this glory that makes us celebrate their births? Many strong men went crazy for glory and said that blood had to be shed for their country 3, and they did not hesitate to spill it, knowing that this life is temporary, but that they had, at least, immortal glory left. What glory of theirs admits of comparison with the glory of the martyrs? Limiting ourselves to the glory of this land, limiting ourselves to human glory, what general could find the glory that the fisherman found? In Rome there are the tombs of brave men who died for their country. Which of those tombs has the emperor deigned to enter? You see that, if earthly glory were to be desired, not even those who sought their honor only among the angels have been deprived of it. We see the glory they enjoy on earth, and we are filled with amazement. What would we experience if we saw it in heaven? Filio tuo non pepercisti, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidisti illum. Quomodo non et cum illo nobis omnia donasti. — Extend your jaws, auare, iam contempne pauca, habebis fines. Vicerat, obtriuerat, calcauerat cupiditatem qui dicebat: Tamquam nihil habentes et omnia possidentes (2 Cor 6,10). 11. Multis ergo lasciuis et auaris martyres sancti insanire uisí sunt quando pro Christi nomine tanta patiebantur et eum ueraciter semper confitebantur. Vt denialent urgebantur; confessi, occisi, incensi, bestiis (403) subrecti in aperto horrida patiebantur; in occulto ineffabiliter coronabantur. Si terrena ab eis quaererentur, quid huíc gloriae addi potest qua eorum natalicia celebrantur. Insanierunt pro glory multi uiri fortes, et pro patria sanguinem fudendum esse dixerunt, nec fundere dubitauerunt, scientes transiré quidem ipsam uitam sed remanere uel immortalem in illis gloriam.

Quae illorum gloria gloriae martyrum comparatur? Quis potuit inuenire in gloria huius terrae, quis potuit inuenire in gloria humanorum rerum, quis potuit inuenire dictator quod potuit inuenire piscator? Virorum fortium qui pro patria perierunt sepulchra sunt Romae. Ad cuius sepulchrum intrare dignitus est imperator? Ecce si terrena gloria fuet concupiscenda, nec ipsa fraudati sunt qui honorem tantum Inter angelos quaesierunt. Videmus eorum glorias in terrís et stupemus. Crux

What amazement would not take hold of us if we saw, full of glory among the angels, the martyrs whose birth we see the people celebrating? 12. Truly, my brothers, seek the invisible things of the martyrs. Love what they loved. Even if you do not have to endure what they endured, prepare your mind for it. First of all, to the extent that you can, choose the cause. In fact, leaving aside the cause, do not martyrs suffer the same thing that thieves, adulterers, slanderers and sacrilegists have often suffered? If you look at the penalties, they are the same; If you look at the causes, they are very far from each other. What things are closer and more similar, without however approaching each other, than the three crosses, one of the Lord and two of the thieves? There were three; They were all crosses, they were all in the same place; All those bodies hung from them, but the cause distinguished them all. In the middle was the savior; on both sides, the prisoners. That cross was a court; the Savior hung on her and distinguished; He judged, he was hanging and he judged those who were hanging with him. Of those two prisoners, one deserved the torture and another the reward. Why did the other deserve the prize? Because, being on the cross, he changed his cause. Hanging on the cross, he believed in long-term realities; In his heart he wanted to have them when the Lord arrived in his kingdom. But what did the Lord answer him when he said to him: Lord, remember me when you come to your kingdom, as if I had confessed to him: «I know my cause, I know what I deserve, I must be tormented pateremur si ín cáelo uideremus? Quantum nos stupor admirationis apprehenderet si uideremus martyres Inter angelos gloriantes, quorum natalicia uidemus populos celebrants? 12. Verum, inuisibilia martyrum quaerite, fratres mei. Quod amauerunt amate. Quod sustinuerunt, etsi non sustinueritis, ad sustinendum courage stop. Causam primitus, quantum potestis, eligite. Nam, non elect causa, nonne talia patiuntur martyres qualia passi sunt saepe latrones, qualia adulteri, qualia malefici, qualia quique sacrilege? Si poenas [754] attendas, pares sunt, si causa plurimas, longe illi ab illis sunt. (404) Quid tam habens proximitatem et similarityinem, et nihil tamen propinquitatem, quam tres cruzes: una domini et duae latronum? Three weret, omnes crosses weret, omnes in uno loco wast, omnia corpora illa ligno pendebant, sed causa omnes dirimebat. In middle saluator; ex utroque latere rei.

Crux illa tribunal Fuit: pendebat et discernebat; iudicatus pendebat et pendentes iudicabat. Ex illis duobus reis unus meruit supplicium, alter praemium. Quare meruit alter praemium? Quia causam in intersection immutauit. Pendens credit in longinquas emissis; quando uenisset dominus in regnum suum, tune in eius animo (405) haberi uoluit. Today you will be with me in paradise. You wait for me to come, but I never fail; I am everywhere and there I go; But today you will be with me in paradise, because there where you will be happy you cannot be happy without me. Thus, all the souls of the blessed, although they have not yet recovered their bodies, live happily with Christ and only from Christ does happiness come to them. They loved him, they felt affection for him; In him they possessed justice, in him wisdom, in him knowledge, in him the hidden treasures of wisdom and science. How many things they despised here with their passion! They didn't want to be rich. What doesn't the poor have, if he has God? 13. Love what is good, my brothers; There is nothing more beautiful, even if it is only seen with the eyes of the heart. I speak to you. See that everything you see through the eyes of the flesh is beautiful: the sky, the earth, the sea and everything in them, the stars that shine in the sky, the sun that fills the day, the moon that moderates the night, the birds, the fish, the animals that walk, men themselves, made, among other things, in the image of God, who praise creation, who love creation, but only if they love the creator. Whatever you love and that leads you to forget God, no one made it but God. Whatever, I repeat, that you love with forgetfulness of God, no one made it but God. If it weren't something beautiful, you wouldn't love it. and from where

Would beauty have come to her if she had not been created by him who is invisibly beautiful? You love gold; God created it. You love beautiful bodies and flesh: God created them. You love lush fields: God created them. You love this light as if it were a big deal: God created it. If you neglect him because of what God created, I beseech you, also love God himself. He is as lovable as he who created everything you love is lovable. Love this, but in a way that you love him more. I don't want you to not love anything, but I want you to order your love 4. Put heavenly goods before earthly ones, the immortal ones over the mortal ones, the eternal ones over the temporal ones. Put before the Lord 8 all of them, not praising him, but loving him. Putting Him first in praise is easy. Temptation comes: that's when I ask you if you put first in your love what you put first in your praise. If you are asked: "Which is better: money or wisdom, money or justice and, finally, money or God?", you do not hesitate to answer: wisdom, justice, God. Don't hesitate to choose what you haven't hesitated to answer. "Which is better: justice or money?" Like children when asked a question at school, you all shout obstinately: "Justice." I know you all say it; I hear your thoughts: justice is better. But temptation will come. It presents you with money on one side. Temptation tells you, “You can get this money; If you commit fraud, you get it.” But justice replies: «What do you choose? It's time to prove what you said." Questioned recently, you preferred justice to money; but

Now, with both things present, money on one side and justice on the other, as if ashamed, you close your eyes against justice and reach out your hand to the money. Ungrateful, foolish; When, when asked about me, you answered that you preferred justice to money, you gave testimony against yourself. Does God need another witness to declare you convicted? In praise you preferred justice; in love, money. Don't you see who you wanted to be on? From what must perish. Without a doubt, money must perish, because the world will pass away, and all its lust. Topic: The combat of martyrdom. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of martyrs.

1. When the holy martyrs suffer evils here, they put their hope in the Lord. In fact, they are saved in hope: they are moving towards what was promised, but they do not yet possess it. Since they waited in the shadow of your wings to bravely endure the evils of the world, what will you give them? They will be drunk with the abundance of your house. If I had more to say, I would autem, positis duabus: hinc pecunia inde iustitía, tamquam erubescens claudis oculos contra iustitiam, manum porrigis ad pecuniam. Ingrate, stulte, quando a me interrogatus iustitiam pecuniae praetulisti, contra temetipsum testimonium dixisti. Numquid quaerit deus alium testem postquam te conuincas. In laudando praelata est iustitia, in choosing praelata est pecunia. Non uides de cuius part uoluisti? From peritura periturae. Pecunia quippe sine dubio peritura est quia et mundus transiet et otnnis concupiscentia eius (1 lo 2,17). Choose iustitiam quia qui fecerit uoluntatem dei manet in aeternum, sicut ipse manet in aeternum (1 lo 2,17; Is 40,8). SERMO

1. ^Martyres sancti, cum hic mala patiuntur, sperant in domino. Spe enim salui facti sunt: ad promissa ambulant, nondum datum tenent. Quia ergo sub tegmine alarum sperabant ut mala saeculi fortiter patienterque sustineant, quid eis dabis? Inebriabuntur ab ubertate domus (4) tuae (Ps 35.9). Si haberet plus quod diceret, diceret. Quid enim djceret?

I would say. What could I say? "Will they drink?" A minimal amount can be drunk. What could I say? “Will they be satisfied?” The sober will also be satisfied. They drink until they get drunk. With that intoxication everything that happened is forgotten. Oh holy intoxication! I wish we were all intoxicated with this intoxication! 2. See what intoxication those who get drunk in the places of the martyrs desire. Those who were persecuted with stones must achieve the merits of the martyrs because they do not sacrifice the members of Christ for the amusement of demons, and think that they please the martyrs, when those they please are the unclean spirits. How much we talk about this! Fix your gaze on those in whose memories you become intoxicated; If they had loved these things, they would not have been martyrs. 3. Do not think, dear brothers, that you cannot achieve the merits of the martyrs because there are no persecutions like those in which they obtained their crown. Now there are no persecutions, but there is never a shortage of temptations. Certainly, my brothers, there are Christian men among those sons of men who wait in the shadow of the wings of God. When the time of hope has passed and the time of joy has arrived, they will be drunk with the abundance of his house and he will give them to drink from the stream of his delights. What will he give them to drink? What will they get drunk with? Listen with what. Because in you is the source of life. The intoxication of living is living without end. That intoxication is indigestible; Nobody digests it and “Bibent”? Bibitur et parum. What do you say? "Saturabuntur"? Saturabuntur et sobrii. Tantum bibent ut inebrientur. Illa enim ebrietate mala omnia praeterita obliuiscuntur. O sancta drunk! Vellem in hac ebrietate omnes essemus ebriosi. 2. Ecce qualem ebrietatem desiderant qui se in locis martyrum inebriant, et quos illi persecuti sunt lapidibus, persequuntur calicibus; insuper etiam saltant et membra Christi ad ludendum daemoníbus donant, et putant se pleasureré martyríbus dum placent inmundis spiritibus. How much is this dicimus? Ipsos certe adtendant ad quorum memorias se inebriant: si ista dilexissent, martyres non essent. 3. Nolite putare ergo, dilectissimi fratres, non uos posse habere merita martyrum quia persecutíones non sunt, quales fuerunt illis temporibus quando martyres coronad sunt. Non sunt moda persecutíones, sed numquam cessant temptationes. Prorsus, fratres mei, sunt nomines christiani de illis filiis hominum qui sub tegmine alarum dei sperant.

Et cum transierit tempus spei, et uenerit gaudium rei, inebriabuntur ab ubertate domus eius et torrente uoluptatis suae potabit eos. Where [778] potabit? Unde inebriabuntur? Audi unde. Quoniam apud te est fons vitae (Ps 35,10). Ebrietas uitae est sine fine uiuere. Ebrietas is indigestibilis est:

He feels thirsty again. There are, then, men among the sons of men who wait in the shadow of the wings of God, who in his own bed fight and conquer, conquer and are crowned. On the other hand, men who belong to man, those who are not sons of man, since they only care about this health which, once it is finished, they think has no continuation, when it begins to fail them, even if they call themselves Christians, seek out sorcerers, turn to astrologers and hang illicit amulets from their necks. They desire health and tie their own necks; They bind the neck of the outer man and strangle the throat of the inner man. Who, on the other hand, says: "I don't do it" - at the suggestion of his friend or whispered by the servant next door, and sometimes even his nanny' -; to whom he says: «I don't do it, I am a Christian; God forbids me; They are demonic rites; Listen to the Apostle: I don't want you to become associates of demons," the one who made the suggestion replies: "Do it and you will be healed; So-and-so did it. And? Are they not Christians? Are they not faithful? Don't you go to church? Still, they did it and are healthy. So-and-so did it, and was instantly cured. Do you not know that he is a Christian and baptized? Look, he did it and he's healthy." But that sick man, who does not love the health that man has in common with the donkeys, says to him: "If he healed in this way, I want to be healed in this way, since he can heal me to whom it was said: Men are already healed."

You will heal the donkeys, Lord, according to the multiplication of your mercy, O God! Look at the athlete of God, look at the athlete of Christ! Oh sick and healthy man at the same time! Oh weak and strong man at the same time! Oh you who lie on the bed and reign in heaven! «But suppose he doesn't want to. Will it deprive me of that divine health? Continue like this: But the sons of men will wait under the protection of your wings. But you do not see this health, because the health of the righteous comes from the Lord. I know he has it in store for me. He who made me, he remade me. But you try to terrify me with death, for whom life itself died! If Christ gave his death to the wicked, will he not give life to the pious? Whoever speaks like this and rejects those remedies, the most approved, especially those so called, as if they were experienced; Whoever flees from them is a martyr in his own bed. Languish and conquer; He barely moves his limbs and fights battles. Therefore, he suffers no harm even if he dies of that disease. He neither perishes nor loses anything; then you rather find what you are looking for. He will go out to meet his Lord with his forehead marked with the cross of Christ, to which he did not insult with illicit amulets. Will he not then give him what he promised his protégé when he was fighting? Certainly, the Lord protected him so that he did not suffer any evil and helped him in combat so that he could defeat the devil. There are many, my brothers, who say: "How did the martyrs defeat the devil?" In the same way that the good faithful overcome it. Listen to what the Apostle says:

nemo illam digest et redit ad sitim. Sunt ergo homines de isto numero <filiorum> hominum sperantium sub tegmine alarum dei qui in lecto suo luctantur et uincunt, uincunt et coronantur. Theme: Loving the behavior of martyrs. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of the Martyrs. In Lent. 1. All the solemnities of the blessed martyrs warn us how much the present life must be despised and the future sought. This is the reason why Jesus Christ our Lord himself, the prince of martyrs, whose passion was the price paid for them, who was born mortal not because his nature demanded it, but out of the condescension of his mercy, wanted to die and also be resurrected. In fact, he would not have died if he had not wanted to; but he would not have been resurrected if he had not died. He wanted both things. With his death he recommended to us the contempt of the present life, and with his resurrection, the desire for the future life. "See both in my passion and in my resurrection: what you must tolerate in the present life and what you must desire for the future." In his uobis eligite, causam bonam et iustam, quoniam beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum (Mt 5:10). SERMO

Theme: Martyrdom is precious in the eyes of God. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of martyrs. 1. We know what we have sung and we remember it perfectly: The death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord. The death of the saints is precious for its price. It is nothing strange that the death of those who were bought at such a price is precious. The world cannot be put on the same scale with the blood of him by whom the world was made. To have blood to shed for us, the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. The price, in fact, paid by all of us is the blood of him who shed it for the forgiveness of sins. What were sinners worth or how much were they valued? Was that blood really the just price for sins? Behold, Christ died for the wicked. Listen to the Apostle: God, he said, show his love will liberate us ab omnibus, et will give nobis pacem, sicut liberauit three ports of the road. Ipsi pueri, uel potius iuuenes — consuetudine enim tres pueri dicuntur, nam scriptura illos... SERMO

1. Scimus quid cantauimus, et bene tenemus: Pretiosa in conspectu domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15). Pretio quippe eius <pretiosa> est mors sanctorum. Non itaque mirandum est mortem esse pretiosam eorum qui both sunt pretio empti. Non enim appenditur mundus contra eius sanguinem per quem factus est mundus. Vt autem haberet (105) sanguinem quem pro nobis funderet, verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,14). Sanguis ergo eius pretium est omnium nostrum, qui tamen sanguis in remissionem fusus est peccatorum. Quid enim ualebant peccatores, aut quanti ualebant? Itane uere erat ille sanguis pretium peccatorum? Etenim Christus pro impiis mortuus est. Apostolum audi; Commendat caritatem suam, inquit, deus in nobis, quia cum adbue!

Emptor ille noster pretio mundauit quod emerat. Peccator enim quomodo tanti emeretur, nisi suo pretio mundaretur? 2. Quod ergo antequam nos emeret eramus non respiciamus, ne in uia temaneamus. How then did he die for sinners, if he did not love sinners? Precisely because he did not love sinners that is why he died for sinners. Understand it and your difficulties will end. You ask me how He who died for them did not love sinners. Answer my question first, and you will give yourself the answer to what you asked me. Whoever loves a thing, does he want it to exist or not to exist? I think that, if you love your children, you want them to exist; Well, if you don't want them to exist, you don't love them. Whatever you love, you want it to exist and in no way do you love what you don't want to exist. What, therefore, did the Lord want when he died for us? That we were sinners or freed from sins? If he died for us precisely to erase our sins, did he love what he destroyed? Who destroys what he loves? If you are faithful, if you have believed in him, if you have lifted up your heart, to write what you are he had to erase what you were. 4. Look at him. Listen to him speak in the psalm through the prophet: Their infirmities multiplied and then they made haste. What does it mean: His weaknesses multiplied? The law came so that crime would abound. What does it also mean: Then they hurried? Where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more. And then what? Then they hurried, since, packed

of illnesses, they sought the doctor. And then? "I will not gather," he said, "their bloody conventicles. What does it mean: I will not gather their blood covens? I will not gather them through those sacrifices, through that blood, but through the blood through which the death of his saints is precious in the eyes of the Lord. Therefore, I will no longer gather their blood covens. That blood convicted them of their sin, but did not purify them. It was delivered, a single purifying blood was shed instead of many others that accused. A single blood was given; and then what? Not even my lips will remember their names. Before that one blood was shed, when their conventicles of blood were gathered together, their names did not die: he who was an adulterer remained an adulterer; the thief, thief; the one who hurt continued to do so; the sacrilegious remained sacrilegious. That one blood was shed: Not even my lips will remember their names. Do not be deceived, says the Apostle, for neither the fornicators, nor the idolaters, nor the adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor the sodomites, nor the thieves, nor the covetous, nor the drunkards, nor the rapacious, nor the revilers will possess the kingdom of God. Prorsus non amando peccatores, pro peccatoribus mortuus est. Intellege, et non laboras. You ask me quomodo non amauit peccatores qui mortuus est pro peccatoribus. Dec mihi prius quod ego te interrogate, et tibi ipse de eo quod interrogaueras (106) responders. Quod quisque amat, uult esse, an non uult esse? Puto quia, if you love your filios, uis illos esse; si autem illos non uis esse, non amas. Et quodcumque amas, uis ut sit, nec omnino amas quod cupis ut non sit. Quid ergo uoluit dominus, cum moreretur pro nobis? Vt peccatores essemus, an ut a peccatis liberaremur? Si propterea mortuus est pro nobis ut peccata nostra deleret, numquid amauit quod deleuit? Quis delet quod amat? Si fidelis es, si in eum credidisti, si sursum cor habes, ut scriberet quod es, deleuit quod fuesti. 4. Vide illum. Audi loquentem in psalmo per prophetiam: MultipUcatae sunt, inquit, infirmitates eorum, postea acceleraverunt (Ps 15*4). Quid est, multipUcatae sunt infirmitates eorum? Lex subintrauit, ut abundaret delictum (Rom 1:20). Et quid, post acceleraverunt? Vbi abundauit delictum, superabundauit grana (ib.). Quid deinde? Post

acceleraverunt, quia morbis impleti medicum quaesierunt. Quid deinde? Non congregabo conventicle eorum, inquit, de sanguinibus (Ps 15,4). Quid est, non congregabo conuenticula eorum de sanguinibus? Non per illa sacrifice pecorum congregabo eos, non de sanguinibus, sed de sanguine, propter quem sanguinem pretiosa in conspectu domini mors sanctorum eius. Iam ergo non congregabo conuenticula eorum de sanguinibus. lilis enim sanguinibus conuincebantur, non mundabantur. Datus est, fusus est unus sanguis mundans, pro multis sanguinibus conuincentibus. Datus est unus sanguis, et quid deinde? Nec memor ero nominum eorum per labia mea (Ps 15:4). Antequam funderetur ille unus sanguis, quando congregabantur conuenticula eorum de sanguinibus, nomina eorum non moriebantur: adulter, adulter erat; fur, fur erat; pester, pester erat; sacrilegus, sacrilegus erat. Fusus est unus sanguis: non (107) memor ero nominum illorum per labia mea. Nolite errare, ait [834] apostolus, ñeque fornicatores, ñeque idolis servientes, ñeque adulteri, ñeque molles, ñeque masculorum concubitors, ñeque fures, ñeque auari, ñeque ebriosi, ñeque rapaces, ñeque maledici, regnum dei possidebunt (1 Cor 6,9-10): haec erat nomina illorum. Et ut scias quia haec erant nomina illorum, audi quid sequitur: Et haec quidem fuestis (1 Cor 6:11). Et ubi est: nec memor ero nominum eorum per labia mea? Be abluti estis, be sanctificati estis (1 Cor 6:11). Ergo iam quod fuestis non estis.

5. There is no doubt that God loves sinners; There is also no doubt that, because of his blood, sinners are not what they were. How are they loved, if Christ the Lord loved the righteous and not the sinners? He loved what he intended to do, not what he found in them. The doctor, if he fulfills what he has been called to do, loves the healthy, not the sick. And I even dare to say, and it is true, that he approached the sick man precisely because he does not love the sick man. It seems that I have said something contradictory, but I ask: "Why did you approach the sick man?" To make him healthy. So he doesn't love the sick person. He loves what he intends to make of it, not what he wants to eliminate. Thus, the holy martyrs, bought at such a high price, redeemed by their creator, recovered their health. Servants twice: as created and as redeemed. From where their double servitude came to them, from there came their freedom: they are servants of the creator and brothers of the redeemer. To see that they are servants, read the gospel as a document that attests to it; see in it how they have been bought. Look at the contract: the bag containing its price was hung from the tree, torn and spilled. He poured out what it contained, and with it he bought. If you read it, you will find in it the document that attests to their status as servants. He made them brothers from servants, and what was a document of their condition as servants became a will for their children. Amen. 5. Certe amat deus peccatores: certe peccatores, per sanguinem ipsius, quod fuerunt non sunt. Quomodo amantur, cum dominus Christus iustos amauit, non peccatores? Quod faceré uoluit amauit, non quod inuenit. Medicus, si implet quod uocatur, healthy amat, non aegrotos. Et prorsus audeo dicere, et uerum est, ideo uenit ad aegrotum, quia non amat aegrotum. Contrarium uidetur quod dixi, sed interrogo: Quare uenit ad aegrotum? Vt faciat sanum. Ergo non amat aegrotum. Quod uult faceré amat, quod uult tollere non amat. Facti ergo sunt sani martyres sancti, so much empti, a creatore suo redempti. Bis serui, quia et facti et empti. Et unde bis serui, inde liberi: mancipia creatoris, fratres redemptoris. Vt uideas seruos, euangelium lege tamquam instrumentum: ibi uide ubi sunt empti. Attend ipsa commerce: sacculus pretii eorum pependit in ligno, percussus est, fusus est. Fudit, et emit: legis, et inuenis seruorum instrumentum. Fecit eos fratres de seruis, et quod erat seruorum instrumentum, factum est filiorum testamentum. Amen.
Topic: Christian combat. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of martyrs.

1. The holy martyrs, the witnesses of Christ, fought to the blood against sin thanks to the assistance of him through whom they conquered. Those who now fight against sin also recognize that the fight is necessary and covet the crown. In fact, when the enemies of the name of Christ persecuted the martyrs, they fought internally and won externally. But there was no external victory if the internal victory did not precede. I am going to tell you how the enemy approached the martyr. They arrested him, chained him and took him before the judge. The judge told him: "Deny Christ if you want to live." But he did not deny it, precisely because he wanted to live. How, then, did he fight within himself before? Because the sweetness of this life told him: "Deny it." He did not listen to him and confess Christ. By conquering the sweetness of this life internally, he defeated the persecutor externally. 2. What does what I just said mean? Those who fight against sin are also in struggle now; and who they are

1. Martyres sancti, testes Christi, usque ad sanguinem contra peccatum pugnauerunt, quia ipse in illis Fuit, per quem uicerunt. Sed non uincebant foris, nisi prius uincerent intus. Ecce dico uobis quomodo ueniebat inimicus ad martirem. Et adprehendebat eum, et alligabat, et ad iudicem perducebat. Iudex saysbat illi: "Nega Christum si uis uiuere." Sed Ule non negabat, quia uolebat uiuere. Quomodo ergo prius intus pugnabat? Quia dulcedo uitae huius dicebat: "Deny." Ule non audiebat, et confitebatur Christum. Vincens intus uitae dulcedinem, uincebat foris persequutorem. 2. Quid est ergo quod dixi? Et nunc pugnant qui <contra peccatum> pugnant, et qui agnoscunt pugnam desiderant coronam. Hoc enim iam

Aware of that fight, they want the crown. I have said this shortly before, and I must explain to you what it is about. You heard it when the Apostle was read. I repeat his same words: Well, if you live according to the flesh, he said, you will die; If, on the other hand, you mortify the works of the body with the spirit, you will live. This is what Christian combat consists of: mortifying the works of the body with the spirit. It is normal in the flesh to desire another's woman: delighting in it and desiring her is already a carnal pleasure. He has not yet committed adultery, but lust knocks at his doors. But conscience will win if patience protects it. Who is there that does not suffer such a war? Everyone suffers it, but not everyone wins. But in the same way that not everyone defeats it, not everyone is defeated either. There are people who don't even fight. As soon as the evil desire appears in their heart, they give their consent. And if you don't put it into effect, it's because you can't find a place. Whoever does not carry it out because he did not find a place, at the same time that he did not find a place on earth, lost it in heaven. 3. Lust arose, and you felt excited. But you can't get to someone else's wife. You are already walking defeated, because your consent meant being held captive. On the other hand, those who do not consent are not overcome by concupiscence. She uses pleasure for her combat; you fight by contradicting it. She will tell you: "Let's do it to live in pleasure." You answer him: "Let's not do it, to live without end." While your fight with her lasts, she begins not to get up. Or if ever doubt arises <dixí>, et debeno uobis exposere quid sit. Audistis quando apostolus legebatur. Ipsa uerba commemoro. Si enim secundutn carnem uixeritis, inquit, moriemini. Si autem spiritu actiones carnis mortificaueritis, uiuetis (Rom 8:13). Haec est pugna christiana: mortificare spiritu actiones carnis. Actio carnis est concupiscere uxorem alienam. Ipsum delectan et concupiscere, iam delectatio carnis est. Nondum facit adulterium, sed iam titillat illum concupiscentia. Be uincet conscientia, si teneatur [840] patientia. Quis est quí non patiatur tale bellum? Omnes patiuntur, (198) sed non omnes uincunt. Quomodo autem non omnes uíncunt, sic nec omnes uíncuntur. Sunt autem qui nec pugnant. Quando enim surrexerit in corde ipsius concupiscentia, ipsa hora consentit illi. Sed ideo non facit, quia non inuenit locum. Qui propterea non facit quia non inuenit, interim et in terra locum non habuit, et perdidit in cáelo locum. 3.

The Christian combat

a little, he immediately blushes and perishes. What I have said about the love of another's wife can be said about the love of drunkenness, money, the love of pride and all other things where bad loves and bad customs occur. 4. He who contradicts bad loves becomes a Christian with good customs. He fights every day in his conscience to ask, once he has won, the crown from those who see him fight. But would he win if he fought himself? Leave him alone there, and he falls defeated. Therefore, when you do not give your consent to the desires of the flesh by boasting of your strength, you are alone, and since you boast of your strength, you act alone. When, on the other hand, you attribute nothing to your strength and give yourself completely to God, it is God who works for you to will and to act according to your good will. That is why he said: If you mortify the works of the body with the spirit, you will live. Nothing is attributed here to human fragility, nothing is put into account of its efforts and strength, because, if it is attributed to itself, it opens the doors to pride, and pride to ruin. Whoever, on the other hand, assigns all his progress to God, makes room for the Holy Spirit. That is why the Apostle says: Those who allow themselves to be guided by the Spirit of God are children of God. Therefore, if we are children of God, the Spirit of God guides us and the Spirit of God acts in us. Whatever we do wrong is ours. Whatever good we do is the work of God, who works in us to will and to act according to our good will. will not arise. Aut si aliquando ad modicum surrexerit, I quote erubescit et perit. Quod dixi de amore uxoris alicnae, hoc dico de amore ebrietatis, de amore pecuniae, hoc dico de amore superbiae et ceteris omnibus ubi sunt amores mali et mores mali. 4. Qui autem contradicit ipsis malis amoribus, fit christianus bonis moribus. Et fight every day in conscientia, ut ab illo qui illud uidet petat coronam, dum uicerit. Sed numquid uicerit, se ipse pugnaret? Dimitte illum illuc solum, et uincitur. Quando ergo <non> consentís (199) concupiscentiís carnis de te praesumens, solus es, et quia de te praesumis, tu solus facis. Quando autem nihil tuis uiribus reputans, totum te deo tradis, deus est qui pro te operatus et uelle et perficere pro tua bona uoluntate (Phil 2,13). Et ideo said: Si spiritu jacta carnis mortificaueritis, uiuetis.

Theme: The Christian life is a ceaseless struggle. Location: Unknown. Date: Feast of a martyred bishop.

1. This solemnity in honor of God, my brothers, takes its foundation from the servant of God. Indeed, when the servant of God is honored as is due, he is honored in the name of his Lord. Thus, then, the blessed..., servant of God, today laid down the burden of his flesh and sent to the earth his flesh that is to be resurrected. The earth was returned to the earth, and the spirit, to the spirit of God. The bowel movement of each man corresponds to his life in the body. Death is a thing in a certain sense neutral; By itself it is neither good nor bad; but, when the last day of this life arrives, it distinguishes and separates two things that had been together: the soul, invisible, from the flesh, visible; the soul, subject of sensations, of the flesh, in which the soul feels, since the flesh without the soul feels nothing. The separation of these two things that are united, although very different from each other, is what causes death. Consequently, death, which separates and separates these two things, by itself does not seem to be either good or bad, but for the good it is good and for the bad it is bad.

Therefore, our teacher's response: You are in error, not knowing the Scriptures and the power of God. At the resurrection, no one will take a husband or wife, for everyone will be like angels in heaven. Why then do you expect to know which of them will have a wife, if no one there will have a wife? Women are necessary in the human journey so that those who are to live are born, succeeding those who are to die. There, however, what need will there be for a spouse, where there will be no need for offspring? What need will there be for children to be born where parents do not die, where everyone has only one father, whom they cannot cast out? Since we have been promised at the resurrection that we will be equal to the angels in heaven, the righteous will live in such eternal remembrance and will not be afraid to hear evil. What eternal memory he will live in is clear, but what bad thing he will not be afraid to hear is not. It is convenient, therefore, that I remind you of what you know by not hearing what you do not know. Now I am going to mention it, and you will all recognize what evil the righteous will not be afraid to hear. 3. The righteous will live in eternal memory.
